papers.title: Thermocatalytic transcarbonation with diethyl carbonate for valorization of glycerol : recycling siliceous bauxite residue waste components and exploring the potential of sodalite hydroxide reservoir
papers.journal: Repository of the Academy's Library (Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences)
papers.abstract: Bauxite residues contain katoites and desilication products (sodalite and cancrinite), which are excellent candidates for Earth-abundant heterogeneous base catalysts from industrial waste sources. For the first time, they were tested in synthetizing the renewable and promising fuel or fuel additive glycerol carbonate for the purpose of recycling glycerol by-products from biodiesel production. Incorporation of silicate was found to enhance the previously established excellent catalytic activity of tricalcium aluminate (Si-free katoite). Performance of sodalites containing four different cage anion-designed (OH, CO3, SO4, Cl) and carbonated cancrinite was determined to a much greater extent by their Brönsted OH content than by the basicity of the caged anions. Direct catalytic use of bauxite residue resulted in a glycerol carbonate yield of over 80%, but it was quickly deactivated due to the limited reusability of many of its most active components (i.e., Si-free and Si-containing katoites, chloride sodalites). However, hydroxysodalites showed excellent reusability, with a glycerol carbonate yield of around 80% even after 5 reuses. The activity of katoites and sodalities overtook that of many complex systems containing relatively rare metals, such as Ni, Cu, Zr, and Ce. Their excellent activity has made it possible to use diethyl carbonate solvent/reagent, which is more favourable in terms of sustainability, instead of the more widely applied dimethyl carbonate, even with as short reaction times as 30–60 min.

papers.title: Hypoxia-responsive supramolecular systems based on macrocycles and self-assembly structures.
papers.abstract: Hypoxia is closely associated with tumor progression, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and diagnostic challenges. The timely detection of hypoxia in live cancer cells is critical for early cancer diagnosis and for monitoring the effectiveness of anticancer therapies. Recently, there has been growing interest in non-covalent supramolecular design strategies for the development of hypoxia-sensitive sensors and prodrugs. Unlike the widely employed covalent approach, supramolecular chemistry eliminates the need for complex and time-consuming synthetic processes. Instead, the individual components of the sensor autonomously self-assemble into the desired structure. This review provides an overview of hypoxia-targeted and hypoxia-activated supramolecular probes, along with their mechanisms of action in tumor diagnosis and therapy. The supramolecular systems considered are classified according to the use of certain classes of macrocycles. The role of macrocyclic derivatives in the various proposed approaches and the response patterns of hypoxic targets will also be analyzed. Various representatives of the macrocyclic platforms, namely cyclodextrins, cucurbiturils, pillararenes, (thia)calixarenes, due to their properties such as molecular recognition, are used as molecular containers-carriers for pharmaceuticals and bio-organic fluorescent dyes. As a result of complex formation, the photostability and the signal-to-noise ratio of dyes increase. In addition, the solubility of hydrophobic guests in water improves, cytotoxicity is reduced, and targeted delivery promotes the accumulation of drugs/dyes in tumor cells.

papers.title: Nitric oxide in the occurrence and development of ischemic cerebrovascular disease.
papers.abstract: Since nitric oxide is a chemically highly reactive free radical that can act as both an oxidizing agent and a reducing agent, it is assumed that it has diverse effects on biological tissues. Nitric oxide is fundamentally important for the regulation of immune, reproductive and neuromuscular system functions and is the main signaling molecule and effector that can dilate blood vessels and modulate energy metabolism. This review examines the key role of nitric oxide in the mechanisms underlying the response to hypoxia, as well as in the effects of factors induced by hypoxia. The available conflicting information allowed us to conclude that at present, there is no consensus about the role of endogenous nitric oxide in the processes occurring after ischemic cerebrovascular disease.

papers.title: Hyperbaric oxygen for the treatment of traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of hyperbaric oxygen therapy for traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury remains a subject of debate. To comprehensively evaluate the impact of hyperbaric oxygen on motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis. We performed a comprehensive search across PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and major Chinese databases for randomized controlled trials published through June 2025. A total of 15 randomized controlled trials were included. The pooled results indicated that hyperbaric oxygen therapy significantly improved the American Spinal Injury Association motor score (mean difference = 10.30, 95% confidence interval: 7.70-12.90), the total American Spinal Injury Association sensory score (mean difference = 29.29, 95% confidence interval: 18.82-39.75), the American Spinal Injury Association light touch score (mean difference = 9.84, 95% confidence interval: 6.15-13.53), and the American Spinal Injury Association pinprick score (mean difference = 8.75, 95% confidence interval: 4.40-13.11). Furthermore, hyperbaric oxygen therapy was associated with significant enhancements in the Barthel Index (mean difference = 16.60, 95% confidence interval: 10.51-22.68) and the Functional Independence Measure (mean difference = 17.41, 95% confidence interval: 10.83-23.98). In conclusion, adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy appears to improve motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury compared to conventional treatments alone. However, due to methodological limitations and potential publication bias in the included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution, and further high-quality, multi-center randomized controlled trials are warranted.

papers.title: High levels of nitric oxide and peroxynitrite with protein nitration: a new therapeutic target for gliomas.
papers.abstract: The gap junction signaling pathway is a core hub mediating intercellular communication, which plays a vital role in maintaining tissue homeostasis, and its dysfunction is closely related to glioma. Nitroproteomics studies have shown that protein tyrosine nitration plays an important role in the progression of glioma, and gap junction is one of the significantly enriched nitroprotein signaling pathways in glioma; proteoformics reveals that nitration can produce various proteoforms of related proteins, which have different functional states in different subtypes of glioma, suggesting that nitration may alter the functional states of related proteins in gap junction pathways. When levels of nitric oxide and peroxynitrite (ONOO-) rise, they induce the tyrosine nitration of key proteins in the gap junction pathway; this nitration not only interferes with the function of the gap junction pathway, but also affects other gap junction-linked signaling networks. Forming an attack network on the gap junction pathway through multi-pathway cross-regulation has great potential for therapeutic strategies targeting the gap junction pathway. We recommend in-depth studies of the gap junction signaling pathway and potential drugs targeting gap junction signals, including drugs that target gap junction communication activators, nitration inhibitors, and drugs that directly target specific nitroproteins, combined with conventional chemotherapy or immune checkpoint inhibitors, as well as the construction of personalized medical frameworks as important future research directions.

papers.title: Antitrust Regulation of Algorithmic "Platform-Driven Involution'': From Governing the Corporate Person to Governing the Platform Ecosystem
papers.abstract: Digital platforms increasingly govern competition through algorithmically administered rules that allocate visibility, subsidies, commissions, participation opportunities, and sanctions. This article reconstructs ``platform-driven involution'' as a testable, portfolio-based theory-of-harm framework rather than a freestanding antitrust offense. Its application remains anchored in market definition, dominance, identified conduct under Article 22 of China's Anti-Monopoly Law, causal proof, competitive effects, and objective justification. The article clarifies that ecosystem analysis supplements rather than replaces relevant-market analysis and develops an evidence architecture for separating platform-induced effects from macroeconomic, demand, cost, and merchant-specific confounders. It then distinguishes preventive measures already supported by Chinese hard law or voluntary compliance guidance from compulsory competition-specific filing and pre-deployment assessment that would require clearer future authorization. The 2026 Trip.com decision is used to show how traffic allocation, exclusivity, lowest-price requirements, technical monitoring, and sanctions can form an integrated abuse architecture while liability remains tied to established statutory categories. Comparative analysis of EU platform regulation and Google Shopping supports calibrated procedural prevention, meaningful explanation, and causal discipline without protecting inefficient competitors or condemning aggressive competition.

The 2026 Trip.com decision is used to show how traffic allocation, exclusivity, lowest-price requirements, technical monitoring, and sanctions can form an integrated abuse architecture while liability remains tied to established statutory categories.

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.abstract: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-performance validation.

The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-performance validation.

papers.title: Current status of room temperature magnetic compensation in impurity-doped Mn4N epitaxial thin films
papers.abstract: Mn4N, a ferrimagnet that does not contain rare-earth elements, possesses attractive properties for spintronics applications. In particular, Mn4N epitaxial films exhibit a small spontaneous magnetization of about 100 kA m(-1), a large spin polarization (p = 0.8), and large perpendicular magnetic anisotropy with a magnetic anisotropy constant of approximately 10(5) J m(-3). More importantly, achieving magnetic compensation at room temperature is possible through impurity doping. This property is particularly significant for spin-torque-based spintronics applications. In the vicinity of the magnetization and/or angular momentum compensation points, magnetization dynamics can be substantially accelerated, enabling high-speed switching and domain wall motion. This article surveys the magnetic properties of impurity-doped Mn4N epitaxial films grown on SrTiO3(001) substrates, highlighting recent results obtained with Cu-, Ag-, Au-, and Pd-doped Mn4N films in comparison with Ni- and Cr-doped Mn4N films. Furthermore, with a view to device applications of Mn4N, we present the formation of ultrathin (similar to 4 nm) Pt epitaxial films with a <100> orientation on MgO (001), which is essential for injecting spins into Mn4N-based overlayers by utilizing the spin Hall effect of heavy metals. papers.title: Reproducible chiroptical activity from aggregated chiral thienopyrroledione-fluorene π-conjugated polymers
papers.abstract: Chiral pi-conjugated polymers have attracted considerable interest because their chiral-aggregated structures can generate pronounced chiroptical responses. Here, we report the design, synthesis, and chiroptical characterization of fluorene - thienopyrroledione polymers bearing a single chiral center in each repeating unit, (R)- and (S)-PFTPD, prepared via direct arylation polycondensation to minimize structural defects. Although only weak chiroptical activity was observed in the solution, the addition of 1-butanol to CHCl3 solutions of the polymers induced the formation of stable aggregates that exhibited strong circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL). Systematic examination of the sample preparation parameters revealed that the mixing process critically influences the chiroptical properties. Dropwise addition of 1-butanol under controlled stirring provided the most reliable results, yielding highly reproducible CD spectra. Under these optimized conditions, the aggregates exhibited an average dissymmetry factor (|g abs|) of 1.5 & times; 10-2 and a CPL dissymmetry factor (|g lum|) of 1.9 & times; 10-2. These values rank among the highest reported for pi-conjugated polymer aggregates bearing only a single chiral source per repetition unit. This study demonstrates that precise control over the solvent-mixing process is essential for the reproducible emergence of chiroptical properties and highlights the chiral TPD unit as a promising platform for chiroptical polymer materials.

papers.title: Somatosensory phenotyping in women with persistent genital arousal disorder: a case-control study.
papers.abstract: Introduction: Persistent genital arousal disorder (PGAD) is a rare and distressing condition characterized by persistent, unwanted genital arousal in the absence of sexual desire or stimulation. Persistent genital arousal disorder is increasingly recognized as a disorder of abnormal genital sensory processing, but objective neurophysiological data remain limited. Methods: We conducted an exploratory case-control study to characterize somatosensory function in women with PGAD. Thirty women with PGAD and 30 age-matched healthy controls were recruited at Leiden University Medical Center. Participants underwent quantitative sensory testing (QST) at hand and external genital sites, conditioned pain modulation, and corneal confocal microscopy. Results: Hand QST values were within normal range in both groups. In the genital region, PGAD participants showed altered thermal pain processing, with cold and heat hyperalgesia compared with controls. Mechanical pain thresholds did not differ between groups; however, PGAD participants reported higher pain intensity ratings to mechanical stimuli and showed significantly greater temporal summation of pain in genital regions. Genital dynamic mechanical allodynia occurred more frequently in PGAD participants but did not differ significantly at the group level. Conditioned pain modulation magnitude did not differ between groups and showed substantial interindividual variability. Corneal confocal microscopy abnormalities were observed in a proportion of participants in both groups without significant between-group differences. Discussion: These findings show that QST is feasible in women with PGAD and indicate that PGAD is associated with altered somatosensory processing demonstrating genital thermal hypersensitivity and central pain sensitization in a subset of patients.

papers.title: Airdrop Sybil Attack detection framework supported by machine learning
papers.journal: International Journal of Electronics and Telecommunication Systems
papers.abstract: A skilled hunter may earn thousands of dollars in tokens from a single airdrop, making airdrop Sybil assaults a profitable endeavor. In this situation, Sybil assaults are not always wanted by projects and are often seen as improper behavior by honest individuals, which may negatively impact a project's image. It is thus to be anticipated that detection methods for Sybil assaults would be continuously enhanced. This study presents a multistep structure. Its concept is to sort blockchain addresses and give each one a score that indicates whether it belongs to the Sybil or regular class. Topologies were classified using a graph isomorphism network, whose parameters were adjusted using a dataset that the authors labeled. In subsequent phases, the account clustering operation was performed using a DBSCAN. Each stage in the framework may be given arbitrary weights by users, which will decide how essential a step is to them and provide a different score for a particular address. A grid search strategy and a threshold after which the address is deemed Sybil were used to find the optimal weights. This article examined a collection of EOAs from the ZK sync rollup. Ultimately, 76% of the examined accounts were classified as Sybils. Compared to the official ZK sync eligibility list, we found 342 addresses that received airdrop tokens but were marked as Sybil by our solution.

papers.title: DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY OF ULTRA-LOW-DOSE CT VS. STANDARD-DOSE CT FOR PULMONARY NODULE DETECTION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
authors: KHALED BONNA , RASHA GALAL ELSAFTY , NORA EID ALANAZI , RANIN JABER M ALMAJRASHI AHLAM ALI Y ASIRI , WALEED MUFAREH ALSHAHRANI , SOMAYYAH SOHAIL MITHA , SHOUG NASSER ALKHAMMASH , BANDAR SAAD ALSHREEF
papers.journal: TPM Testing, psychometrics, methodology in applied psychology
papers.abstract: Background: Standard dose computed tomography (CT) is a primary modality for detecting pulmonary nodules (PNs), but the health risk from cumulative radiation exposure has prompted the emergence of ultra-low-dose CT (ULDCT) as an alternative to reduce this dose, because its diagnostic accuracy remains variable, this systematic review and meta-analysis aims to synthesize the existing evidence to determine the diagnostic accuracy and effective radiation dose of ULDCT for pulmonary nodule detection. Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Ovid MEDLINE for original research published between 2015 and 2025 that evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of ULDCT for PN detection, for which a meta-analysis using random-effects models was performed to calculate the pooled sensitivity for nodule detection and the pooled mean effective radiation dose, with a subgroup analysis conducted to assess the impact of different reconstruction algorithms. Results: Forty-two studies comprising 15,792 patients were included, from which a meta-analysis of 11 studies demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 91.9% (95% CI: 84.6%–97.1%) for PN detection with heterogeneity (I²=93.0%), and a pooled mean effective dose from 12 studies of 0.22 mSv (95% CI: 0.11–0.33 mSv), a level comparable to standard chest radiography, while subgroup analysis revealed a trend towards higher sensitivity with advanced reconstruction algorithms (96.7%) compared to standard iterative reconstruction (87.9%) that was not statistically significant (p=0.091), and a narrative synthesis confirmed ULDCT's accuracy for solid nodules but identified reduced sensitivity for subsolid, ground-glass, and small (<6 mm) nodules, with performance limited in patients with a high body mass index (BMI). Conclusion: ULDCT combined with advanced reconstruction techniques offers high diagnostic accuracy for the detection of solid pulmonary nodules and reduces radiation exposure to levels approaching that of a chest X-ray, but its utility is limited for detecting subsolid and small nodules and in obese patients, making protocol standardization and patient-specific considerations essential to optimize its clinical implementation.

papers.title: Management rather than climate and biodiversity shapes long-term delta15N dynamics in grassland soils
papers.abstract: The bulk soil δ 15 N signature in grassland soils serves as a fingerprint of nitrogen inputs, turnover and losses, reflecting the influence of land management, climate, plant biodiversity and abiotic soil properties.Although natural abundance δ 15 N has been proposed as an indicator for these factors, previous studies yielded mixed results regarding the importance of its drivers.In this study, we quantified changes in soil δ 15 N across 72 German grassland sites after 12 years (2011 vs. 2023) and analysed relationships with detailed records of land use intensity, plant biodiversity, climate, and soil properties.Land use intensity was quantified on a continuous scale based on mowing, grazing and fertilisation.In the top 10 cm of soil, δ 15 N changes ranged from -0.86 to + 2.49‰, equating to an average increase of + 0.35‰ per decade.Over two-thirds of our study sites showed a long-term increase in δ 15 N associated with high land use intensity.Our findings indicate that fertiliser application and grazing are the dominant drivers of δ 15 N increases, while a biodiversity-mediated decrease via reduced N losses was not observed.The slow decadal-scale shifts suggest that single soil δ 15 N measurements without known initial values are only informative for long-term management processes and not for assessing recent management impacts.

papers.title: Efficient deoxygenation of palm oil to green diesel using a metal oxide catalysts supporting on ZrO2-enhanced graphene oxide
papers.journal: Universiti Putra Malaysia Institutional Repository (Universiti Putra Malaysia)
papers.abstract: NiO, Fe2O3, and bimetallic oxide NiFe2O4 catalysts supported on graphene oxide and promoted with ZrO2 were synthesized via wet-impregnation approach. A systematic characterization of the catalysts physicochemical properties was evaluated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR), Temperature-programmed desorption CO2 (TPD-CO2), Brunaur-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area, Field emission Scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), and Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis. The catalysts were evaluated as heterogeneous catalysts in the deoxygenation (DO) of palm oil for green diesel production under varying operating conditions. Among the catalysts tested, Fe2O3/ZrO2-GO (calcined at 400 °C for 4 h, 5 wt% loading) demonstrated superior catalytic activity, achieving a maximum hydrocarbon yield (HC%) of 98.0%, bio-jet fuel (BJF) selectivity of 40%, and kerosene yield of 86%. The exceptional performance is attributed to the catalyst’s large BET surface area (18.64 m2/g), substantial pore volume (0.027 cm3 /g), and moderate surface basicity (3234.65 μmol/g), which collectively facilitate efficient deoxygenation via decarboxylation (DCO2) and decarbonylation (DCO) pathways while suppressing undesired cracking. Furthermore, the catalyst exhibited remarkable stability and reusability over four consecutive reaction cycles, retaining 92% hydrocarbon yield and 80.9% kerosene yield, with BJF selectivity increasing to 84%. The gradual decline in performance is attributed to carbon deposition (coke formation), pore blockage, and sintering-induced degradation of the mesoporous network, as confirmed by post-reaction XRD and BET analysis.

papers.title: Al1−xHfxN Thin Films with Enhanced Piezoelectric Responses for GHz Surface Acoustic Wave Devices
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Ternary compounds obtained by alloying wurtzite AlN with transition metals have emerged as promising materials with significantly enhanced piezoelectric characteristics relative to binary AlN. The increased electromechanical coupling in these compounds boosts the performance of high‐frequency acoustic devices. To date, progress has largely focused on aluminum scandium nitride (), which, while widely deployed, relies on scandium, a costly and critical element that is challenging to refine. Here, we investigate aluminum hafnium nitride () as a more economical and accessible alternative to . Using reactive co‐sputtering on both Si and ‐ substrates, we demonstrate wurtzite thin films () with strong ‐axis texture and nearly isotropic lattice expansion upon Hf incorporation. X‐ray absorption spectroscopy indicates cross‐gap hybridization between N 2 and Hf 5 states, which can enhance the Born effective charge and, thereby, the piezoelectric response. The incorporation of Hf leads to a multifold enhancement in the piezoelectric coefficient, , relative to AlN, despite increasing structural disorder in these thin films. Building on this increased electromechanical coupling, we present functional GHz surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators that exhibit enhanced performance, as well as efficient excitation of bulk acoustic waves with low propagation losses. These results establish as a promising platform for next‐generation high‐frequency electromechanical devices, with prospects for further piezoelectric enhancements through improved epitaxy.

papers.title: Dataset merging strategy for efficient construction of a machine-learning force field: A case of CeO2 surfaces with an oxygen vacancy
papers.abstract: The accuracy and transferability of machine-learning force fields (MLFFs) critically depend on the quality of the training database. Here, we propose a dataset merging strategy for efficiently constructing a transferable MLFF for pristine and oxygen-defective CeO2 surfaces. The proposed strategy is based on three key elements: (1) initiating on-the-fly training from small, less stable slab models to accelerate early stage convergence by sampling diverse high-energy configurations; (2) sampling diverse local structures by gradually increasing the temperature during molecular dynamics simulations while avoiding excessively rapid atomic motions and unphysically short contacts; and (3) merging independently generated datasets from slab models with different thicknesses and defect conditions to improve transferability. The resulting MLFF is validated on larger slab models containing 144 atoms and applied to structural optimization of pristine and oxygen-defective surfaces as well as lattice oxygen diffusion pathways on defective surfaces. The predicted pathways and energy barriers are in good agreement with density functional theory results, particularly for pathways involving relatively large structural and energetic changes. Furthermore, the merged MLFF was applied to ideal CeO2(111) slabs containing up to 5183 atoms, yielding only weak size dependence of the predicted vacancy-migration barrier. These results highlight that systematic dataset merging across model sizes and configurations provides a practical route to constructing transferable MLFFs for complex oxide surfaces.

papers.title: Promise and challenges of heart chamber segmentation from noncontrast CT scans using contrastive unpaired image translation: a feasibility study
papers.abstract: PurposeTo evaluate the feasibility and challenges of heart chamber segmentation from noncontrast CT scans using contrastive unpaired image translation and deep learning-based segmentation.ApproachWe developed ChameleonNet, a framework utilizing the Contrastive Unpaired Translation (CUT) network with decoupled contrastive learning (DCL) loss to synthesize noncontrast CT from contrast CT scans. Using annotations of four heart chambers (left atrium (LA), left ventricle (LV), right atrium (RA), and right ventricle (RV)) from contrast scans, we trained a Hausdorff distance loss-enhanced nnU-Net on synthesized noncontrast images. The translation model was trained with 35,538 contrast-enhanced and 37,197 noncontrast CT slices. The segmentation model was trained with 292 synthesized noncontrast scans. Performance was evaluated using Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and 95th Hausdorff distance (HD95) on 36 synthesized noncontrast scans, and volume agreement on 36 real noncontrast CT scans was assessed using Pearson correlation, mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), and mean percentage error (MPE).ResultsThe segmentation model achieved DSC of 0.94 (±0.01), 0.91 (±0.04), 0.92 (±0.03), 0.93 (±0.02), and HD95 of 3.63 (±1.49), 5.74 (±4.08), 5.18 (±1.77), and 5.51 (±3.21) mm on synthesized noncontrast images for LA, LV, RA, and RV, respectively. On real noncontrast CT scans, Pearson correlations were 0.93, 0.82, 0.87, and 0.89 (all p<0.001), with MAPE ranging from 9.22% to 20.79%, and MPE ranging from −12.52% to 4.67%.ConclusionsChameleonNet demonstrated feasibility for heart chamber segmentation from noncontrast CT without manual noncontrast annotations. However, volume errors, particularly for LV and RV, indicate that further refinement and validation are needed before clinical use.

papers.title: Supramolecular Binary Systems of Flavonoids: Design, Structure, and Physicochemical Properties
papers.abstract: Abstract In this study, an environmentally friendly mechanochemical approach was used to prepare and characterize a series of new cocrystals and salt cocrystals with a 1:2 stoichiometry. The flavonoids apigenin (APG), luteolin (LUT), fisetin (FIS), kaempferol (KAE), and quercetin (QUE) were mixed with pyridarone [4-(1-benzofuran-2-yl)pyridine (BZFP)] as the coformer. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), combined with Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) and Fourier transform Raman (FT-Raman) spectroscopy, confirmed the formation of well-defined supramolecular architectures stabilized predominantly by intermolecular O−H···N bonds. These interactions involve the terminal hydroxyl groups of the flavonoids (7OH and 3′OH/4′OH) acting as hydrogen bond donors and the pyridyl nitrogen atoms of BZFP serving as acceptors. The nature and dynamics of the hydrogen bonding network were further investigated using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). Analysis of the N 1s spectra revealed proton transfer in the LUT/BZFP, KAE/BZFP, and QUE/BZFP binary systems, indicating the presence of a mixed neutral−salt character. The remaining cocrystals were neutral. Thermal analysis showed that the obtained cocrystals have greater thermal stability than the pure components. Dissolution kinetics, solubility, and octanol−water partition coefficient studies (using chromatographic methods)compared to the parent flavonoidsrevealed a significant increase in dissolution rates, saturation concentrations, and solubility of the neutral and salt cocrystals under simulated gastric conditions (pH 1.9). Dissolution rates, saturation concentrations, and solubility values change with acidity in a complex manner. These variations can be explained by two opposing effects: on one hand, increased acidity protonates BZFP, making both pure BZFP and the cocrystals highly soluble, while the flavonoids become neutral and only sparingly soluble. Conversely, when acidity decreases, BZFP becomes neutral, reducing its solubility but increasing that of the flavonoids due to ionization. Overall, these results demonstrate that mechanochemical synthesis is a practical, effective, and sustainable strategy for improving the physicochemical properties of potent bioactive natural compounds, which can possibly be used in pharmaceutical formulations.

papers.title: Learning control policies from heterogeneous multi-horizon time series in battery energy management systems
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Representation-to-Decision (R2D), an end-to-end imitation learning framework that maps heterogeneous multi-horizon time-series inputs directly to battery control decisions through modular Temporal Feature Extractors (TFEs) and a shared latent representation, without an explicit load and PV forecasting step. While accurate forecasting improves prediction quality, optimal control performance remains unguaranteed in prediction-then-optimization pipelines; standard Reinforcement Learning (RL) lacks the long-horizon temporal awareness due to short-window observations, even when forecast signals are available as additional inputs. R2D offers a different perspective: rather than forecasting first and deciding second, it learns to decide directly from raw temporal inputs, with control optimality anchored by an aging-aware Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) expert through Behavior Cloning (BC). Benchmarked against six controllers on a high-fidelity electro-thermal battery simulation across five industrial sites, R2D achieves 62--77\% of the global clairvoyant optimum, outperforms the tested Model Predictive Control (MPC) and RL benchmarks, and yields battery degradation nearly identical to its MILP teacher across all five sites. Comprehensive ablation studies over temporal backbone, model size, expert formulation, aging-cost weighting, and horizon configuration confirm that an LSTM encoder with a 15-minute single-step control horizon provides the most robust and deployment-ready configuration, and cross-site and single-factor out-of-distribution tests show that generalization to unseen profiles is profile-dependent, with policies trained on high-activity sites transferring most reliably.

papers.title: Multi-Electron Transfer in Zinc-Based Batteries: Unraveling Redox Mechanisms Toward Next-Generation Self-Powered Technologies
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of autonomous IoT networks and wearable electronics has intensified the demand for photo-rechargeable zinc-based batteries (PRZBBs). While realizing high overall energy conversion efficiency intrinsically relies on cathode materials capable of multi-electron transfer reactions, current literature largely treats the fundamental electrochemistry of aqueous zinc batteries and the macroscopic engineering of solar-integrated devices as isolated domains. This review bridges this critical gap, offering a unique positioning by establishing a unified analytical framework that directly links fundamental multi-electron redox mechanisms to the dynamic architectural requirements of PRZBBs. Moving beyond a conventional cataloging of material classes, we critically evaluate diverse cathode platforms, including transition metal oxides, Prussian blue analogues, organics, halogens, and sulfur. Our incremental contribution lies in decoupling how specific multi-step reaction kinetics, distinct voltage plateaus, and dominant charge carriers dictate solar cell coupling strategies, particularly concerning maximum power point matching and intermittent charging adaptability. Furthermore, we critically and systematically assess the practical bottlenecks of these chemistries, such as shuttle effects, kinetic limitations, and voltage hysteresis, that hinder scalable integration. Finally, we distill these insights into a prioritized, roadmap-oriented perspective, outlining the short- to long-term engineering and scientific milestones necessary to translate fundamental multi-electron zinc chemistry into next-generation, commercially viable self-powered technologies.

papers.title: High-precision characterization of scattering losses in YAG and Yb:YAG ceramics with an integrating sphere and multipass-cell
papers.abstract: Abstract Transparent ceramic laser materials have been extensively studied for high-power laser applications, where scattering loss is a significant factor affecting laser output power. This study presents a method based on an integrating sphere combined with a multipass cell for measuring the scattering and absorption coefficients of laser materials, providing improved measurement precision. Pure YAG and Yb:YAG ceramic samples were investigated and systematically compared with pure YAG and Yb:YAG single crystals with the same Yb 3+ doping concentration. Specifically, the scattering coefficients at 1064 nm were measured to be 0.0046 cm −1 for YAG ceramic and 0.0093 cm −1 for Yb:YAG ceramic, while the corresponding absorption coefficients were 0.0267 cm −1 and 0.0221 cm −1 , respectively, which are close to those of the single crystals. Furthermore, overall optical quality and wavefront distortion were analyzed using a Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor. The proposed method increases the effective optical interaction length, enhances the detectable loss signal, and improves measurement reliability, providing a practical approach for characterizing scattering and absorption losses in low-loss laser materials.

papers.title: Cavity-Filling Calcite in the Deccan Traps as a Natural Analogue for Mineral Carbon Sequestration and Low-Temperature Deformation
papers.abstract: Cavity-filling calcite is among the most widespread secondary phases in the Deccan Traps, and its position late in the amygdale paragenesis, after zeolites and silica phases, is long established. Two questions that remain open are addressed here: whether this calcite retains a mechanical record of deformation imposed after the cavities were sealed, and what a naturally carbonated flood-basalt pile can tell us about the durability of engineered mineral carbon storage. Calcite from three closely spaced amygdaloidal basalt exposures in the district of Maharashtra, Ane Ghat in Junnar taluka, Pune, Shindewadi 1 and Shindewadi 2 in Parner taluka, Ahilyanagar was examined by transmitted-light petrography, scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectrometry (SEM–EDS) and micro-Raman spectroscopy, with growth features deliberately separated from post-growth strain features. All three occurrences comprise coarse, optically continuous calcite grown into open voids: rhombohedral cleavage is perfect, birefringence is extreme, planar crystal faces survive in secondary-electron images, and no replacement front is developed against the basalt wall. Superimposed on this growth fabric are closely spaced polysynthetic e-twin lamellae, undulose extinction, cleavage-controlled intracrystalline microfractures, and healed fractures carrying trails of secondary inclusions. Because these features truncate cleavage and crystal boundaries that are continuous elsewhere in the same individual, they post-date crystal growth. Twin morphology is dominated by thin, straight lamellae, which on the Ferrill classification indicates deformation below roughly 170–200 ◦C. EDS spectra confirm a Cacarbonate composition; because light-element quantification in a coated carbonate is not reliable, measured Ca/C atomic ratios of 1.31–1.61 depart substantially from the ideal value of unity and the analyses are treated as semi-quantitative throughout. Micro-Raman spectra are those of well-ordered calcite, with lattice modes near 156 and 279–281 cm−1 and internal modes at 711–712 cm−1 (ν4) and 1085–1087 cm−1 (ν1); differences between sites do not exceed instrument calibration uncertainty. The results are placed in the framework of in situ mineral carbon sequestration. Deccan amygdale calcite is a completed natural experiment in basalt carbonation: divalent cations liberated by fluid–rock interaction was fixed as a thermodynamically stable carbonate that has survived approximately 66 million years in the same pore volume now targeted for engineered CO2 injection. The microstructural record modifies that otherwise reassuring picture in a specific way. Mineralized amygdales were subsequently strained, brittle microfractures propagated through the carbonate cement, and those fractures were later healed by carbonate-bearing fluids. Permanence of mineral trapping in a tectonically quiescent plateau interior is therefore neither unconditional nor catastrophically compromised: it is a balance between fracture generation and carbonate self-sealing that can be read directly from the cement.

Twin morphology is dominated by thin, straight lamellae, which on the Ferrill classification indicates deformation below roughly 170–200 ◦C. The results are placed in the framework of in situ mineral carbon sequestration.

papers.title: Cross-stress transcriptomic integration in Marchantia polymorpha reveals stress-specific expression of regulated cell-death-associated genes
papers.abstract: Regulated cell death (RCD) contributes to plant development, stress adaptation, and immunity, but whether RCD-associated genes show conserved transcriptional responses across diverse stresses remains unclear. Here, we performed a comparative reanalysis of publicly available Marchantia polymorpha RNA-seq datasets to investigate recurrent and stress-specific expression of RCD-associated genes. We uniformly processed 36 RNA-seq samples from three independent studies, yielding nine stress-versus-control comparisons: eight abiotic (seven from one study and an independent high-light experiment) and one pathogen infection. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified for each of the 9 stress datasets compared to their respective controls, which were then examined for shared DEGs among different sets of stress vs. control comparisons. A curated list of 14 RCD-associated genes previously identified in M. polymorpha were used to examine conservation of transcriptional response. Integrated expression data were additionally examined using weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) after batch correction of dataset. Of 34 DEGs shared across all nine comparisons, only 12 changed in the same direction in every comparison. The 34 genes included two transcription factors, an AP2/ERF-family factor (Mp5g22160) and a bHLH factor (Mp2g00890), which were upregulated in infection and Schröder high-light but downregulated in all seven Tan et al. comparisons. Among 14 curated RCD-associated genes, 10 were differentially expressed in at least one comparison, and MpZOU2 was the only one regulated in more than one (upregulated in cold, darkness and infection; downregulated in Tan high-light). WGCNA identified 64 co-expression modules, including an infection-associated module enriched in protein ubiquitination, proteasome-mediated degradation, ER-associated degradation, autophagy, and membrane trafficking, and a nitrogen-deficiency and osmotic-stress-associated module enriched in oxidative stress responses and cell-wall organization. Together, these findings indicate that M. polymorpha does not exhibit a uniform transcriptional RCD program across diverse stresses. Instead, RCD-associated genes appear to be selectively recruited within broader, context-dependent stress-response networks. The recurrent regulation of MpZOU2 identifies it as a candidate for functional investigation, while emphasizing that transcript-level changes alone do not establish RCD execution.

Integrated expression data were additionally examined using weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) after batch correction of dataset.

papers.title: One-step microbial conversion of waste molasses into bioactive fulvic-like acid fertilizer for sustainable soil quality improvement and agricultural waste valorization
papers.abstract: Waste molasses (WM), a carbon rich by-product of sugar production, is frequently underutilized, resulting in environmental pollution and resource loss. In this study, a one-step microbial bioconversion process using Bacillus subtilis was developed to transform WM into molasses derived fulvic acid (MFA). The highest MFA yield (33.54%) was achieved at 35 °C, 48 h, and a 5% inoculation rate. Integrated GC-MS and LC-MS analyses revealed dynamic substrate transformation during fermentation and suggested that 4-hydroxy-2-methylacetophenone, 4-oxododecanedioic acid, and 3-hydroxy-2-octylpentanedioic acid were putative intermediates involved in MFA formation. Structural characterization showed that the resulting MFA possessed a loose, porous morphology and abundant hydroxyl, carboxyl, and carbonyl groups. In a single 150 d field trial, MFA application was associated with higher soil organic carbon and humus contents than the unfertilized control and promoted maize vegetative growth. MFA also enriched the microbial communities including Pseudomonas , Acidobacterium , Actinobacteria , and Bacteroidetes . The abundance of several genes related to carbon assimilation and carboxylation, including rbcL , rbcS , accB , accC , and pccA , has also increased. Metabolomic analysis further revealed shifts in metabolites associated with central carbon metabolic pathways, including glycolysis and the pentose phosphate pathway MFA application also markedly promoted maize growth without chemical fertilizer input, demonstrating its potential as an organic soil amendment and partial fertilizer substitute. Collectively, these findings suggest that a one-step microbial transformation can convert WM into functional fulvic-like acid fertilizer. This method provides a potential route for mineral derived FA production. Simultaneously combining the reuse of agricultural waste, improvement of soil quality, reduction of partial fertilizer dependence, and development of circular agriculture.

papers.title: N-Doped Carbon-Confined Metal Sulfide Heterojunctions for Solar Water Evaporation and Adsorption-Assisted Photocatalytic Antibiotic Removal
papers.abstract: Abstract Solar-driven interfacial evaporation offers a promising route for freshwater production, yet organic micropollutants such as tetracycline (TC) in feedwater may become enriched during evaporation, jeopardizing water quality. Herein, we design a dual-functional Co8FeS8/Co9S8-based aerogel (denoted as CFS/CS@NC-H) via H2/Ar etching, which simultaneously achieves high-rate evaporation and in situ TC degradation. The introduced sulfur vacancies and the bimetallic sulfide heterostructure broaden light absorption, suppress radiative electron–hole recombination, and promote nonradiative relaxation, giving rise to a synergistic photothermal–photocatalytic effect. Raman spectroscopy and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) analyses further reveal that the Co8FeS8/Co9S8-based material effectively activates water molecules and substantially reduces the evaporation enthalpy. Consequently, under 1 sun illumination, the CFS/CS@NC-H aerogel delivers an evaporation rate of 2.31 kg m–2h–1 in pure water, and comparable rates are sustained in lake water, seawater, heavy metal-containing wastewater, and TC solution, demonstrating excellent salt resistance and practical adaptability. During evaporation, the aerogel efficiently degrades TC, thereby mitigating the risk of pollutant accumulation. The detoxification efficacy was further validated via pea sprout germination bioassays; the degraded TC solution achieved a germination rate of 84%, closely approaching that of pure water (90%) and far surpassing that of the untreated TC solution (56%), unequivocally confirming the drastic reduction in biological toxicity resulting from the catalytic degradation. This work highlights H2/Ar etching as an effective strategy to engineer transition metal sulfide-based materials for integrated solar evaporation and pollutant degradation, holding significant promise for sustainable water purification in complex aquatic environments.

papers.title: Carbon Pore Architecture for Sulfur Accommodation, Retention, and Electrochemical Kinetics in Lithium–Sulfur Cells
papers.abstract: Abstract Lithium–sulfur cells provide an ideal platform for studying how carbon pore architecture governs sulfur accommodation, polysulfide retention, and electrochemical kinetics. Although porous carbons with different pore characteristics have been investigated, their intrinsic pore-structure effects remain difficult to distinguish because previous studies generally employ independently synthesized carbons with different surface chemistries and morphologies. Here, we establish an experimental platform by systematically blending commercial porous carbons with controlled pore architectures while preserving their intrinsic physicochemical properties. Dynamic image analysis, gas adsorption, electron microscopy, elemental mapping, and thermogravimetric analysis reveal systematic changes in pore structure, particle morphology, sulfur distribution, and sulfur retention as the carbon ratio is varied. Sulfur confined within micropore-dominated structures exhibits greater thermal stability than sulfur accommodated in mesopore-dominated structures, demonstrating that sulfur accommodation and sulfur retention are fundamentally different processes. Electrochemical measurements further establish a clear structure–property relationship, showing that micropore-dominated architectures enhance sulfur retention but impede ion transport, whereas mesopore-dominated architectures facilitate reaction kinetics at the expense of sulfur confinement and electrode stability. An optimized pore architecture balances these competing effects, enabling efficient sulfur utilization, suppressed polysulfide migration, improved reaction kinetics, and stable cycling under high sulfur loading. As a result, this study provides mechanistic insight and practical design principles for rational pore-architecture engineering in lithium–sulfur cells.

papers.title: Comparative Study of Synthesis Characterization and Thermal Properties of Homomer and Copolymers of N-Benzylmaleimide
papers.journal: American Journal of Polymer Science and Technology
papers.abstract: N-Benzylmaleimide (NBMI) was synthesized and subsequently copolymerized with methyl methacrylate (MMA) through free-radical polymerization in tetrahydrofuran (THF), using azobisisobutyronitrile (AIBN) and benzoyl peroxide (BPO) as initiators. The synthesized NBMI homopolymer and NBMI-MMA copolymer (CBMI) were characterized by Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, proton nuclear magnetic resonance ( 1 H NMR) spectroscopy, solubility studies, intrinsic-viscosity measurements, gel permeation chromatography (GPC), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). The NBMI homopolymer and CBMI copolymer were obtained in yields of 39.5% and 44.0%, respectively, with intrinsic-viscosity values of 0.031 and 0.060 dL/g. FT-IR and 1 H NMR analyses confirmed the consumption of the maleimide carbon–carbon double bond during polymerization, while the characteristic imide-ring structure remained intact. Solubility studies revealed that the CBMI copolymer exhibited favourable solubility in several organic solvents. GPC analysis showed that the copolymer possessed a molecular weight of 25,881 g mol −1 . Furthermore, TGA demonstrated a predominantly single-stage degradation pattern and satisfactory thermal stability. The higher yield and intrinsic viscosity of CBMI compared with the NBMI homopolymer indicate the successful incorporation of MMA into the polymer system. Overall, the results demonstrate that NBMI-MMA copolymer exhibits favourable structural, physicochemical, and thermal characteristics, making it a promising material for potential advanced polymer applications.

papers.title: Recent advances in critical care nutrition: from dose escalation to phase-guided and response-guided care
papers.abstract: Purpose of review To critically appraise recent advances that are shifting critical care nutrition from uniform nutrient targets towards phase-guided, phenotype-guided and response-guided care, with particular emphasis on major studies published in 2025–2026. Recent findings Recent large trials do not support routine early full-dose energy or high-dose protein delivery in unselected critically ill patients, and some higher dose strategies have generated safety signals. Indirect calorimetry improves measurement of energy expenditure, but measured expenditure is not synonymous with the dose that should be delivered. Emerging data suggest that dynamic responses, including early phosphate trajectories, may help identify metabolic readiness for feeding, although no validated bedside marker exists. Pharmacological intravenous vitamin C has shown no benefit and recurring harm signals in shocked patients, whereas micronutrient care should distinguish physiological requirements and deficiency correction from megadosing. After ICU discharge, intake frequently falls during the transition from enteral to oral nutrition, and intake-guided protocols have achieved high nutritional adequacy in proof-of-concept studies. Summary Critical care nutrition is moving from universal targets towards phase-guided, phenotype-guided and response-guided treatment. Acute-phase caution should not become prolonged underfeeding; repeated metabolic assessment, body composition, reliable intake monitoring and continuity through recovery are central priorities.

papers.title: RSM-based optimization of mechanical and moisture resistance properties of ternary polymer nanocomposites
papers.abstract: Abstract Epoxy-based polymer Nanocomposites are widely investigated for electrical insulation applications due to their exceptional mechanical and dielectric properties; however, moisture absorption and brittleness remain major challenges. This study aimed to develop and optimize Epoxy/ Ethylene Propylene Diene Monomer (EPDM) /nano-silica ternary nanocomposites with increased tensile strength and reduced water absorption using Response Surface Methodology (RSM) based on Central Composite Design (CCD). The effects of EPDM concentration, nano-silica loading, and sonication time were evaluated through 20 experimental runs. Water absorption was measured according to ASTM D570 after 240-hour immersion, while tensile strength was determined using ASTM D638 standard. The statistical analysis showed that all three processing parameters significantly affected the measured responses within the investigated experimental ranges, with nano-silica loading showing the largest statistical effect. The developed linear models showed satisfactory fit and predictive statistics, with non-significant lack-of-fit results. Increasing nano-silica loading and sonication time was associated with increased tensile strength and reduced water absorption within the experimental design space. These response trends may be related to changes in the polymer–filler environment and the processing-dependent state of the silica-containing phase. The optimized formulation exhibited a tensile strength of 90.9 ± 0.46 MPa and water absorption of 0.0441 ± 0.0003% under the investigated test conditions. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of the Epoxy/EPDM/nano-silica system as a candidate for further investigation in electrical-insulation applications.

papers.title: Forest-residue-derived constituents for low-carbon cementitious materials: evidence boundaries, quantitative trade-offs, and cold-region service qualification
papers.abstract: Forest-residue-derived constituents are increasingly being considered for low-carbon cementitious materials, but their functions differ substantially and should not be treated as a single waste-substitution category. Wood ash may serve as a screened supplementary cementitious material or mineral filler, wood-derived biochar mainly modifies hydration and pore-water behavior at low dosage, and wood fiber acts primarily as crack-control reinforcement. This review compares these three material classes through their source-specific characteristics, quantitative performance ranges, and governing microstructural mechanisms. Direct evidence from wood-derived constituents is distinguished from mechanistic analog evidence from non-wood biomass ashes and lignocellulosic fibers. Published studies commonly examine wood ash at approximately 5%–20% cement replacement and biochar at low dosages, often at approximately 0.5–3 wt% of binder, while wood and related lignocellulosic fibers are generally used at low volume fractions. These ranges are screening values rather than universal design limits because performance depends strongly on processing, water demand, dispersion, interfacial behavior, and mixture composition. Cold-region exposure is considered a demanding service-qualification case rather than as a separate material theme. Freeze–thaw, salt exposure, and chloride transport are used to assess whether changes in pore-water distribution, air-void stability, interfaces, and crack connectivity remain beneficial under severe service conditions. The review concludes with a staged route from constituent characterization and mixture screening to mechanism verification, exposure-relevant testing, and field validation.

papers.title: Robustness-aware multi-objective optimization of injection molding processing conditions and cooling channel geometry
papers.journal: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
papers.abstract: Abstract The optimization of injection molding is strongly affected by variations in operating conditions, which influence part quality, cycle time, and energy consumption. Traditional approaches focus on nominal conditions and neglect unavoidable process fluctuations, whereas robust optimization seeks solutions that remain stable under variability. However, robustness is usually imposed through a single predefined formulation, even though different formulations may yield different optimization outcomes. This work investigates how the choice of robustness formulation affects multi-objective optimization in injection molding, using a two-ring case study modeled in Moldex3D with artificial neural network surrogates and a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm. In a first stage, the operating conditions (melt and mold temperatures) are optimized by comparing variance-based, average, worst-case, and expectation-based formulations through their Pareto fronts and solution rankings. In a second stage, the analysis is extended to conformal cooling channel geometries (two-ring, three-ring, spiral, and zig-zag), assessing how robustness against operating-condition variability influences geometry selection. The formulation reshapes the Pareto fronts and the solution rankings at both levels, but changes the selected solution unevenly: the recommended operating point stays essentially fixed at the lower boundary of the operating window, whereas the preferred cooling-channel geometry and the cost of imposing robustness depend on the formulation, because near-equivalent designs differ widely in geometry. Robustness is therefore not a neutral metric and must be defined according to the application and to the level, process parameters, or cooling-channel design, at which the engineering decision is made. The reported insensitivity of the recommended operating point to the robustness formulation is specific to the present material (PP, Borealis Borcom BG055AI) and operating window, whereas the general result is the asymmetry between the process-parameter and geometry levels.

papers.title: Rooftop Photovoltaic Panel Segmentation in UAV Imagery Using Attention U-Net with a ResNet34 Encoder
papers.journal: Gümüşhane Üniversitesi Fen Bilimleri Enstitüsü Dergisi
papers.abstract: Today, satellite image analysis and mapping systems play a significant role in urban planning, energy management, potential assessment, and sustainable development studies. In addition to the difficulty and high cost of fieldwork, the analysis of observations delays potential assessment and detection efforts. To overcome this delay and high cost, the use of satellite imagery is among the most important methods that facilitate these processes. In this study, a deep learning-based method is proposed to detect solar power plants from satellite imagery. This proposed method combines the U-Net architecture with an attention mechanism with the pre-trained ResNet34 encoder, enabling the efficient integration of both low-level and high-level features. The Albumentations library was used for data augmentation during the model training process, and the images were resized to 256x256. In the post-processing stage, the Dense Conditional Random Fields (CRF) method was applied to improve the accuracy of the segmentation masks generated by the model. For the test subset of the PV01 dataset, 95% IoU, 97% Dice, 99% Precision, 97% Recall, and 98% Accuracy were achieved. These results lead to lower costs and sharper results in determining energy potential.

papers.title: Engineering Interface and Orientation to Construct BNNS/LM Heterostructures with High Thermal Conductivity and Electrical Insulation for Improved Phonon Transport
papers.abstract: Abstract The synergistic optimization of high thermal conductivity and electrical insulation is a key challenge in thermal interface materials (TIMs). Conventional ceramic-based composites are inherently incapable of reconciling the contradictory demands of thermal conduction, electrical insulation, and low brittleness, while liquid metal fillers are plagued by poor interfacial compatibility and the risk of leakage. To address these issues, a synergistic strategy integrating molecular interfacial modification and microstructural alignment is developed to construct boron nitride nanosheets (BNNS)/liquid metal (LM) heterostructures. Using H2O2-assisted chlorosulfonic acid intercalation, h-BN is efficiently exfoliated and hydroxylated. Thiomalic acid (TMA) serves as a bridge, achieving uniform LM anchoring on BNNS and preventing LM leakage at a high loading of 42 wt %. A pressure-induced orientation is further applied to vertically align BNNS/LM hybrids, generating preferentially oriented and interconnected thermally conductive networks. The resulting composite exhibits an out-of-plane thermal conductivity of 17.76 W m–1 K–1, while maintaining good electrical insulation with an electrical resistivity exceeding 6 × 109 Ω m. LED tests show that this material reduces LED chip temperature by 16.7 °C compared to a commercial thermal pad. This cross-scale synergistic strategy provides a material design solution that combines high thermal conductivity and electrical safety for thermal management of high-power-density electronic devices.

papers.title: Fast structural remodeling of Jatropha curcas thylakoids upon recovery underpins chloroplast resilience to drought
papers.abstract: Abstract Jatropha curcas is a moderate stem-succulent oil crop renowned for its drought tolerance. While the photosynthetic activity of drought-stressed and rewatered Jatropha curcas has been investigated, little is known about the effects of drought and rewatering on chloroplast integrity and thylakoid architecture, critical determinants of photosynthetic performance under stress. Here, we exposed J. curcas seedlings to 19 days of water withdrawal followed by rewatering. Leaf relative water content remained unchanged throughout, indicating efficient water retention. Leaf anatomy was largely preserved, but chloroplasts became slightly smaller. Small-angle neutron scattering and transmission electron microscopy revealed a 2–4 nm decrease in granum repeat distance under drought. Electron microscopy further showed that this decrease was stronger in palisade than in spongy parenchyma chloroplasts. In thylakoids, the photosynthetic complexes were adjusted differently under drought: photosystem (PS) I and light harvesting complex (LHC) II remained unchanged, whereas PSII complexes decreased, increasing the PSI/PSII and LHCII/PSII ratios. Among the remaining PSII, larger supercomplexes were proportionally enriched, suggesting their higher drought stability. These changes coincided with a moderate decrease in PSII activity ( F v /F m ) and increased non-photochemical quenching. After rewatering, granum repeat distances recovered within hours (0.5–1 h in spongy and 5 h in palisade chloroplasts), revealing the involvement of rapidly reversible membrane remodeling under drought, while full recovery of photosynthetic performance and thylakoid protein composition was slower, requiring days. The high plasticity and rapid recovery of the thylakoid architecture is proposed to enable Jatropha curcas to restore its drought-affected photosynthetic apparatus and resume photosynthesis once water becomes available.

papers.title: Binary systems based on fatty acids and alcohols as bio-based thermochromic phase change materials for thermal energy storage
papers.journal: Journal of Thermal Analysis and Calorimetry
papers.abstract: Abstract In this study, bio-based thermochromic phase change materials (TPCMs) were obtained for potential energy storage applications. The phenomenon of thermochromism enables the observation of color changes in TPCMs during phase transitions. Three-component thermochromic systems were prepared using bromocresol purple as the organic dye, stearic acid as the color developer, and behenyl alcohol as the organic solvent. Simultaneously, both fatty acid and alcohol acted as phase change materials. Different mass ratios of the components were prepared and analyzed. The resulting TPCM mixtures were examined by Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, differential scanning calorimetry, and thermal imaging. The obtained TPCMs exhibited high melting enthalpy (ca. 150–200 J g −1 ) in the temperature range of 50–70 °C, good thermal stability up to approximately 190 °C (T3% ≈ 190 °C), and a pronounced thermochromic response (Δ E ≈ 30). These materials show potential for application not only as phase change energy storage media, but also as colorimetric indicators.

papers.title: POSSIBILITIES OF SYNCHRONOUS THERMAL ANALYSIS FOR ASSESSING THE FIRE HAZARD PROPERTIES OF POLYMER MATERIALS
papers.journal: Problems of risk management in the technosphere
papers.abstract: The article discusses the possibilities of the synchronous thermal analysis method combined with infrared spectroscopy to assess the fire-hazardous properties of polymer materials using the example of two polyvinyl chloride materials, which are quartz-vinyl tiles and canvas for a stretch ceiling. The study was carried out on a synchronous thermal analyzer NETZSCH STA 449 F3 Jupiter at a heating rate of 20 °C/min to 900 °C in an atmospheric atmosphere with simultaneous analysis of volatile products using an IR Fourier spectrometer FSM-1201. It has been established that due to the content of an additional organic filler (wood flour), quartz vinyl decomposes in four stages, with the first stage (≈287 °C) characterized by an exothermic peak on the DSC curve, accompanied by intense release of HCl, CO and Co₂, which indicates possible flaming. The stretch ceiling fabric (plasticized PVC without combustible fillers) decomposes according to the scheme typical for PVC plastics in three stages; Up to temperatures above 405 °C, the active release of gaseous products is accompanied by the presence of exothermic peaks on the DSC curve, which indicates the absence of flaming . It is shown that the dynamics of the release of gaseous carbonyl compounds, HCl, CO, and co₂, determined by the characteristic bands in the IR spectra, allows us to identify temperature and time intervals in which the occurrence of flame combustion of the materials under consideration is possible. It is concluded that the STA–X method provides objective information on the thermal and oxidative degradation of polymers, thermal effects, and kinetics of gas release and can be used to assess the fire hazard of materials and predict their behavior in a fire.

papers.title: Polylactide‐polydimethylsiloxane copolymers enabled by one‐pot chain‐shuttling ring‐opening copolymerization: Synthesis, properties and chemical recycling
papers.abstract: Abstract The development of degradable and incompatible copolymers with tunable material properties has garnered significant attention. Direct copolymerization of lactide (LA) and hexamethylcyclotrisiloxane (D 3 ) faces severe technical barriers due to their significant structural and reactivity differences. In this study, one‐pot chain shuttling ring‐opening polymerization process for the copolymerization of LA and D 3 is reported using the Zn‐Co double metal cyanide as heterogeneous catalyst and propylene oxide (PO) as bridging intermediate. Copolymerization kinetic study shows that the polymerization of LA is dominant in the early stage, and the average molecular weight of the copolymer unimodally increases with monomer conversion. Mechanistic investigations based on experimental and computational studies support a dual‐cycle chain‐shuttling pathway, in which PO acts as an intermediate in the chain shuttling process between the LA‐PO and D 3 ‐PO copolymerization cycles. The as‐prepared copolymers with different chemical compositions exhibit tunable thermal properties. Moreover, the resulting copolymers can be depolymerized to regenerate LA and silicone oil, demonstrating their potential for chemical recyclability. This study presents a practical and versatile approach for the synthesis of degradable and incompatible copolymers.

papers.title: SOLID SOLUTION REGIONS AND PHASE EQUILIBRIA IN THE Ag8GeS6‒Ag7SiS5I SYSTEM
papers.journal: Scientific Bulletin of the Uzhhorod University Series «Chemistry»
papers.abstract: In this work, a physicochemical study of phase equilibria in the Ag8GeS6–Ag7SiS5I system was carried out for the first time, which is of key importance for the development of new functional materials and solid electrolytes with enhanced ionic conductivity for all-solid-state power sources and energy storage systems. The relevance of the study is driven by the necessity to search for superionic conductors based on Ag+ silver cations that crystallize in the argyrodite structural type and combine high ionic mobility, chemical stability, and operational safety. Synthesized polycrystalline samples of the Ag8GeS6–Ag7SiS5I system were investigated by differential thermal analysis (DTA) and X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) with indexing of diffraction patterns using the EXPO 2014 software. Based on experimental data, the complete phase diagram of the Ag8GeS6–Ag7SiS5I system was constructed for the first time. It was established that a continuous series of solid solutions (Roozeboom Type I) is formed in the high-temperature region above the phase transition temperatures of the initial components. The smooth course of the liquidus and solidus curves confirms the complete mutual solubility of the components in the liquid and high-temperature solid states. Upon cooling, a solubility gap is observed, accompanied by the formation of a two-phase region coexisting terminal Ag8-xGe1-xSixS6-xIx solid solutions with the orthorhombic structure of LT-Ag8GeS6 (SG Pna21) and Ag8-xGe1-xSixS6-xIx solid solutions with a cubic structure based on Ag7SiS5I (space group F-43m). The homogeneity ranges of the terminal solid solutions exceed 25 and 60 mol.%, respectively. The compositional dependence of the unit cell volumes of the alloys is in good agreement with the identified boundaries of the phase regions. The formation mechanism of substitution solid solutions with the composition Ag8-xGe1-xSixS6-xIx was described via defect reactions in Kröger–Vink notation. It was demonstrated that simultaneous isovalent (Ge+4↔Si+4) and heterovalent (S-2↔I-) two-ion substitution is accompanied by the formation of additional silver cation vacancies. The emergence of new cation vacancies creates favorable conditions for reducing the activation energy of Ag+ ion migration and serves as a prerequisite for increasing ionic conductivity. The asymmetry in the extent of the boundary solid solutions was explained within the polarity of isomorphism, taking into account the size factor and unit cell volume. It was shown that the cubic structure of Ag7SiS5I, featuring a larger cell volume and longer interatomic distances, significantly more effectively relaxes local structural stresses upon the incorporation of the Ge+4 ion, which accounts for its wider homogeneity range. The obtained results establish a fundamental framework for the targeted design of new solid electrolytes with controlled defect structure and high ionic conductivity.

papers.title: Preparation and application of functional hydroxyethyl cellulose hydrogels containing β-cyclodextrin complexes for cosmetic materials
papers.abstract: To address the formulation challenges associated with cosmetic active ingredients, including degradation, oxidation, and potential skin irritation, functional supramolecular inclusion complexes were prepared by a coprecipitation method using arbutin, niacinamide, and benzoic acid as guest molecules and β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) as the host. Unlike conventional single-component encapsulation approaches, this study proposes a novel multi-component co-delivery strategy for the simultaneous incorporation of multiple skin-brightening agents and a poorly water-soluble preservative into a single delivery platform. The potential host–guest interactions and complexation behavior were investigated using UV–Vis spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), proton nuclear magnetic resonance ( 1 H NMR) spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM). The resulting inclusion complexes were subsequently incorporated into a hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC)-based hydrogel to formulate multifunctional topical lotions. The formulations exhibited weakly acidic pH values of 5.53 and 5.55, within the range generally considered compatible with human skin. Rheological and texture profile analyses demonstrated pseudoplastic (shear-thinning) behavior and appropriate mechanical properties, including hardness, adhesiveness, and cohesiveness, for topical application. Furthermore, disk diffusion assays demonstrated antifungal activity against Candida albicans in the formulations containing the benzoic acid/β-CD inclusion complex. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the integration of multi-component β-CD inclusion complexes into an HEC hydrogel network yields functional formulations with potential as cosmetic platforms.

papers.title: Formulation and characterization of solid dispersion adsorbate of Candesartan Cilexetil: in vitro dissolution and in vivo performance
papers.abstract: Introduction Candesartan Cilexetil (CC) is a non-peptide angiotensin II type 1 receptor antagonist widely used in the treatment of hypertension. However, CC has poor aqueous solubility (0.006 ± 0.002 mg/mL), low oral bioavailability (15%) and undergoes significant first-pass metabolism. Methods Candesartan Cilexetil Solid Dispersion adsorbate (CC-SDAs) was formulated by the fusion method, employing polyethylene glycol (PEG) 4000 as a hydrophilic carrier and Neusilin® US2 as an adsorbent, to improve the solubility, dissolution, and oral bioavailability of CC. The formulation was optimized using a 3 2 factorial design. Results and Discussion The optimized SDA formulation exhibited the following properties: Carr’s index (9.86 ± 0.09%), Hausner’s ratio (1.10 ± 0.16) and angle of repose (26.00 ± 0.19°), which shows improved flow property. DSC and XRD studies confirmed the conversion of the crystalline drug into an amorphous form. The optimized SDA formulation achieved %CDR of 90.41 ± 0.95% at Q30 min, demonstrating a marked improvement in in vitro dissolution compared to the pure drug (%CDR of 57.20 ± 3.78% at Q30 min). Furthermore, in vivo pharmacokinetic studies revealed a 2.02-fold enhanced oral bioavailability of CC from the SDA formulation compared to the CC suspension. Therefore, the SDA technique proves to be a promising approach for enhancing the solubility and dissolution of poorly water-soluble drugs.

papers.title: Tropospheric Ozone Assessment Report II: Changing health impacts of global ozone exposure
papers.journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A Mathematical Physical and Engineering Sciences
papers.abstract: As part of the second Tropospheric Ozone Assessment Report (TOAR-II), we synthesize global observations and observationally constrained estimates of surface-level ozone (O3) with contemporary literature to characterize the global distribution and trends of long-term O3 exposure, focusing on two health-relevant metrics and health impacts attributable to long-term exposure. The highest 2016-2020 surface-level O3 concentrations are observed or estimated in South Asia, eastern China, and parts of the Middle East and North Africa. From 2000 to 2020, O3 declined across southeastern North America and parts of Eastern Europe, while the largest increases occurred in South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa. Global premature mortality from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) attributable to long-term O3 exposure nearly doubled between 2000 and 2020, reaching approximately 500 000 deaths annually. This overall increase obscures decreasing attributable deaths across North America and Europe and increasing deaths across large parts of the Global South. To spur high-quality, robust research on O3 health impacts, we summarize state-of-the-science practices for conducting health impact assessments (HIAs) and characterizing associated uncertainty. We also call for expanded in situ monitoring, improved health datasets and epidemiologic evidence, and sustained precursor emission reductions to clarify and limit the growing global health burden of O3 under climate change and demographic shifts. This article is part of the theme issue 'Tropospheric Ozone Assessment Report II'.
