papers.title: Thermal analysis of ternary hybrid nanofluids for advanced cooling of AI chips and data centers using dual numerical techniques
papers.abstract: The problem of controlling the massive heat produced by high-performance AI processors has become more difficult due to the quick development of artificial intelligence (AI) and the exponential expansion of data centers. In addition to reducing processing efficiency, excessive heat endangers system dependability and energy sustainability. To mitigate this challenge, the present study investigates the application of ternary hybrid nanofluids (Tri-HNF: Al₂O₃–CuO–GNP/EG) as advanced coolants, comparing their performance with binary hybrid nanofluids (Di-HNF: Al₂O₃–CuO/EG) and mono nanofluids (NF: Al₂O₃/EG) in enhancing thermal regulation over a flat surface. The Collocation Chebyshev Method (CCM) and the Galerkin-weighted residual Method (GWRM), two separate numerical techniques included in Mathematica 11.3, were used to convert the governing nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) to ordinary differential equations (ODEs) and solve them numerically. The excellent agreement between the two methods demonstrates the consistency and accuracy of the numerical schemes. The effects of magnetic field, viscosity, suction, radiation, and heat generating factors on the flow and temperature fields were revealed using parametric experiments. Findings show that the Tri-HNF exhibits superior thermal performance due to the synergistic effects of Al₂O₃ (enhanced stability), CuO (excellent thermal conductivity), and graphene nanoplatelets (GNP) (exceptional heat transport efficiency). Compared to Di-HNF and NF, the Tri-HNF achieves higher Nusselt numbers, improved heat dispersion, and lower thermal resistance. In summary, this work demonstrates that Tri-HNF provide an efficient and reliable solution for cooling AI chips, microelectronics, and data centers, offering a pathway toward sustainable and thermally stable next-generation computing systems.

papers.title: Bio-Briquettes Derived from Fibrous Agricultural and Softwood (FAS) Residues: A Review on Production Methods, Effects of Chemical Components, Utilization Potential, and Future Outlooks
papers.abstract: Fibrous Agricultural and Softwood (FAS) residues represent abundant lignocellulosic resources for bio-briquette production, yet their potential is strongly influenced by feedstock characteristics, chemical composition, processing conditions, and application requirements. A structured narrative review of 106 publications was conducted to synthesize these interrelationships and identify development prospects. FAS bio-briquette performance is governed by interactions between feedstock composition and processing conditions, with lignocellulosic fractions and ash-forming minerals determining the balance among mechanical integrity, energy performance, and combustion behavior. Various FAS residues, including rice husk and straw, corn cob, sugarcane bagasse, coconut and oil palm residues, cocoa pod shell, fruit and nut residues, pine residues, and softwoods have been investigated under diverse processing conditions. Reported properties varied widely with densities of 0.30–1.32 g/cm3, calorific values of 12.41–31.51 MJ/kg, moisture contents (MC) of 0.3–29.72%, ash contents of 0.1–59.2%, volatile matter (VM) of 0.9–90.7%, fixed carbon (FC) of 22.97–81.73%, compression strength of 0.004–21.75 MPa, ignition times of 10.25–106 s, burning rates of 0.119–5.85 g/s, and burning times of 23.88–84 min, while shatter resistance >99% and shatter indices 0.56–2.49%. Beyond domestic cooking and heating, FAS bio-briquettes show potential for coal co-firing, metallurgical reduction, and construction-material applications through ash utilization, although suitability depends on application-specific trade-offs. Future development should prioritize feedstock-specific optimization, scalable production, techno-economic and life-cycle assessment, and standardized quality and sustainability criteria for reliable commercialization.

papers.title: Effect of continuous high thermal processing on physico-chemical and nutritional alterations in cold-pressed and refined edible oils
papers.abstract: Background Continuous high thermal processing of edible oils induces significant physicochemical and nutritional alterations, influence their safety, stability, and consumer acceptability. Cold-pressed oils are generally perceived as nutritionally superior, but their oxidative stability under continuous heating remains less understand compared to the refined oils. Methods Twelve edible oils (7 cold-pressed and 5 refined oils) were collected and subjected to the continuous high thermal processing at 230 ± 5 °C for 0, 1, 2, and 4 h. Fatty acid composition, peroxide value, saponification value, free fatty acid percentage, acid value, iodine value, conjugated dienes, conjugated trienes, refractive index and colour were analysed. Results Among the oils available in the both cold-pressed and refined types, cold-pressed groundnut, sunflower, rice bran and palm oil retained more polyunsaturated fatty acids at 1 h, but showed greater losses after 4 h then their refined types. Soybean oil exhibited a sharp rise in trans fatty acids (0.76 to 5.88%), whereas, coconut oil remained lowest (0.38%) at 4 h. Peroxide value increased in refined sunflower oil (7.60 to 15.81 mEq O 2 /kg), but refined and cold-pressed rice bran oil declined to 0.01 mEq O 2 /kg in after 2 h. Free fatty acid and acid values decreased variably across oils. Iodine value reduction was highest in coconut oil and minimal in soybean oil (6.72%). Saponification peaked in coconut oil (321 ± 0.68 mg KOH/g) and lowest in cold-pressed sunflower oil (213 ± 0.83 mg KOH/g). Conjugated triene rose steadily but remained below diene, while progressive darkening (L* reduction) was observed in all oils. Heating for 1 to 2 h impacted the saturation of fatty acids, while 4 h can increase the risk of trans fatty acid and dienes/trienes formation. Conclusion Continuous high thermal processing compromises the nutritional and oxidative stability of edible oils. Coconut oil showed minimal alterations, while soybean oil and sesame oil were highly susceptible. These findings highlight the need for cautious thermal application in cooking practices to preserve oil quality.

Results Among the oils available in the both cold-pressed and refined types, cold-pressed groundnut, sunflower, rice bran and palm oil retained more polyunsaturated fatty acids at 1 h, but showed greater losses after 4 h then their refined types. These findings highlight the need for cautious thermal application in cooking practices to preserve oil quality.

papers.title: Modifying Airbus A220S Fuel Tank by Electrical Heating Unit for Use of Neat Biodiesel as Aviation Fuel Without Freezing Problem
papers.journal: Düzce Üniversitesi Bilim ve Teknoloji Dergisi
papers.abstract: In this study, an active thermal management system was developed to optimize the integration of Waste Cooking Oil (WCO) biodiesel into the Airbus A220 platform to reduce the carbon footprint in the aviation sector. Biodiesel’s Cold Filter Plugging Point (CFPP), which is disadvantageous compared to Jet A-1 and is set at -5 °C, poses a risk of fuel flow interruption during high-altitude operations (-56.5 °C outside air temperature). To counter such a probability, the 9.8 cubic meters (15,000 lb) fuel tank in the center of the aircraft was modeled in a 3D environment, consisting of a structure made of Aluminum 6061, along with copper heating elements spaced 90 mm vertically. The thermal performance of the developed system was evaluated using high-resolution 3D steady-state thermal analyses in ANSYS Mechanical. In the numerical analyses, a constant surface heat flux of 500 W/m² was applied in the regions where the heating cables are in contact with the tank surface. Under International Standard Atmosphere (ISA) conditions, the analysis results at the cruising altitude of 41,000 ft indicate that the system can safely sustain the fuel temperature above the critical CFPP of -5 °C. In addition, a worst-case scenario representing the possible failure of the heating system was defined to evaluate the operational limits of the fuel tank. Contour plots indicate that the fuel tank temperature is within safe operational limits. The study results show that active fuel tank heating systems enable WCO biodiesel to be used as a sustainable alternative fuel in modern regional jets.

The study results show that active fuel tank heating systems enable WCO biodiesel to be used as a sustainable alternative fuel in modern regional jets.

papers.title: Engineering Allosteric RNA Aptamers: Molecular Mechanisms, Functional Devices, and Translational Applications
papers.abstract: Abstract Allostery enables selective and context-dependent regulation of biological function. Although classically associated with proteins, RNA also samples dynamic conformational ensembles in which ligand binding can be coupled to a spatially or functionally distinct output. Allosteric RNA aptamers harness this property to convert molecular inputs into fluorescence, catalysis, RNA processing, translational control, macromolecular recruitment, or therapeutic activity. Their modularity, genetic encodability, and intracellular functionality position them at the intersection of chemical biology, synthetic biology, functional genomics, and RNA medicine. This Review examines the mechanisms of RNA allostery, strategies for engineering ligand-responsive architectures, and applications in live-cell sensing, drug discovery, and therapeutic regulation. Representative systems are evaluated by target, structure, affinity, dynamic range, output modality, and application. We highlight aptazymes, conditional gene-control modules, biomarker-responsive circuits, and RNA-scaffolded proximity-inducing systems, and compare RNA devices with DNA aptamers, DNAzymes, and switches. Key translational barriers include context-dependent folding, intracellular instability, delivery, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, immunogenicity, and inadequate manufacturing and assay standardization. Advances in ensemble-resolved structural biology, high-throughput evolution, artificial intelligence-assisted design, and RNA delivery may establish allosteric aptamers as programmable pharmacological systems coupling molecular recognition to spatiotemporally controlled therapeutic activity.

papers.title: Regulating Silicate Speciation and Geopolymerization Kinetics through Crystalline Water in Solid Sodium Silicate Activator
papers.abstract: Abstract The performance of one-part alkali-activated materials (OP-AAMs) is strongly influenced by the hydration state and silicate speciation of solid alkali activators. In this study, the role of crystalline water in solid sodium silicate activators was systematically examined by varying the ratio of sodium metasilicate hydrate (Na2SiO3·9H2O) to anhydrous sodium silicate, while maintaining a constant Na2SiO3 dosage and effective water-to-binder ratio. Fresh and hardened properties were characterized using in situ fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR)–rheometry, isothermal calorimetry, 29Si MAS NMR, X-ray diffraction (XRD), mercury intrusion porosimetry, and scanning electron microscopy. Reducing crystalline water increased the proportion of reactive Q1 species from 24.7% to 86.0%, enhanced workability with a spread diameter of 235 mm, and accelerated early reaction kinetics, shifting the main exothermic peak from ∼20 min to 3–5 min. An optimal 50/50 blend achieved a compressive strength of 73.8 MPa at 28 days, a nanopore fraction of 83.86%, and a highly polymerized Q4/Q4(1Al)-rich gel network. These results highlight crystalline water as a key regulator of reactivity and gel structure in OP-AAMs.

papers.title: Sodium-activated bentonite as a dual-function clay platform for amikacin adsorption, pH-responsive release, and antibacterial activity
papers.abstract: Antibiotic contamination of aquatic environments is a recognized driver of antimicrobial resistance, and amikacin — a clinically important aminoglycoside — poses dual concerns: environmental persistence and systemic toxicity that limits its clinical use, underscoring the need for materials capable of both sequestering it from wastewater and delivering it locally in a controlled manner. This study aimed to evaluate sodium-activated bentonite (SB), prepared from locally sourced Iraqi bentonite, as a dual-function platform for amikacin adsorption, pH-responsive release, and antibacterial activity. An amikacin-loaded composite (AMK-SB) was prepared and characterized by FESEM-EDS, XRD, FTIR, TGA, and nitrogen adsorption–desorption analysis. Batch adsorption experiments investigated the effects of adsorbent dose, contact time, pH, and temperature, followed by kinetic, isotherm, and thermodynamic modeling. pH-responsive release was evaluated at pH 3.0–9.0, and Korsmeyer–Peppas fitting was applied only to release profiles that provided sufficient data within the valid early-release range. Antibacterial activity, matrix effects in simulated hospital effluent, and regeneration over four cycles were also assessed. Sodium activation increased BET surface area from 16.9 to 27.7 m 2 g⁻ 1 and pore volume from 0.0623 to 0.0872 cm 3 g⁻ 1 ; amikacin loading (∼6.7 wt%) partially reduced these values, consistent with drug deposition in interlayer spaces and pores. Adsorption followed pseudo-second-order kinetics (R 2 = 0.9983–0.9997) and the Langmuir isotherm (R 2 = 0.9737–0.9916), with qmax of 63.29–81.55 mg g⁻ 1 over 25–60°C. The process was spontaneous and exothermic (ΔG° = -26.99 to -28.79 kJ mol⁻ 1 ; ΔH° = -11.65 kJ mol⁻ 1 ). Under the selected operating conditions, amikacin removal remained high, generally within the ∼88–90% range depending on the experimental endpoint. Antibacterial activity was retained against S. aureus, E. coli , and P. aeruginosa (inhibition zones: 30, 29, and 26 mm). Release was pH-dependent, approaching 100% at pH 3.0 but only ∼38% at pH 9.0 after 180 min. The material retained ∼85% adsorption capacity after four regeneration cycles. These findings establish AMK-SB as a low-cost, recyclable clay platform integrating antibiotic adsorption from aqueous media with pH-responsive release and preserved antibacterial activity, offering potential applications in both environmental remediation and localized antimicrobial delivery at acidic infection sites.

papers.title: Pixel-wise state node encoding for noise-robust event-based optical flow
papers.abstract: Abstract Event cameras provide sparse, asynchronous measurements triggered by changes in scene brightness, offering high temporal resolution but also making learning-based optical flow sensitive to illumination-induced noise. We propose pixel-wise state node (SN) encoding, a biologically inspired state-space representation in which each pixel maintains a persistent state that evolves via leaky temporal integration with continuous-time dynamics. By embedding temporal information directly into state evolution, SN introduces a strong inductive bias that yields compact and stable spatio-temporal features while naturally suppressing spurious events arising from sensor noise. Integrated into RAFT-style optical flow models, SN encoding consistently improves over time surfaces on MVSEC and DSEC-Flow, and achieves competitive performance relative to voxel-grid-based approaches while avoiding explicit temporal binning and additional temporal aggregation mechanisms required to process multiple bins. As a result, SN improves accuracy and robustness under event noise and offers a promising pathway toward low-latency, near-sensor edge-device implementations.

papers.title: A narrative review of the decade-long integration of professional postgraduate education with standardized residency training in China
papers.abstract: Since 2014, China has comprehensively implemented the Standardized Residency Training (SRT) program nationwide, and the integration of professional postgraduate education with SRT has operated for over a decade. This narrative review, based on searches of Wanfang Data and PubMed from January 2015 to December 2025, examines the achievements, persistent challenges, and reform options of this integration system. While the system has shortened medical training from six to three years and enriched clinical exposure, a fundamental structural contradiction persists: the dual identity of professional postgraduates as both “students” and “residents” creates an inherent conflict between clinical practice and academic training. Within the fixed three-year period, postgraduates bear the combined burden of 33 months of clinical rotations, coursework, and thesis research, leaving insufficient protected time for scientific research, compounded by misaligned training objectives, welfare inequity, delayed licensure, and elevated mental health burdens. Enrollment expansion has further strained training capacity and produced crowding-out effects on the broader medical talent pipeline. Implementation-level adjustments can partially alleviate these issues but cannot resolve the core contradiction. Reform should prioritize addressing the dual-identity tension through either flexible decoupling or complete separation of the two pathways, drawing on international experiences.

papers.title: Effect of Alkali Treatment on the Structure, Mechanical Behavior and Damage Response of Areca Leaf Sheath Fiber Reinforced Epoxy Composites
papers.journal: Journal of Macromolecular Science Part B
papers.abstract: Areca leaf sheath fiber (ALSF) was investigated as a sustainable reinforcement for epoxy composites, focusing on the effects of sodium hydroxide (NaOH) treatment on structural, mechanical, and thermomechanical properties. ALSF was treated with 0, 3, 5, 7, and 10% NaOH, and composites were fabricated using 200 mL of epoxy resin through compression molding at 50 bar and room temperature for 24 h. FTIR and XRD were used to examine chemical modifications and crystalline characteristics, respectively. Tensile, flexural, impact, hardness, and dynamic mechanical properties were evaluated to determine the influence of alkali treatment. Among the investigated concentrations, 5% NaOH provided the best overall performance. Tensile strength increased from 18.2 to 26.4 MPa, while flexural strength improved from 31.5 to 42.6 MPa. Impact strength increased from 6.3 to 9.8 kJ/m2, and Shore D hardness rose from 62 to 72. Higher NaOH concentrations reduced performance, suggesting excessive fiber modification and structural degradation. XRD and dynamic mechanical analysis supported treatment-dependent changes in crystallinity and glass-transition behavior. SEM revealed fiber fragmentation, irregular fracture regions, possible fiber pull-out, and matrix cracking. These findings demonstrate that controlled alkali treatment, particularly at 5% NaOH, enhances the mechanical and thermomechanical performance of ALSF/epoxy composites.

papers.title: Cotinus coggygria Scop. extract-loaded polycaprolactone/hyaluronic acid nanofibers as candidate wound dressings: in vitro characterization, cytocompatibility and antibacterial evaluation
papers.abstract: Cotinus coggygria Scop. (Anacardiaceae) possesses antibacterial, antioxidant, anticancer, and wound-healing properties. Hyaluronic acid (HA), a key extracellular matrix component, supports tissue regeneration. In this study, electrospun polycaprolactone (PCL) nanofibers containing C. coggygria extract and HA were developed as wound dressings. Optimized polymer solutions and electrospinning parameters were used according to material composition. Nanofibers were characterized by contact angle measurements, texture analysis, scanning electron microscopy, and in vitro cell culture assays. The fiber diameters ranged from 300 to 700 nm, and contact angle decreased to 65.3°, indicating improved hydrophilicity due to HA and C . coggygria extract incorporation. The addition of extract and HA yielded a maximum tensile strength of 2.40 MPa. After 24 h of exposure, the F5 maintained L929 fibroblast viability above 80% across the entire tested range (0.062–1 mg/mL). At 48 h, F5 produced the lowest apoptotic (6% ± 1%) and necrotic (10% ± 1%) indices among the extract-containing fibers at 1 mg/mL, indicating cytocompatibility towards L929 fibroblasts under the conditions tested. Antibacterial tests revealed inhibition zones of 21 ± 0 mm against Staphylococcus aureus and 6 ± 1 mm against Escherichia coli . Overall, PCL nanofibers incorporating C. coggygria extract and HA demonstrate promising potential for wound healing applications owing to their favorable mechanical properties, high biocompatibility, and notable antibacterial activity.

papers.title: Effect of Isobutane Content on the Properties of PET Foam Sheets Produced With a Biodegradable Polymer Based Chain Extender for Food Tray Applications
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The influence of isobutane loading on the properties of extruded PET foam sheets for food tray applications is investigated. A biodegradable polymer‐based chain extender is used as a sustainable alternative to conventional PET‐based carriers, supporting more sustainable PET foam production. Five formulations with isobutane contents from 0.6 to 1.4 wt% are prepared under constant conditions, and characterization is performed before and after thermal treatment at 250°C for 90 s to simulate thermoforming. The 1.2 wt% formulation delivers maximum thickness (2.31 mm before oven, 3.91 mm after) and minimum density (177.3 kg/m 3 before, 116.9 kg/m 3 after), achieving an 87% density reduction relative to solid PET. This formulation also exhibits the most uniform cellular architecture, with an average cell diameter of 211.1 ± 25.7 μm. The tensile behavior, characterized by reduced strength and modulus alongside increased elongation up to 1.2 wt%, is consistent with the reduced density and increased cell expansion at higher isobutane loadings. At 1.4 wt%, cell coalescence and collapse occur. Thermal analysis shows amorphous character before oven exposure, while post‐treatment X‐ray diffraction indicates crystallization enhancement. The optimal formulation is successfully thermoformed into a tray, demonstrating industrial processability and distinguishing this work from previous laboratory‐scale PET foaming studies. This study highlights isobutane as a key parameter for tailoring PET foam properties and supports PET foam as a nontoxic, recyclable alternative to polystyrene trays.

papers.title: FusionSwinUNETR: A multimodal deep learning model for abdominal mass segmentation in pediatric CT
papers.abstract: Research on computational methods for pediatric solid tumors is constrained by data scarcity, a focus on single tumor types, and the limits of imaging alone. We present FusionSwinUNETR, a multimodal segmentation model that conditions a SwinUNETRv2 backbone on patient metadata and clinician-written findings alongside CT images, and we evaluate it on a multi-center paired dataset of 750 pediatric patients spanning 12 mass types — a considerably broader diagnostic range than previous single-tumor studies. Against an image-only baseline evaluated on the same 60 held-out patients, the fusion model improved every metric: DSC 0.900 ± 0.044 versus 0.882 ± 0.064, precision 0.928 ± 0.051 versus 0.913 ± 0.062, recall 0.880 ± 0.081 versus 0.866 ± 0.110, and HD95 4.79 ± 3.31 versus 8.93 ± 6.22 mm, a 46% reduction in boundary error. Paired within-patient testing with correction for multiple comparisons confirmed these gains: HD95 improved significantly for all three multimodal configurations, and the fusion model was the only configuration whose DSC improvement survived correction (Hodges–Lehmann + 0.012, q = 5.6 × 10⁻ 4 ) and the only one to improve precision and recall concurrently, indicating that metadata and clinical findings contribute complementary rather than redundant information. Incorporating clinical information already available at the time of image interpretation therefore yields more accurate and more reliable segmentation across a wide range of pediatric abdominal masses.

papers.title: Association between the frequency of achieving recommended daily step counts and a decline in quantitative ultrasound measurements in premenopausal and postmenopausal women: a 4-year prospective study of the Tohoku Medical Megabank Community-Based Cohort study
papers.abstract: Achieving 7000 steps/day on ≥3 days/week significantly reduced the risk of decline in quantitative ultrasound measurements in premenopausal women, but not in postmenopausal women. Less frequent achievement (1–2 days/week) showed no significant association in either group. To examine the association between the frequency of achieving the recommended daily step count (7000 steps/day) and the incidence of a decline in quantitative ultrasound (QUS) measurements among pre- and postmenopausal women. In this prospective cohort study of the Tohoku Medical Megabank Community-Based Cohort, baseline and follow-up surveys were conducted between 2013–2016 and 2017–2021 (mean follow-up: 42.5 months). Participants were 3529 women (1013 premenopausal, 2516 postmenopausal). Daily steps were objectively measured using pedometers. The number of days per week achieving 7000 steps was categorized as Inactive (0 days), Low active (1–2 days), and Active (≥3 days). The outcome was the incidence of a decline in QUS measurements, defined as a QUS T-score ≤–2.5 or a self-reported diagnosis of osteoporosis. Adjusted risk ratio (RR) and 95% confidence interval (CI) were calculated using modified Poisson regression models, with the Inactive group as the reference. During follow-up, the outcome occurred in 70 premenopausal and 662 postmenopausal women. In premenopausal women, the Active group had a significantly lower risk of the outcome compared to the Inactive group (RR: 0.478, 95% CI: 0.271 to 0.843). In postmenopausal women, no statistically significant association was observed (RR for the Active group: 0.937, 95% CI: 0.807 to 1.088). The findings suggest that the association appeared to differ by menopausal status, achieving 7000 steps/day on ≥3 days/week was associated with a significantly reduced risk of a decline in QUS measurements in premenopausal women. However, for postmenopausal women, walking alone may be an insufficient strategy.

papers.title: Effect of a Surfactant on Fabrication and Released Property of Nanopesticides Based on a Covalent Organic Framework
papers.abstract: Abstract The triaminoguanidine covalent organic framework (COF) has abundant cationic charges, excellent stability, and strong adsorption capacity, which make it become a potential drug release carrier. In this study, two kinds of COFs, COF1 and COF2, were prepared by reacting triaminoguanidine hydrochloride with 2,5-dihydroxyp-benzaldehyde and 3,3′-dihydroxyl-[1,1′-biphenyl]-4,4′-diformaldehyde, respectively, and then the COF was combined with dinotefuran (DIN)-solubilized surfactant (S) micelles to obtain a series of DIN@S-COF nanopesticides. The effect of S on the structures of S-COF and DIN@S-COF was investigated by XRD, FT-IR, TGA/DTA, contact angle, SEM, and BET methods. The pore diameter of COF2 (2.4 nm) was higher than that of COF1 (1.6 nm). The pore sizes of S-COF1 and DIN@S-COF1 were obviously larger than that of COF1, and those of S-COF2 and DIN@S-COF2 were changed. The effect of S on the release behavior of DIN@S-COF was also investigated and discussed. DIN@DSS (SDS, MADS, AOT)-COF1 and DIN@AOT-COF2 displayed a sustained release behavior. The release behavior was mainly influenced by the pore diameter of the COF, surfactant structure, and the attractive interaction between COF, S, and DIN. The DIN release from the composite could be well fitted by parabolic diffusion and pseudo-second-order models. COFs had the potential application as a new and efficient pesticide delivery system.

papers.title: Cellulose acetate nanoparticles: impacts of concentration and exposure time on the biochemistry and hematology of juvenile Colossoma macropomum
papers.abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the physiological impacts of acute-exposure of tambaqui ( Colossoma macropomum ) to different concentrations of cellulose acetate nanoparticles at different sampling times. A total of 120 juvenile C. macropomum (38.91 ± 5.57 g and 13.76 ± 0.74 cm in total length) were distributed in 12 tanks of 150 L, in a recirculating aquaculture system (RAS). The juveniles were kept in water containing cellulose acetate nanoparticles (CANs) at four different concentrations (treatments): 0 mg L − ¹, 0.01 mg L − ¹, 0.10 mg L − ¹ and 1.00 mg L − ¹. Blood samples were collected after 1 and 24 h of exposure. The juveniles were then relocated to a tank with clean water, where they remained for another 24 h, after which a new blood sample was collected (24 h). Hemoglobin, serum protein and globulin were reduced after 1 h of exposure for the group exposed to 1.00 mg L − ¹ of CANs. Glucose levels increased after 24 h for the groups exposed to 0.10 and 1.00 mg L − ¹. Urea increased after 1 h for the groups exposed to 0.10 and 1.00 mg L − ¹. Triglycerides and cholesterol were reduced both after 1 h and 24 h of exposure for the 1.00 mg L − ¹ group, returning to baseline levels at 24 h. The activities of aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase were altered after 24 h. Albumin was lower after 1 h and 24 h compared to after 24 h for the 1.00 mg L − ¹ group. Exposure of juvenile C. macropomum to CANs caused transient physiological changes, with partial recovery being observed after transfer to clean water.

papers.title: Nanocochleates as Smart Lipidic Nanocarriers for Improved Anticancer Therapy Recent Advances and Future Perspectives
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Cancer therapy is frequently limited by poor aqueous solubility, inadequate bioavailability, rapid degradation, nonspecific distribution, systemic toxicity, and multidrug resistance, creating a need for advanced drug-delivery systems.Nanocochleates have emerged as promising lipidic nanocarriers characterized by compact, tightly packed multilamellar structures formed through interactions between negatively charged phospholipids and divalent cations, particularly calcium ions.Their distinctive architecture provides drug protection, improved retention, and potential for sustained and controlled release.This review discusses the development of nanocochleates as smart nanocarriers for improved anticancer therapy, with emphasis on their fundamental characteristics, composition, formation mechanisms, preparation approaches, and physicochemical characterization.Their potential for delivering conventional anticancer agents and poorly bioavailable natural compounds is discussed, including applications involving doxorubicin, fisetin, paclitaxel, curcumin, quercetin, and resveratrol.Particular attention is given to passive and active tumor targeting, folate-, antibody-, peptide-, and tumor-microenvironment-based strategies, as well as pH-, redox-, enzyme-, and reactive oxygen species-responsive systems.The review further highlights nanocochleateenabled combination therapy, drug/gene co-delivery, immunotherapy integration, and potential approaches for overcoming multidrug resistance.Safety, toxicity, biocompatibility, formulation reproducibility, scale-up, quality control, regulatory requirements, and clinical translation are also considered.Future perspectives include multifunctional and theranostic nanocochleates, artificial intelligence-assisted formulation optimization, Quality by Design, personalized nanomedicine, and scalable manufacturing.Overall, nanocochleates represent a promising platform for precision cancer therapy, although rigorous in vivo validation, standardized manufacturing, long-term safety assessment, and well-designed clinical studies are required to establish their therapeutic and translational value and demonstrate clear advantages over established nanomedicine platforms in efficacy, safety, stability, and patientspecific therapeutic outcomes.

papers.title: Circadian rhythms in health and disease
papers.abstract: Abstract Circadian rhythms, serving as a crucial temporal bridge linking neural activity and pathological biology, are regulated by central pacemaker neurons to maintain cellular homeostasis and coordinate diverse biological processes. Circadian rhythm disruption is closely associated with various diseases, including neurodegenerative disorders, metabolic disorders, and cancer. Circadian rhythms are controlled by core clock genes, such as BMAL1 and CLOCK, modulating numerous physiological processes, encompassing metabolism, immune responses, neural activity, and hormone regulation. Circadian rhythms disruptions arising from shift work, jet lag, or inconsistent sleep schedules are implicated in both the onset and progression of numerous diseases, notably Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease. The article highlights how circadian dysregulation alters cellular processes to potentially accelerate disease progression. Circadian disruption results in impaired immune function, further promoting disease development and resistance to treatment. Potential therapeutic applications based on circadian biology, such as chronotherapy and personalized medicine, are also discussed. Recent technological advances, embodied in wearable devices and omics approaches, are increasingly providing deeper insights into circadian biology. Further unveiling the role of circadian in health and disease opens new avenues for tailoring treatment timing to patients' biological rhythms, thereby enhancing therapeutic outcomes across various diseases. By bridging fundamental circadian mechanisms with clinical pathology, this review provides a roadmap for future chronotherapeutic interventions in precision medicine.

papers.title: Silica–Chitosan Hybrid Gels: Preparation, Solution Chemistry, Optical and Thermal Properties
papers.abstract: Silica–chitosan hybrid gel composites containing up to 3.3 wt% chitosan are prepared by a simple and reproducible sol–gel route based on the acid-catalyzed hydrolysis and condensation of tetraethoxysilane. The resulting materials are characterized by UV–Vis and FTIR spectroscopy, thermogravimetric and differential thermal analysis, scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, and thermal conductivity measurements. Increasing the chitosan content resulted in densification of the silica network from 1.56 to 1.70 g·cm−3. Even at low chitosan concentrations, its incorporation produces measurable changes in the structural, optical, and thermal properties of the sol–gel-derived silica, thus preserving its amorphous nature. The thermal conductivity of the gels decreases from 0.1 W/m·KW/m·K to 0.09 W/m·K with chitosan doping, combined with an increase in optical absorption at 300 nm. A simple empirical method based on UV–Vis reflectance spectroscopy is proposed for determining the chitosan content in silica powders. Optical properties of low-doped silica gels and chitosan solutions are described. Hydrothermal treatment of the chitosan solution improves optical absorption at 285 nm. Overall, the preparation–structure–property relationships of the hybrid gels demonstrate their potential as optical matrices with tunable properties.
papers.summary: Silica–chitosan hybrid gel composites containing up to 3.3 wt% chitosan are prepared by a simple and reproducible sol–gel route based on the acid-catalyzed hydrolysis and condensation of tetraethoxysilane. A simple empirical method based on UV–Vis reflectance spectroscopy is proposed for determining the chitosan content in silica powders. Overall, the preparation–structure–property relationships of the hybrid gels demonstrate their potential as optical matrices with tunable properties.

papers.title: Reprogramming secretion systems in Klebsiella quasipneumoniae: from pathogenic functions to candidate industrial secretion chassis
papers.abstract: Efficient extracellular secretion remains a major bottleneck in microbial cell factories, motivating the search for chassis organisms with native high-throughput transport capacity. Klebsiella quasipneumoniae (Kqp), a recently delineated member of the Klebsiella pneumoniae species complex, encodes diverse secretion-related systems, including RND-type efflux pumps, type II and type VI secretion systems (T2SS/T6SS), outer membrane vesicle (OMV) pathways, and capsular polysaccharide (CPS) export machinery. In clinical settings, these systems contribute to opportunistic pathogenicity, antimicrobial resistance, and host adaptation; in biotechnology, they may provide transport modules that can be detoxified and redirected for extracellular production. This review examines the feasibility of reprogramming Kqp from a pathogen-related bacterium into a safe industrial secretion chassis. We summarize the molecular architecture, substrate-recognition logic, and regulatory networks of major secretion pathways, then discuss CRISPR-Cas-driven removal of virulence and resistance determinants, biocontainment, and synthetic-biology strategies for reallocating secretory capacity. We further survey potential applications in bulk chemicals, human milk oligosaccharides, recombinant proteins, and industrial enzymes. Finally, we identify key barriers to industrial translation, including growth-secretion energetic trade-offs, periplasmic protein misfolding, endotoxin-associated downstream processing, OMV heterogeneity, scale-up robustness, and quantitative safety validation. Establishing Kqp as an industrial chassis will require evidence-tiered strain selection, quantitative secretion-capacity measurement, regulatory decoupling of resistance-associated pumps, and One Health-aligned safety assessment. Direct evidence in K. quasipneumoniae remains limited; therefore, this review distinguishes direct Kqp observations from studies in other KpSC members or K. oxytoca , evidence from non-Klebsiella hosts, and forward-looking proposals. OMV yield is considered separately from lipid A/endotoxin-related properties.
papers.summary: Efficient extracellular secretion remains a major bottleneck in microbial cell factories, motivating the search for chassis organisms with native high-throughput transport capacity. We further survey potential applications in bulk chemicals, human milk oligosaccharides, recombinant proteins, and industrial enzymes. OMV yield is considered separately from lipid A/endotoxin-related properties.

papers.title: Comprehensive characterization of shilajit from varied provenance: elemental profile, urolithin A content, and antimicrobial activity
papers.abstract: Shilajit is an exudate rich in humic substances that collected from rocks in several mountain ranges and has been used for centuries in traditional medicine for fatigue, physical performance, and general vitality. Ten shilajit samples from five mountain regions (Himalayas, Andes, Altai, Caucasus, and Carpathians) were assessed by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), elemental composition by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS), urolithin A (Uro-A) content by liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), and antimicrobial activity by broth microdilution against five bacterial and five fungal species. DSC identified two distinct thermal groups: seven samples showed only melting transitions between 100–159 °C, while three samples exhibited low-temperature crystallization and sub-zero melting. ICP-MS revealed potassium as the dominant macroelement (up to ~95,600 ppm), with essential trace elements (selenium, zinc and iron) and toxic elements [arsenic (0.14–1.34 ppm), cadmium (0.01–0.10 ppm) and lead (0.35–3.01 ppm)] all present at levels well within FDA/WHO tolerable intake thresholds, comparable to background levels reported in common foods such as dark chocolate. Uro-A content was strongly solvent-dependent, ranging from 0.07 to 1.63 ppm in methanol to 3.46–58.46 ppm in a methanol/ethyl acetate mixture. Antimicrobial activity was species-dependent (MIC 3.12–25 mg/mL), limited to Bacillus subtilis and Staphylococcus aureus and only two fungal strains ( Mucor mucedo and Geotrichum candidum ), with no activity against the Escherichia coli and Proteus mirabilis . These findings support shilajit’s compositional diversity and highlight Uro-A as its most promising bioactive component, warranting further standardization and origin-based sourcing studies for future bioavailability studies for the potential use as a functional food ingredient.

papers.title: Case Report: Low-dose donor lymphocyte infusion for secondary poor graft function after haploidentical HSCT in a child with β-thalassemia
papers.abstract: Poor graft function (PGF) is a serious complication after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT), particularly when persistent cytopenia occurs despite complete donor chimerism. We report a 5-year-old girl with transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia major who developed refractory secondary PGF after haploidentical allo-HSCT following cytomegalovirus reactivation. Bone marrow was markedly hypocellular, and and multilineage cytopenias progressively worsened after plasma CMV DNA became undetectable and antiviral therapy was completed. Contributions from infection-related injury, antiviral-associated myelotoxicity, or endothelial injury could not be fully excluded. Multiple supportive and immunomodulatory interventions failed. Because a CD34 + selected stem cell boost was not feasible, the patient received intentionally low-dose donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI) on days +270 and +284. Multilineage hematopoietic recovery occurred 27 days after the first infusion, and transfusion independence was maintained for more than 14 months. Post-DLI events included manageable grade I cutaneous graft-versus-host disease and transient tachypnea of uncertain etiology. Longitudinal immune profiling showed recovery of naive T-cell compartments, contraction of effector-memory subsets, and expansion of CD8 + CD28 - T cells without overt T-cell activation. This observation provides a hypothesis-generating rationale for prospective studies evaluating the efficacy and safety of low-dose DLI in pediatric secondary PGF.

papers.title: Nanosponge-Based Topical Delivery Systems for Psoriasis: Advances, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic, immune-mediated inflammatory skin disorder characterized by abnormal keratinocyte proliferation, epidermal hyperplasia, and persistent inflammation.Although topical therapy remains an important approach for mild-to-moderate psoriasis, conventional formulations are often associated with poor drug solubility, inadequate skin penetration, rapid drug release, limited skin retention, and potential adverse effects.Nanotechnologybased delivery systems have therefore emerged as promising strategies for improving localized and controlled drug delivery.Among these, nanosponges are porous, three-dimensional, cross-linked nanocarriers capable of incorporating active pharmaceutical ingredients and functioning as drug reservoirs.Their unique architecture offers advantages including enhanced solubility, drug protection, controlled release, and improved skin deposition.This review discusses the potential of nanosponge-based topical delivery systems for psoriasis, with emphasis on their pharmaceutical characteristics, types, preparation strategies, drug-loading mechanisms, and physicochemical characterization.Current evidence on nanosponge formulations containing antipsoriatic agents, including clobetasol propionate, curcumin, caffeine, and sulfasalazine, is critically examined with respect to drug release, skin delivery, and preclinical therapeutic outcomes.The incorporation of nanosponges into topical gels and hydrogels is also discussed as an approach to improve residence time, spreadability, and localized drug delivery.Despite encouraging preclinical findings, challenges remain regarding formulation optimization, batch reproducibility, dermal safety, scaleup, regulatory requirements, and clinical validation.Future development may focus on targeted and stimuli-responsive nanosponges, combination therapy, quality-by-design approaches, artificial intelligence-assisted optimization, and scalable manufacturing.Overall, nanosponges represent a promising platform for developing localized, sustained, and patient-friendly topical therapies for psoriasis.

papers.title: Toxic Aromatics Inclusion and Water Vapor Adsorption/Desorption of a 3D Supramolecular Architecture via π–π Assembly of 2D Zn-Based Layered MOFs
papers.abstract: Abstract A three-dimensional (3D) supramolecular architecture, {[Zn(dpds)(bdc)]·MeOH·1.5H2O}n (1) (dpds = 1,2-bis(4-pyridyl)disulfide and bdc2– = dianion of 1,4-benzenedicarboxylic acid), assembled by a two-dimensional (2D) layered metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) via interlayer sandwich-type πpyridyl–πbenzene–πpyridyl and πpyridyl–πpyridyl interactions, is examined using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to reveal their structures and chemical environments. Compound 1 exhibits a significant water vapor adsorption/desorption isotherm for pretreated 1, which displays a maximum value of 215.5 cm3g–1 at a relative pressure P/P0 = 1.00, corresponding to adsorption of approximately four water molecules per asymmetric unit (ASU). In addition, a series of toxic aromatics, namely, benzene (PhH), toluene (PhCH3), anisole (PhOCH3), and nitrobenzene (PhNO2), can be absorbed by 1 in liquid phases to generate new host–guest compounds, {[Zn(bdc)(dpds)]·0.5Ph·1.5H2O}n (1⊃Ph), {[Zn(bdc)(dpds)]·0.5Ph(CH3)·H2O}n (1⊃PhCH3), {[Zn(bdc)(dpds)]·0.5PhOCH3·1.5H2O}n (1⊃PhOCH3), and {[Zn(bdc)(dpds)]·0.5Ph(NO2)·1.5H2O}n (1⊃PhNO2), which have been indetified by IR, X-ray diffraction method, and TG analysis. Structural characteristics and photoluminescent properties associated with theoretical calculation for 1⊃Ph, 1⊃PhCH3, 1⊃PhOCH3, and 1⊃PhNO2 are studied and discussed.

papers.title: Influence of BaTiO 3 Incorporation on the Morphological, Mechanical, Thermal, and Dielectric Properties of ABS-Based Composites
papers.abstract: In this study, Barium Titanate, BaTiO3, (BT) as a functional filler at different loadings (10, 15, and 20 wt. %) was incorporated into Acrylonitrile-Butadiene-Styrene (ABS) matrix. The frequency dependence of conductivity, dissipation factor, and dielectric constant of BT-filled ABS composites was investigated at room temperature. The structural, morphological, thermal, mechanical, and dielectric properties of the composites were characterized. X-ray diffraction (XRD) confirmed the presence of the crystalline BT phase within the amorphous ABS, while scanning electron microscopy (SEM) revealed uniform dispersion at lower loadings and increased agglomeration at higher loadings. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) showed improved thermal stability as BT content increased. Mechanical testing indicated a continuous increase in tensile modulus with filler content, while tensile strength showed an initial decrease followed by recovery at higher loadings. Dielectric analysis revealed a significant enhancement in dielectric constant with increasing BaTiO3 content, particularly at low frequencies. 20 wt% BT-filled ABS-3D composites exhibit the highest AC conductivity, reaching approximately 1.79 × 10−6 S/cm at 107 Hz. However, neat ABS shows the lowest conductivity, peaking at roughly 3.08 × 10−7 S/cm. Overall, the results demonstrate that ABS/BT composites offer a promising balance of processability, mechanical performance, and dielectric functionality, highlighting their potential for dielectric applications requiring enhanced permittivity and processability.

Mechanical testing indicated a continuous increase in tensile modulus with filler content, while tensile strength showed an initial decrease followed by recovery at higher loadings. Overall, the results demonstrate that ABS/BT composites offer a promising balance of processability, mechanical performance, and dielectric functionality, highlighting their potential for dielectric applications requiring enhanced permittivity and processability.

papers.title: A Synergistic Effect of Multifunctional Magnesium Hydroxide@Layered Double Hydroxide Nanohybrid and an Organotin Polymer on the Poly(Vinyl Chloride) Properties
papers.journal: Journal of Vinyl and Additive Technology
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) is widely used for its versatility and cost‐effectiveness, but its inherent thermal instability requires advanced stabilization and flame‐retardant systems. Simultaneously enhancing thermal stability, flame retardancy, and mechanical performance remains challenging, as conventional additives often act through a single mechanism and suffer from poor PVC compatibility and limited synergy. Overcoming this, particularly through uniform dispersion and strong interfacial interaction between the organic and inorganic components, was a main challenge of this work. A hybrid formulation was developed to improve the thermal stability and fire performance of plasticized PVC by combining a pyridine‐based organotin polymer (PSn) with a multifunctional organo‐modified magnesium dihydroxide (MDH)@Zn‐Al layered double hydroxide (MLDH). Scanning electron microscope (SEM) showed improved dispersion with reduced aggregation in hybrid samples, while the absence of the LDH reflections in X‐ray diffraction (XRD) suggested uniform distribution within the PVC matrix. Thermal analysis revealed an enhancement in stability for the PSL5 sample (containing 2.5 wt.% PSn and 2.5 wt.% MLDH), where the onset degradation temperature increased from 165°C for neat PVC to 229°C, along with an increase in char residue from 10% to 21%. Thermal aging results further demonstrated a clear delay in discoloration compared to neat PVC. Flammability performance evaluation indicated that the total heat release (THR) decreased from 16.9 kJ g −1 (PVC) to 11 kJ g −1 (PSL5), while the limiting oxygen index (LOI) value increased from 26.8% to 28.7%, confirming relatively improved flame retardancy. Mechanical properties were also enhanced, with tensile strength increasing from 59.02 MPa (PVC) to 100.41 MPa (PSL5) and modulus from 2.68 to 4.98 GPa, while maintaining acceptable elongation.

papers.title: Environmental Durability and Microstructural Evolution of Industrial-Waste-Modified Pisha Sandstone Cementitious Composites
papers.abstract: The water-induced swelling and disintegration of pisha sandstone (PS) are modified through gel-mediated cementation, thereby providing a technical pathway for the resource utilization of PS. This study investigated the durability of PS geopolymer cementitious materials (PSCM) incorporating four industrial solid wastes, including blast furnace slag (BFS), fly ash (FA), silica fume (SF), and steel slag (SS), under dry–wet cycles, freeze–thaw cycles, and water immersion. X-ray diffraction, thermogravimetric analysis, and scanning electron microscopy were employed to characterize the evolution of the mineral phase composition and gel structure of PSCM. The results show that BFS can effectively improve the durability of PSCM. With 40% BFS, the strength of PSCM reaches 25.82 MPa after 10 dry–wet cycles; the strength loss rate drops to 27% after 10 freeze–thaw cycles; and the softening coefficient reaches 0.89 after 28 d immersion. With 20% BFS, the strength loss of PSCM specimens is only 10.3% and 9.3% after 10 dry–wet and freeze–thaw cycles followed by 7 d immersion. BFS promotes the formation of calcium-rich C-A-S-H gels, enhancing interparticle bonding and matrix integrity, thus enhancing the durability of PSCM. This study provides a theoretical basis for understanding the microstructure evolution and durability differences in PSCM modified by different solid wastes.
papers.summary: The water-induced swelling and disintegration of pisha sandstone (PS) are modified through gel-mediated cementation, thereby providing a technical pathway for the resource utilization of PS. This study investigated the durability of PS geopolymer cementitious materials (PSCM) incorporating four industrial solid wastes, including blast furnace slag (BFS), fly ash (FA), silica fume (SF), and steel slag (SS), under dry–wet cycles, freeze–thaw cycles, and water immersion. The results show that BFS can effectively improve the durability of PSCM.

papers.title: From seed centres to tray cells: a geometry-aware machine vision framework for full-tray sowing quality assessment in maize plug trays
papers.abstract: Accurate sowing-quality assessment of maize seedling trays requires both reliable seed localisation and correct correspondence between detected seeds and physical tray cells. This study presents a semi-automated machine-vision framework combining heatmap-based seed-centre localisation, sliding-window inference, global non-maximum suppression (NMS), and four-corner-calibrated adaptive grid assignment. Each assessable cell was classified as empty, single-seeded, or multi-seeded according to the number of assigned seed centres. On source-image-independent subsets, the framework achieved an accuracy of 0.9821 and a macro F1-score of 0.9040 for 27 complete-tray images (3,456 cells), and 0.9798 and 0.9344, respectively, for 9 visible-cell images (1,140 assessable cells). Separately, the larger evaluation sets yielded accuracy/macro F1 values of 0.9783/0.9145 for 44 complete trays and 0.9782/0.9368 for 30 visible-cell images. These results support cell-level sowing-quality assessment under the evaluated acquisition conditions and within manually assessable regions. The source-image-independent subsets control direct source overlap but remain within the same acquisition domain; external generalisation across production sites, imaging devices, tray specifications, and acquisition conditions has not yet been established.

papers.title: Benzoxazine Functionalization of CO2-Derived Block Copolymers toward High-Performance Thermosets through Cooperative Covalent Crosslinking and Hydrogen Bonding
papers.abstract: Abstract CO2-derived aliphatic polycarbonates have attracted considerable attention as sustainable polymeric materials; however, their relatively low glass transition temperature and limited thermal stability restrict their applications in high-performance engineering materials. Herein, a series of benzoxazine-functionalized CO2-derived block copolymers, poly(cyclohexene carbonate)-b-poly(styrene-alt-1-(3-phenyl-3,4-dihydro-2H-benzoxazin-6-yl)-1H-pyrrole-2,5-dione) (PCHC-b-PSHPMIBZ), were successfully synthesized through sequential ring-opening copolymerization (ROCOP) of cyclohexene oxide and CO2 and reversible addition–fragmentation chain-transfer (RAFT) polymerization. The thermal properties of the resulting block copolymers were systematically tailored by varying the PSHPMIBZ contents followed by thermal ring-opening polymerization (ROP). During thermal curing, the benzoxazine units simultaneously generated a covalently crosslinked network and abundant phenolic hydroxyl groups, which established extensive intermolecular and intramolecular hydrogen-bonding interactions with neighboring carbonate and imide carbonyl groups. The thermal ROP mechanism and structural evolution were comprehensively elucidated using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), in situ Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, two-dimensional (2D) correlation FTIR spectroscopy, and solid-state 13C NMR spectroscopy. These complementary analyses revealed that hydrogen-bonding formation occurred immediately following benzoxazine ring opening, producing a hierarchical dual-network architecture composed of covalent crosslinks and supramolecular hydrogen bonds. Consequently, the glass transition temperature of PCHC-b-PSHPMIBZ51 increased dramatically from 115 to 199 °C, while the char yield increased from 0.9 wt % for the corresponding PCHC-b-PSHPMI51 copolymer to 25.3 wt %, and further to 38.3 wt % after post-curing at 270 °C. The cured block copolymers retained homogeneous morphology despite extensive crosslinking, demonstrating that benzoxazine functionalization provides an effective molecular design strategy for converting sustainable CO2-derived polycarbonate block copolymers into thermosetting materials with substantially elevated glass transition temperatures and enhanced thermal resistance.

papers.title: Risk Analysis of Combustible Cladding in Proximity to Vehicles
papers.abstract: Abstract Building façade fires resulting from the ignition of combustible cladding materials have been reported extensively. However, research specifically addressing the risk posed by external fire sources, such as vehicles parked near cladding, is still limited. This study applies probabilistic analysis to assess fire risks associated with car fires in proximity to combustible cladding, considering Aluminium Composite Panels (ACP) containing a polymer-based core and Expanded Polystyrene (EPS). The influence of wind conditions is incorporated into the analysis. The objective is to create a database supporting decision-making on rectification measures, reducing façade fire risks, and ensuring occupant safety. This study is developed within Cladding Safety Victoria’s framework for mitigating fire risks.

papers.title: Microbial flavoprotein oxidases
papers.abstract: Selective oxidation reactions are critical steps in catalysis towards industrial-relevant compounds. Flavin-dependent enzymes of the VAO/PCMH and GMC families provide numerous candidates that can be applied in various formats and scales. Progresses in catalyst production, mechanistic understanding, structural information, and protein engineering enabled their successful applications. Hence, some candidates are already in use for large-scale chemical syntheses and biosensor applications such as vanillin production, biofuel cells, blood glucose sensing, and glucose monitoring in foods and beverages. The most recent advances related to these oxidases are summarized herein, highlighting recent developments beyond well-known applications that pave the way for novel developments.

papers.title: Low energy availability in recreational high-intensity functional training athletes: associations with health and performance outcomes
papers.abstract: Introduction Low energy availability (LEA) is the primary etiological factor underlying Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (RED-S), yet limited research has examined LEA risk and associated health and performance outcomes in recreational high-intensity functional training (HIFT) athletes. The purpose of this study was to evaluate energy availability (EA) and physiological outcomes aligned with the RED-S Health and Performance Models in a recreational HIFT cohort. Methods Thirty participants (females: n = 18, males: n = 12; 31.2 ± 8.2 years) completed two-week prospective observational study with repeated measures of energy intake, exercise energy expenditure, and associated health and performance-related measures. Energy intake was assessed via dietary logs, exercise energy expenditure was estimated using a wearable armband, and EA was calculated relative to dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry–derived fat-free mass. Participants were classified as LEA if EA was <30 kcal·kg −1 FFM·day −1 . Performance-related outcomes included rating of perceived exertion (RPE), perceived recovery status (PRS), and total quality recovery (TQR). Health-related outcomes included sleep duration, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and bone mineral density (BMD) (reported by Z -Score). Results Mean EA was 24.9 ± 9.7 kcal·kg −1 FFM·day −1 , with 80% ( n = 24) of participants demonstrating EA below the LEA classification threshold. LEA. The high prevalence of LEA should be interpreted cautiously given the potential for underreporting dietary intake. LEA status was not associated with differences in recovery, sleep quality, or BMD ( p > 0.05), and EA was not significantly correlated with performance or health outcomes. In an exploratory analysis, sleep duration was moderately positively associated with TQR ( ρ = 0.46, p = 0.01); however, this finding should be interpreted cautiously given the number of comparisons performed. Discussion Despite the high prevalence of LEA, associated health and performance impairments were not detected, suggesting that measurable consequences of LEA may not be evident over a short observation period in recreational HIFT athletes. These findings support ongoing monitoring of EA, fueling practices, and recovery behaviors to reduce the potential long-term consequences associated with RED-S.

papers.title: TACE-HAIC plus targeted therapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis of TACE- and HAIC-based comparisons
papers.abstract: Background Against the backdrop of targeted therapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), the additional benefit of combining TACE and HAIC remains uncertain in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC). We separately evaluated TACE-based and HAIC-based comparator strategies. Methods CNKI, the Cochrane Library, Embase, PubMed, SinoMed, VIP, Wanfang, and Web of Science were searched from inception to 19 August 2026. Overall survival (OS) was designated as the sole primary efficacy outcome; progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), and complete response (CR) were secondary efficacy outcomes. Comparator-specific random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Risk of bias for survival outcomes was assessed using ROBINS-I, and certainty of evidence across outcomes was evaluated using GRADE. Results In all, 14 retrospective cohort studies were included. The TACE-based and HAIC-based OS analyses included nine and five comparisons involving 1,510 and 572 participants, respectively. Compared with TACE plus targeted therapy and ICIs, TACE-HAIC plus targeted therapy and ICIs was associated with a lower hazard of death (HR = 0.59, 95% CI: 0.47–0.75) and progression or death (HR = 0.65, 95% CI: 0.55–0.78), and with higher ORR (RR = 1.34, 95% CI: 1.19–1.52), DCR (RR = 1.14, 95% CI: 1.07–1.21), and CR (RR = 2.17, 95% CI: 1.46–3.21). Against an HAIC-based comparator, TACE-HAIC was associated with a lower hazard of death (HR = 0.56, 95% CI: 0.43–0.72) and progression or death (HR = 0.64, 95% CI: 0.48–0.86), and with a higher ORR (RR = 1.24, 95% CI: 1.03–1.50), whereas DCR and CR showed no clear between-group differences. Overall grade ≥3 TRAEs were imprecisely estimated in both comparisons (TACE-based: RR = 1.16, 95% CI: 0.81–1.67; HAIC-based: RR = 1.27, 95% CI: 0.92–1.74). Conclusions TACE-HAIC plus targeted therapy and ICIs was associated with improved survival and tumor-response outcomes compared with a TACE-based regimen. Against an HAIC-based regimen, associations favored TACE-HAIC for OS, PFS, and ORR in the main analyses, although the PFS and ORR findings were less robust in sensitivity analyses. Available evidence is insufficient to determine whether TACE-HAIC increases the overall risk of grade ≥3 TRAEs. The certainty of evidence was low to very low, and prospective validation is required. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261286742 , identifier CRD420261286742.

papers.title: Putting PASPT2 on a Firmer Basis
papers.abstract: Abstract The recently proposed partial-active-space (PAS) multistate second-order perturbation theory (PASPT2) [Precision Chemistry 4, 997 (2026)] features connected amplitudes and a connected and closed intermediate Hamiltonian. Despite these hallmarks, PASPT2 (denoted as PASPT2H from now on) is not strictly size-extensive, as originally thought (and numerically confirmed), albeit strictly size-consistent. Nevertheless, PASPT2 is near-extensive for the states with major projections on the chosen PASM0. This becomes more transparent upon introducing PASPT2X, a strictly size-extensive variant. Compared with the intruder-prone PASPT2X, the intruder-free PASPT2H merely neglects second-order corrections that are important only for those states with major projections on the orthogonal complement RX of M0 within the closed space MX ( =M0⊕RX). Such states are usually not supported by the chosen finite one-particle basis set. The weak violation of size-extensivity is therefore numerically insignificant for the target states supported by M0, reinforcing the theoretical basis of PASPT2H.

papers.title: A Self-Healing Adhesive Exploiting Hydrogen-Bonding Interactions and Aromatic Disulfide Units in Energetic Composites
papers.abstract: Energetic composites with high solid content are prone to microcracking and interfacial debonding, which can compromise mechanical integrity and service reliability. To address these long-standing durability challenges, herein, a self-healing polyurethane with hydrogen bonds and disulfide bonds (PUHD) was designed by integrating hydrogen-bond reorganization with dynamic disulfide-bond exchange. PUHD was synthesized using polytetramethylene ether glycol (PTMEG) as the soft segment and isophorone diisocyanate (IPDI) and 4,4′-dihydroxydiphenyl disulfide (DHDPS) as hard-segment components. FT-IR, Raman, XRD, GPC, and DSC analyses confirmed the successful construction of a predominantly amorphous dual dynamic network with suitable chain mobility and thermal stability for energetic-composite applications. The neat PUHD exhibited a hardness of 0.94 MPa and a storage modulus of 3.15 MPa at 20 °C and 5 Hz; surface cracks disappeared within 24 h at ambient temperature, and the storage-modulus recovery reached approximately 97%. In sample filler-containing composites, increasing solid content enhanced hardness and modulus but restricted polymer-chain mobility, thereby slowing crack repair and reducing healing recovery. In nitrocellulose/nitroglycerin (NC/NG)-containing composites, the visible crack closure could be achieved within 24 h, while maintaining useful mechanical properties after self-healing. Notably, JQ-e showed the highest initial hardness of 2.69 MPa and retained 2.19 MPa after healing. These findings collectively demonstrate that the synergistic dynamic network not only enables efficient room-temperature crack repair but also preserves adequate mechanical reinforcement, thus offering a viable pathway toward more reliable energetic-composite formulations.

papers.title: A Right to Delegate to AI: The Regulatory Safety Halo and the Acceleration of Agentic Consumer Markets
papers.abstract: Abstract The European Law Institute’s Guiding Principles and Model Rules on Digital Assistants for Consumer Contracts (DACC) propose a right for consumers to use digital assistants in business-to-consumer relations. The DACC’s definition encompasses consumer AI agents (CAIAs), which use AI-generated outputs to determine transactionally relevant matters left open by consumers and initiate or perform transactional actions. The article examines two concerns. First, recognition and safeguards may create a regulatory safety halo, causing consumers to overestimate CAIAs’ technical reliability and the effectiveness of remedies for unwanted outcomes. Second, recognition may accelerate agentic markets, disproportionately benefit incumbents in adjacent digital markets, and foster concentration, to which the DMA and EU competition law provide only partial responses. Legislation should therefore first establish essential rules governing delegation, responsibility and market contestability. Technical implementation may be entrusted to European standardisation bodies, but the Commission’s request should define tasks precisely and maximise transparency and balanced stakeholder participation to mitigate legitimacy concerns. Only once CAIAs are sufficiently reliable and the legal framework more mature should the right to use a CAIA be recognised.

papers.title: Chitosan–Silica Composites: Effect of Polymer Loading and Immobilization Strategy on Surface Structure and Ni(II)/Co(II) Adsorption
papers.abstract: In this work, the effects of chitosan loading and immobilization strategy on the structure and Ni(II) and Co(II) adsorption properties of chitosan–silica composites were studied. To examine the effect of polymer loading, CS/SiO2 composites containing 5–20 wt.% chitosan were prepared by pH-induced precipitation of chitosan onto pristine SiO2. The effect of the immobilization strategy was investigated using an alternative approach involving preliminary functionalization of SiO2 with APTES followed by chitosan deposition. The obtained materials were characterized by TGA, elemental analysis, FTIR spectroscopy, nitrogen adsorption–desorption analysis, SEM, and XPS. Direct precipitation of chitosan onto SiO2 resulted in the formation of smaller polymer-containing domains on the silica surface compared with the large agglomerates of pristine chitosan, while regions retaining the characteristic morphology of the silica support remained visible. Chitosan modification improved metal-ion adsorption already at a loading of 5 wt.%. Further increasing the chitosan content to 20 wt.% produced a comparatively smaller additional effect. Preliminary APTES functionalization promoted a more uniform surface morphology of CS/SiO2–APTES compared with directly prepared CS/SiO2. These morphological differences were accompanied by differences in the spectral response of the composites following metal adsorption. CS/SiO2–APTES exhibited smaller shifts in the main N 1s XPS component and almost no change in the silanol-related FTIR band, in contrast to the more pronounced changes observed for CS/SiO2. The directly prepared composite also exhibited faster initial metal uptake. Nevertheless, both composites showed relatively similar equilibrium metal uptake values. These findings highlight the importance of considering polymer organization and surface chemistry when designing supported polymer composites for adsorption and other potential applications.

papers.title: Development of a magnetite functionalized cow horn pumice biocomposite for hexavalent chromium removal
papers.abstract: Abstract A magnetite-functionalized cow horn/pumice (Fe 3 O 4 –CH/P) biocomposite was synthesized via in situ co-precipitation and evaluated for the removal of hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)) from aqueous solutions. A multifunctional adsorbent was engineered by integrating keratin-rich cow horn with highly porous pumice and incorporating magnetite, thereby enhancing its physicochemical properties and enabling efficient magnetic separation. To fully characterize the magnetite-functionalized biocomposite, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) were all employed. At optimized adsorption conditions (pH 3, contact time 120 min, 2 g per100 mL solution (20 g·L − 1 ) dosage), batch adsorption tests showed a very high removal efficiency (> 99.8%). This demonstrates the material’s high affinity for oxyanion species of Cr(VI). The adsorption data are well predicted by the pseudo-second-order kinetic model (R 2 = 0.99926), indicating that surface-mediated interactions are crucial to the adsorption process. It was determined through isotherm analysis that the Langmuir model provided a better fit (R 2 = 0.9994, a maximum capacity of 15.34 mg·g − 1 ), indicating that homogeneous active sites with a maximum capacity of 15.34 mg·g − 1 and monolayer adsorption are the dominant mechanism. The adsorption process is regulated by electrostatic attraction, surface complexation, and potential redox interactions. According to the results, the magnetite-functionalized cow horn/pumice (Fe 3 O 4 –CH/P) bio-composite is environmentally friendly and a highly effective adsorbent for treating water contaminated with chromium.

papers.title: Thermal Phase Behavior, Structure, Acidity, and Quantum Chemical Insights into Novel Hydroxylamine Hydrochloride (HACl)-Methanesulfonic Acid (MSA) Deep Eutectic Solvents
papers.abstract: Abstract The present study undertakes the first characterization of hydroxylamine hydrochloride (HACl)-methanesulfonic acid (MSA) deep eutectic solvents (DESs), a new generation of sustainable, dual-functional solvents with exceptionally strong acidic and inherently reduced properties. Employing FTIR, Raman, and NMR spectroscopy, the nature of HACl-MSA DESs’ molecular interactions was probed with varying molar ratios between 1:4 and 1:8. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) revealed composition-dependent phase behavior, transitioning from an amorphous glass-forming liquid at 1:4 (Tg = −89 °C, peak at 85.87 °C) to congruent melting at 1:5 (Tm = +5.43 °C). For 1:6 to 1:8 formulations, invariant eutectic behavior was observed with a shared solidus transition at about −53.80 °C and a clear melting range ending between −45.91 and −39.21 °C. Spectroscopic analyses confirmed the formation of a homogeneous, single-phase protic DES characterized by a robust, shielded hydroxylammonium core ([NH3OH]+) at 9.87–9.88 ppm and a dynamic acid proton pool that shifts downfield from 13.19 to 13.63 ppm. This shifting resonance directly reflects a tunable macroscopic acidity driven by the expansion of the MSA-MSA hydrogen-bonded network. Quantitative Hammett measurements (H0), determined via UV–vis spectroscopy, demonstrated significant acidity, reaching −6.116 at the 1:8 ratio. Density functional theory (DFT) analysis also confirmed the results, revealing a greater internal thermodynamic stability for the 1:5 ratio with a |ΔEint| = 4.280 eV. However, conceptual DFT descriptors, including a smaller energy gap (7.324 eV), a larger global softness value of 0.137 eV–1, and a more negative chemical potential (−4.506 eV), highlight the 1:4 ratio as a promising theoretical candidate for further evaluation in metal coordination processes. While these electronic metrics suggest a highly polarizable microenvironment, direct extraction yields, leaching kinetics, viscosity, and selectivity require future experimental validation. Through correlations established between molecular structure, frontier orbital analysis, and macroscopic Brønsted acidity trends, HACl–MSA DESs are highlighted as promising candidate platforms for potential application in hydrometallurgical leaching processes. However, definitive claims regarding selective metal extraction, long-term stability, recyclability, and environmental sustainability require comprehensive future experimental evaluation.

Density functional theory (DFT) analysis also confirmed the results, revealing a greater internal thermodynamic stability for the 1:5 ratio with a |ΔEint| = 4.280 eV. However, definitive claims regarding selective metal extraction, long-term stability, recyclability, and environmental sustainability require comprehensive future experimental evaluation.

papers.title: Characterization of PLA–hemp biocomposites produced by hot-pressing
papers.journal: Turkish Journal of Forestry | Türkiye Ormancılık Dergisi
papers.abstract: This study investigates the thermal, chemical, physical, morphological, and mechanical properties of hot-pressed PLA-hemp biocomposites produced without compatibilizers. Hemp particles below 75 µm were composed of PLA at 3%, 6%, and 9 wt%, and neat PLA was evaluated in both granular and extruded forms. The composition was compounded using a twin-screw extruder and converted into plates by hot pressing. TGA showed that extrusion slightly improved the thermal stability of neat PLA, whereas hemp addition reduced degradation temperatures. DSC results demonstrated that hemp fibers increased earlier crystallization and the crystallinity of the PLA matrix. FTIR spectra showed that the interaction between PLA and hemp was mainly physical but there is no evidence of new chemical bond formation. Water absorption and thickness swelling increased with hemp content, reaching the highest values in PLA-H9. Surface roughness was significantly affected by sample type, while tensile and flexural strengths decreased after hemp incorporation. SEM images depicted fiber pull-out, interfacial debonding, and micro voids, confirming limited matrix–fiber adhesion. Overall, hemp addition improved bio-based content but reduced strength without compatibilization.

papers.title: Ultrasound-assisted micro-solid-phase extraction using a MIL-53(Al)/Diaion SP-850 composite for trace determination of erythrosine in food and environmental samples
papers.journal: International Journal of Environmental & Analytical Chemistry
papers.abstract: In this work, a dispersive microsolid phase extraction and determination of erythrosine from water, food and environmental samples was performed. A MIL-53(Al)/Diaion SP-850 composite was prepared and characterised by Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET). Micro-solid phase extraction parameters, such as pH, adsorbent amount, adsorption and desorption duration, sonication time, sample volume, eluent type and volume were investigated before the application of the method to real samples. Buffer pH 3.0 phosphate, 10 mg of adsorbent, 60 seconds for adsorption, 3 min for desorption, sample volume of 40 mL and 1 mL absolute ethanol were the optimum conditions resulted from this investigation. Along with the optimisation of the technique, the environmentally friendliness and environment sustainability of the method, namely, Analytical GREEnness Metric Approach (AGREE) and Analytical Greenness Metric for Sample Preparation (AGREEprep) and the Bluenness evaluation (BAGI) were evaluated demonstrating 0.68, 0.75, and 60.0 respective scores. Combining with UV–vis spectrophotometer, the developed ultrasonic-assisted dispersive micro-solid phase extraction method exhibited a linear range of 2.4–3000 µg L−1, low detection limit of 0.80 µg L−1 and a preconcentration factor (40). The method was applied for preconcentration and separation of erythrosine in food and environmental samples presented extraction recovery values ranging 91–102% with relative standard deviation of 4.2%.
