papers.title: Highly Tunable Thermal Properties of Multifunctional Thiol‐Ene Networks Derived From Sugar‐Based Monomers
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Multifunctional sugar monomers offer a variety of structural scaffolds for the formation of thiol‐ene networks. Eleven allylated sugars, each having a nominal number of functionalities ranging from 4 to 11, were combined with seven dithiols that were structurally different to produce 77 thiol‐ene networks. Network formation was assessed by ATR‐FTIR, gel‐fraction, and swelling measurements, whereas the thermal and dynamic mechanical analyses indicated that the glass‐transition temperatures T g were in the range from −45°C to 53°C, the midpoint degradation temperatures were between 277°C and 378°C, and the rubbery storage moduli at 100°C were between 3 and 155 MPa. The sugar scaffolds with higher‐functionality generally increased the ranges of the rubbery modulus, the DMA‐derived apparent elastic‐strand density, T g , and relaxation breadth, although the extent of these effects depended strongly on the structure of the dithiol. Analysis based on composition demonstrated that the T g ‐ v c ,app relationship differed in the various dithiol series rather than following a general high‐density plateau. Examination of E ′, E ″, and tan delta showed that there were composition‐dependent differences in relaxation breadth. The sugar and the dithiol structure provide complementary structural parameters for adjusting the thermal and thermomechanical response of multifunctional sugar‐derived thiol‐ene networks.

papers.title: Preparation and evaluation of chitosan-pectin hydrogel films incorporated with Aloe vera-mediated ZnO (AV-ZnO) for diabetic wound healing
papers.abstract: Abstract: Background: Diabetic wounds are challenging due to delayed healing, inflammation, oxidative stress and bacterial infections, which conventional dressings often inadequately address. Objectives: To develop and characterize Aloe vera-mediated ZnO-loaded chitosan-pectin composite hydrogel films and evaluate their physicochemical, antibacterial, antioxidant, and in-vivo wound-healing efficacy in streptozotocin-induced diabetic male Wistar rat. Methods: AV-ZnO was synthesized using Aloe vera gel extract and incorporated into CS/PT hydrogels via solution casting to formulate three groups: PC (without AV-ZnO), PCG-1 (10 mg AV-ZnO), and PCG-2 (20 mg AV-ZnO). Physicochemical characterization included FTIR, SEM, AFM, TGA, gel fraction, contact angle, and tensile testing. Antibacterial activity was assessed against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli via disk diffusion, and antioxidant activity via DPPH radical-scavenging assay. In-vivo wound-healing efficacy was evaluated in streptozotocin-induced diabetic male Wistar rats (N = 24, n = 6/group) across four groups: untreated control, gentamicin-treated control, topical PCG-2, and exploratory oral PCG-2 hydrogel. Results: AV-ZnO incorporation improved tensile strength (10.1 MPa for PCG-2), hydrophilicity, gel fraction, and thermal stability. PCG-2 exhibited the strongest antibacterial activity, with inhibition zones of 28 mm against S. aureus and 20 mm against E. coli, attributed to AV-ZnO (Zn²⁺ release kinetics not evaluated). Antioxidant activity rose concentration-dependently, with PCG-2 showing 60.33% radical scavenging at 0.6 mg/mL. In-vivo, topical PCG-2 showed the highest wound contraction (89.09% ± 0.61 %, p < 0.05 vs. control) by day 15, surpassing exploratory oral treatment (72.84% ± 0.65%) and gentamicin (topical treated group) (83.77% ± 0.25%). Histology indicate improved re-epithelialization and collagen organization with topical treatment versus controls.

papers.title: Bio‐Based Citric Acid‐Cured Epoxy Shape Memory Composites: Effect of Mineral Fillers on Thermal and Shape Memory Performance
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of sustainable thermosetting polymers with thermo‐responsive shape memory capability has attracted increasing attention due to their potential applications in smart materials and advanced engineering systems. In this study, bio‐based citric acid was employed as an alternative curing agent for epoxy resin to fabricate thermo‐responsive shape memory epoxy composites. The thermal properties, as well as shape memory behavior of the composites were investigated by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) analysis and bending tests, respectively. The effects of polyethylene glycol (PEG) as a plasticizing agent in addition to sepiolite and colemanite as mineral reinforcing fillers on the thermal and shape memory properties of the epoxy composites were systematically investigated. The incorporation of PEG improved the chain mobility of the epoxy network, enabling decreased T g and enhanced shape recovery behavior. The optimized composites exhibited excellent thermo‐responsive shape memory performance, achieving high shape recovery ratios with rapid recovery response under thermal stimulation. The obtained results demonstrate that citric acid‐cured epoxy composites reinforced with natural mineral fillers provide a promising sustainable platform for the development of high‐performance shape memory materials.

papers.title: Multiphysics Modeling of Thermo-viscoelastic Damage in Functionally Graded Abradable Coatings with Probabilistic Geometric Tolerance Analysis
papers.abstract: Abstract In aircraft engines, functionally graded abradable coatings are used to control blade-tip clearance, but their durability is governed by effects that are often treated separately in existing models, including temperature-dependent viscoelastic softening, progressive damage, deposition-induced microstructural modulation, and geometric tolerances. Models that consider these effects independently may underestimate damage initiation because smooth material gradients evaluated at nominal geometry cannot capture the local stress concentrations produced by microstructural modulation and geometric variability. This study integrates these effects within a unified multiphysics–probabilistic framework. The solved domain is a local through-thickness coating column driven by prescribed strain and temperature histories that include thermal eigenstrain and coating–substrate expansion mismatch. The results show that periodic property modulation increases end-of-cycle damage relative to the monotonic gradient and concentrates the maximum stress within a localized modulation crest. Propagating symmetric geometric tolerances through the coupled solver produces a strongly right-skewed damage distribution and a higher classification-level exceedance probability for the modulated gradient than for the monotonic gradient. This exceedance behavior cannot be obtained from a deterministic analysis performed at nominal geometry. The exceedance probability is also evaluated as a continuous function of the classification level to assess the sensitivity of the comparison to the selected screening criterion. The implementation is verified through spatial and temporal refinement, closed-form unit tests, nested Monte Carlo convergence with Wilson confidence intervals, and a hold-out-validated polynomial response surface. Numerical verification is clearly distinguished from experimental validation, and the simulated case is presented as a generic benchmark rather than an identified material model. The framework links deposition parameters and tolerance bands to damage-exceedance risk, supporting reliability-oriented screening of graded and multilayer coating systems.

papers.title: Best Response Dynamics for Zero-Sum Dynamic Games with Partial-Asymmetric Information
papers.journal: Journal of Guidance Control and Dynamics
papers.abstract: This work studies a class of zero-sum stochastic linear quadratic dynamic games (LQDGs) under partial and asymmetric information. Information asymmetry introduces fundamental challenges related to belief representation and theory of mind, where players must impute belief states and estimates of other players to inform their strategies. Existing work highlights the difficulty of applying a dynamic programming-like decomposition approach to these problems. An alternative approach based on best response dynamics is proposed, which provides insights into belief representation and theory of mind challenges. Explicit expressions for each player’s best response within the class of pure linear dynamic output feedback control strategies are derived, where the internal state dimension of each control is an integer multiple of the system state dimension. As players iteratively update their best responses, they form increasingly higher-order belief states, leading to infinite-dimensional internal states. However, numerical results reveal that the game’s value converges after only a few iterations, suggesting that higher-order belief states provide vanishing benefit. This work further conducts numerical experiments to analyze the impact of asymmetric beliefs, belief orders, relative controllability and observability, and direct feed-through on a linear quadratic pursuit–evasion game’s value.
papers.summary: This work studies a class of zero-sum stochastic linear quadratic dynamic games (LQDGs) under partial and asymmetric information. papers.title: Integrative approach reveals hidden diversity in the Brachionus (Rotifera, Monogononta)
papers.abstract: The phylum Rotifera has many species complexes that require integrative analyses to resolve their taxonomic identity. Brachionus angularis comprises different morphotypes. In Aguascalientes, Mexico, we observed two of these morphotypes coexisting. To explore their species identity, we applied an integrative approach that combined taxonomical, ecological, and molecular data. Our results demonstrate taxonomic differentiation in the lengths of females, males, and diapausing eggs between the two morphotypes. We also observed distinct hatching patterns and clearly different ornamentation in diapausing eggs between the two morphotypes. Genetic variation between one monoclonal culture of each morphotype revealed distances of 18.8% for mitochondrial COI and 13.73% for nuclear ITS1 regions. These marked, concordant divergences in mitochondrial and nuclear markers across the closely related Brachionus species, together with diagnostic morphological and ecological differences, support the recognition of the two morphotypes as distinct species. Accordingly, we describe Brachionus agsensis sp. nov. and Brachionus hydrocalidensis sp. nov. as new species.

papers.title: Properties of Cellulose Nanocrystals Extracted Using Deep Eutectic Solvents
papers.abstract: Abstract Cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) are biosourced colloidal building blocks that have attracted significant scientific attention due to their unique properties, such as high mechanical strength, biodegradability, nontoxicity, and potential for sustainable material development. Acidic hydrolysis utilizing strong acids, mainly sulfuric acid, remains the predominant method for CNC production on both laboratory and commercial scales. However, this approach involves challenges associated with the use of corrosive reagents, acid neutralization, and extensive purification. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have been proposed as alternative processing media for CNC extraction, with potential advantages including reduced reliance on concentrated mineral acids and opportunities for solvent recovery and recycling. Here, we report a detailed characterization of DES-extracted CNCs and their characteristics and properties contrasted with those of commercial acid-extracted CNCs. The DES-CNCs were dispersible but with lower ζ-potential and typically longer lengths, forming colloidal gels down to low concentrations that prevent the formation of liquid crystalline phases at higher concentrations, while ultrasound application and increased ionic strength were also found to promote aggregation. The mechanical response of these eutectic-extracted CNCs is followed by linear and nonlinear rheometry at different concentrations and is compared to that of commercial sulfuric acid-extracted CNCs.

papers.title: Transforming Pediatric Thoracotomy: The Critical Role of Thoracic Paravertebral Block in Cyanotic Congenital Heart Disease
papers.journal: Solo Journal of Anesthesi Pain & Critical Care (SOJA)
papers.abstract: Background: Cyanotic Congenital Heart Disease (CCHD) encompasses a range of cardiac anomalies that result in low oxygen levels in the blood. This case report explores the use of Thoracic Paravertebral Block (TPVB) as an effective anesthetic technique in a pediatric patient with multiple congenital heart defects. Case Illustration : We report the case of a 46-day-old male pediatric patient diagnosed with CCHD, including pulmonary atresia and Transposition of the Great Arteries (TGA) with Ventricular Septal Defect (VSD) and Atrial Septal Defect (ASD). The patient had previously undergone a right Blalock-Taussig (R-BT) shunt and PDA stenting, during which he experienced cardiac arrest but achieved return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). He was admitted for another operation, thoracotomy and decortication due to trapped pleural effusion and empyema. The intraoperative management included the use of TPVB, which provided effective analgesia and hemodynamic stability throughout the procedure. Discussion: TPVB has been increasingly recognized as a valuable regional anesthetic technique in pediatric cardiac surgery. Its use can mitigate the hemodynamic fluctuations often seen with general anesthesia alone, especially in patients with compromised cardiovascular status. In this case, TPVB facilitated stable anesthesia, reduced the requirement for systemic opioids, and helped manage recurrent episodes of desaturation and bradycardia. Conclusion: TPVB is a viable anesthetic option in pediatric patients with CCHD undergoing thoracic surgery. It offers substantial benefits in terms of hemodynamic stability and pain management, contributing to improved perioperative outcomes in this high-risk population

papers.title: Release factor 3 degradation enhances aminoglycoside-mediated translational readthrough at MECP2 nonsense mutations
papers.abstract: Abstract Premature termination codons (PTCs) in the MECP2 gene are a major cause of Rett syndrome, resulting in truncated proteins and loss of function. Pharmacological induction of translational readthrough (TR) can restore full-length protein, but clinical translation is hindered by the limited efficiency and toxicity of current inducers. Here, we investigated whether targeted degradation of the eukaryotic Release Factor 3a by the small molecules CC-885 or CC-90009 enhances TR at MECP2 PTCs in HeLa cells. Using a dual-fluorescence reporter assay, we found that neither degrader alone significantly increased TR efficiency. However, cotreatment with the TR inducer G418 produced a synergistic effect, resulting in increased TR compared to G418 alone. Although gentamicin, a less toxic TR inducer, led to only weak TR induction on its own, combination with CC-885 resulted in TR levels similar to G418. Combined CC-885 and G418 treatment enabled recovery of full-length MeCP2 protein as well as proper nuclear localization, consistent with functional recovery of the nuclear localization signal. These findings establish eRF3a degradation as a potential strategy to enhance TR and suggest that the combination of aminoglycosides with release factor degraders could provide a less toxic yet effective therapeutic option for PTC-associated disorders.

papers.title: Green synthesis of lanthanum oxide nanoparticles using Stachytarpheta jamaicensis leaf extract for solar driven organic dye degradation and biological applications
papers.abstract: Metal oxide nanoparticles with superior physicochemical properties for environmental and medical applications have been developed due to recent breakthroughs in nanoscience. As part of the study, lanthanum oxide (La 2 O 3 ) nanoparticles were fabricated through the use of a green method, in which leaf extract of Stachytarpheta jamaicensis (L.) Vahl was employed as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent, thus offering a green option instead of traditional chemical methods. The resulting nanoparticles were thoroughly analysed by XRD, SEM, FTIR, UV-Visible spectroscopy, DLS/zeta potential and TG/DTA tests to verify phase purity, morphology, elemental composition, functional groups, particle size distribution, and optical properties. PXRD showed the presence of a crystalline structure with an average crystallite size of 38.52 nm. UV-visible spectroscopy absorption bands at 216 and 233 nm accompanied by an absorption edge at 335 nm revealed a semiconducting optical bandgap of around 2.9 eV. La 2 O 3 nanoparticles (0.5 mg/mL) under solar light exhibit degradation of methylene blue and Congo red at about 94.8% and 93.1%, respectively, with pseudo-first- order rate constants of 0.01134 min − 1 for MB and 0.02046 min − 1 for CR. Hydroxyl (·OH) and superoxide (O₂· − ) radical species were found to be the major reason for the degradation based on trapping experiments. Besides that, La 2 O 3 nanoparticles were shown to have a strong antimicrobial effect on Escherichia coli , Pseudomonas aeruginosa , Bacillus subtilis , and Staphylococcus aureus . This work indicates that green-synthesized La 2 O 3 nanoparticles have a good prospect of being used for wastewater treatment, Environmental degradation and other related applications in a Biomedical and environmentally friendly way.

papers.title: Exploring supervised and unsupervised methods for brain tumor segmentation in MRI images
papers.abstract: Accurate brain tumor segmentation from MRI images is crucial for diagnosis, treatment planning, and prognosis. In this study, we compare two fundamentally different approaches to tumor segmentation: a supervised deep learning model (2D U-Net) and an unsupervised clustering algorithm (K-means). We evaluate multiple variants of the 2D U-Net trained on different (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) MRI sequences (FLAIR and T1-Gd), as well as a fine-tuned model adapted across modalities, and compare them with K-means clustering applied separately on both modalities.

papers.title: Numerical Analysis Applications in Improving Engineering Models
papers.journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
papers.abstract: Numerical analysis serves as the fundamental pillar of modern engineering modeling, providing the mathematical and computational tools necessary to transform complex physical equations into practical numerical solutions. This study reviews contemporary applications of numerical analysis in enhancing engineering models, focusing on methodological advancements in solving partial differential equations, data-driven model order reduction techniques, adaptive mesh methods, and machine learning-based surrogate models. The study employs a synthetic analytical approach that combines a review of recent literature with an analysis of empirical results from various numerical methods, addressing hybrid models that integrate traditional techniques with artificial intelligence. The analysis demonstrates that combining traditional numerical analysis methods with artificial intelligence and reduced-order models has revolutionized the ability of engineers to simulate complex multiphysics systems with unprecedented accuracy and computational efficiency; hybrid models have achieved computational speedups ranging from 72 to 522 times compare to traditional methods. Furthermore, the study addresses challenges related to computational cost and solution sensitivity to initial conditions, examining cutting-edge innovative solutions such as physicsinformed neural networks and causality-based learning. The study concludes that future trends in this field are shifting towards the development of hybrid models that combine analytical accuracy with computational speed, with an increasing emphasis on generalization capabilities beyond the training data. This opens up broad prospects for digital engineering and digital twin applications across the industrial, energy, and infrastructure sectors. The study offers a comprehensive perspective on the development of engineering models using advanced numerical analysis techniques and identifies promising future research directions in this vital field.

papers.title: Emerging Roles of Gold Nanoparticles in Lung Cancer Diagnosis and Imaging: A Promising yet Underexplored Frontier
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Cancer is known to be a major cause of death worldwide, with lung cancer responsible for the maximum number of deaths. There is an urgent need for early and effective diagnosis of lung cancer to improve the overall survival rate, which is extremely low to date. Studies have shown that 57% of lung cancers are detected only after metastasis of the tumor. Economic restraints in hospitals are resulting in decreased early diagnosis of lung cancer and an increase in aggressive, incurable grades. Traditional imaging modalities like ultrasound, x‐ray, CT, and MRI scans are often unable to precisely locate the extent of metastasis of lung cancer, paving the way for better, more sophisticated diagnostic tools. Nuclear medicine techniques help in better understanding of the metabolic extent of cancer cells using radioactive isotopes. PET/SPECT scans help provide more precise grading and better understanding of tumor morphology. However, the lack of distinction between inflammatory and malignant lesions remains a diagnostic challenge. Gold nanoparticles (GNPs) have been studied as effective contrast agents, enhancing the diagnostic efficiency of lung cancer. Formulation and tagging of GNPs have improved efficacy and biodistribution of cancer drugs; however, no such gold nanoformulation is available for diagnosis to date. The use of different shapes of GNPs functionalized with specific lung cancer biomarkers can potentially increase the specificity of lung tumor diagnosis. In this review, we address the lacunae and provide a strategic roadmap for the effective development of GNP‐based diagnostics, from benchtop to high‐fidelity biomaterials with clinical applications for efficient lung cancer management.

In this review, we address the lacunae and provide a strategic roadmap for the effective development of GNP‐based diagnostics, from benchtop to high‐fidelity biomaterials with clinical applications for efficient lung cancer management.

papers.title: Research and Development Process, Regulatory Requirements and Clinical Trial of Medical Devices: A Review within the Framework of the Turkish Medicines and Medical Devices Agency (TITCK) and the European Union (Regulation 2017/745)
papers.abstract: Medical devices encompass a wide range, from simple instruments to complex implants and software, and recent technological advancements have significantly increased both their number and clinical significance. Bringing a medical device from concept to clinical use requires an integrated pathway combining structured research and development, risk management, regulatory compliance, and robust clinical evidence. In the European Union, Regulation 2017/745 (Medical Devices Regulation) superseded previous directives and strengthened the requirements for clinical evaluation, technical certification, post-market surveillance, and traceability. Türkiye has aligned its national framework with this regulation through the Medical Devices Regulation published by the Turkish Medicines and Medical Devices Agency (TITCK). This review addresses the medical device lifecycle from a regulatory and scientific perspective, covering device definition and risk-based classification, the design and development process and the supporting quality and risk management standards, preclinical laboratory and biological evaluation, in vivo studies, and clinical evaluation and clinical research requirements. Particular attention is paid to the alignment between Good Clinical Practices (ISO 14155) and post-market obligations for device research within the Turkish (TITCK) and European (Regulation No. 2017/745) frameworks. Understanding this integrated pathway in the early stages of development is crucial for the efficient, compliant, and patient-centered transfer of medical devices to clinical practice.

papers.title: Hetero-grafting affects sugar and flavonoid accumulation in ‘Misty’ blueberry (Vaccinium corymbosum)
papers.abstract: Introduction Grafting can be used in blueberry cultivation to improve soil adaptability and scion fruit quality. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Methods We investigated the effects of rabbiteye blueberry ( Vaccinium virgatum ) ‘Climax’ and ‘Brightwell’ rootstocks on fruit quality, biochemical characteristics, and related gene expression in ‘Misty’ blueberry ( Vaccinium corymbosum ). Results The fruit quality of ‘Climax’-grafted ‘Misty’ (CM) was superior to that of ‘Brightwell’-grafted ‘Misty’ (BM). CM showed greater scion stem diameter and fruit size, as well as the net photosynthetic rate, and chlorophyll contents in leaves. Notably, LC-MS/MS analysis detected significant increases in specific sugars and flavonoids in CM fruit, with glucose and fructose contents 10.2% and 11.4% higher than BM, respectively. Twenty-four out of the 31 quantified flavonoids were more abundant in CM. In contrast, 26 of the 28 detected amino acids accumulated at higher levels in BM, as did most organic acids. A total of 1,411 differentially expressed genes, including 830 upregulated and 581 downregulated genes, were detected between CM and BM fruit, in which the genes associated with sugar ( VcSWEET12 and VcINV1 ) and flavonoids ( VcF3′H and VcUFGT ) were upregulated in CM fruit. An integrated analysis pinpointed nine transcription factors, including VcWRKY75 and VcWRKY24 , as potential modulators of sugar metabolism and flavonoid biosynthesis. Discussion These findings indicate that different rabbiteye blueberry rootstocks are associated with distinct physiological and metabolic responses in southern highbush blueberry. Compared with ‘Brightwell’, the ‘Climax’ rootstock was more conducive to improving the comprehensive quality of ‘Misty’ blueberry fruit. The results provide candidate molecular targets for dissecting the process of fruit quality formation mediated by rootstock–scion interactions, and they form a basis for high-quality blueberry cultivation.

papers.title: Advances in myopia progression control – from atropine to personalised treatment
papers.abstract: Krótkowzroczność stanowi jedno z największych wyzwań współczesnej okulistyki, a głównym celem jej leczenia jest obecnie nie tylko korekcja wady refrakcji, lecz przede wszystkim zahamowanie progresji i ograniczenie ryzyka rozwoju wysokiej krótkowzroczności. W ostatnich latach strategie terapeutyczne ewoluowały od pojedynczych interwencji do kompleksowego, spersonalizowanego podejścia obejmującego farmakoterapię, zaawansowane technologie optyczne oraz modyfikację czynników środowiskowych. Atropina, szczególnie w niskich stężeniach, pozostaje jedną z najlepiej udokumentowanych metod kontroli progresji, jednak dynamiczny rozwój technologii optycznych umożliwił wprowadzenie nowych rozwiązań, takich jak soczewki H.A.L.T., D.I.M.S., DOT i C.A.R.E., wykorzystujące kontrolowane rozogniskowanie krótkowzroczne. Coraz większe zainteresowanie budzą również innowacyjne metody oparte na modulacji światłem, w tym terapia powtarzanym światłem czerwonym o niskiej intensywności (RLRL) oraz cyfrowa fotobiomodulacja, choć wymagają one dalszej oceny bezpieczeństwa i skuteczności. Istotnym kierunkiem rozwoju pozostaje terapia skojarzona, łącząca różne mechanizmy działania, szczególnie u dzieci z szybką progresją krótkowzroczności. Przyszłość kontroli krótkowzroczności będzie opierać się na indywidualizacji leczenia, uwzględniającej profil ryzyka pacjenta, tempo wydłużania osiowego oraz optymalny dobór metod terapeutycznych.

papers.title: Chitosan coating with Pickering emulsion of cellulose nanofibril/kaffir lime leaf essential oil for gourami fillets preservation
papers.journal: Frontiers in Food Science and Technology
papers.abstract: Gourami fillets ( Osphronemus goramy ) are susceptible to rapid deterioration during chilled storage. This study developed a chitosan-based edible coating containing a cellulose nanofibril (CNF)-stabilized Pickering emulsion of kaffir lime leaf essential oil (KEO) and evaluated its fish-preservation performance. A CNF concentration of 0.25% was selected as chitosan/CNF/KEO (ChiCK) stabilizer, and comparing with chitosan (Chi), chitosan/Tween 80/KEO (ChiTK). A ChiCK showed the highest zeta potential (57.00 ± 1.04 mV) and inhibition zones of 9.262 ± 0.639 mm, 10.306 ± 0.127 mm, 9.472 ± 0.824 mm, and 8.696 ± 0.260 mm against Escherichia coli , Pseudomonas aeruginosa , Bacillus cereus , and Staphylococcus aureus respectively. Its application on gourami fillet was able to suppress microbial growth with total plate count of 5.30 ± 0.05 log CFU g −1 , 1.12 log units lower than that of the uncoated fillets by day 2 storage and remined below the maximum limit of safe level (5.70 log CFU g −1 ), although the treatment did not reduce weight loss by day 3. The CNF-stabilized KEO coating therefore had potential for preserving the gourami fillets during chilled storage (5 °C–10 °C).

papers.title: MHD analysis of tangent hyperbolic micropolar fluid flow over a permeable stretching surface
papers.abstract: This investigation analyzes the effects of micropolar tangent hyperbolic hybrid nanofluid flow over a porous stretching sheet. Additionally, the influences of magnetohydrodynamics and heat source/sink effects are also considered into the analysis. The angular momentum equation is employed to examine the micro-rotation characteristics of the fluid flowing, whereas the enhancement in heat transport performance is evaluated through the inclusion of hybrid nanoparticles. These equations are subsequently reduced to a system of ordinary differential equations using suitable similarity transformations. The resulting nonlinear system is solved numerically using the Runge-Kutta-Fehlberg 45 (RKF-45) method in conjunction with a shooting technique. The effects of relevant physical parameters are illustrated through graphical representations, highlighting their physical significance. Graphical representations depict the physical significance of relevant parameters. Validation of numerical results is performed by comparing them with previously published data. The main conclusions of the study are as follows: (1) a gradual reduction in fluid velocity is observed with an increase in Weissenberg number $$\:(We=0.0,\:0.5,\:1.0)$$ , and permeability parameter $$\:\:(K=0.0,\:0.4,\:0.8)$$ , while the surface condition parameter is fixed at $$\:n\:=\:0.5$$ , (2) the skin friction coefficient shows a pronounced decrease as the permeability parameter increases $$\:(K=0.0,\:0.5,\:1.0)$$ , (3) the wall couple stress exhibits an increasing trend with rising values of the micro-rotation parameter $$\:({\Psi\:}=0.0,\:2.0,\:4.0)$$ . Owing to the unique rheological behavior, tangent hyperbolic fluids are widely applicable in engineering and biomedical systems, where they facilitate controlled transport in food processing, polymer technology, oil recovery, and blood flow analysis.

papers.title: Design and multiphysics analysis of an active-passive thermal protection strategy for transverse flux induction heating of moving strips
papers.abstract: Transverse flux induction heating (TFIH) offers distinct advantages in the field of metal strip heat treatment. However, optimizing its heating performance and ensuring the stable operation of the inductor requires a comprehensive multiphysics coupled analysis. To address the excessive inductor temperature rise caused by narrow air gaps in novel coil designs during high-temperature strip processing, this paper proposes a thermal protection strategy that combines active internal water cooling with passive composite thermal insulation. Forced water passages inside the hollow copper turns evacuate internal ohmic dissipation, while thin multi-layer ceramic-vacuum boards intercept intense radiative and convective heat fluxes from the moving strip. A finite element model of TFIH for moving strips is developed, accounting for strip motion, temperature-dependent material properties, water cooling, and thermal insulation. This modeling approach is experimentally validated using a low-power diamond-coil prototype. Subsequently, the validated method is applied to simulate a TFIH system featuring a novel dual-hexagonal-coil structure. Results demonstrate that the dual-hexagonal-coil structure significantly improves the thermal uniformity of the strip. Furthermore, the proposed protection measure not only prevents inductor overheating but also minimizes heat loss from the strip, producing a measurable rise in the delivered strip temperature without increasing input power. This study provides a valuable technical framework for the design and optimization of TFIH devices.

papers.title: Elapsed irrigation time improves morpho-kinematic classification of lettuce irrigation-stress histories
papers.abstract: Plant movement carries information on water status, but its predictive value may depend on the recent irrigation context in which movement is expressed. Previous lettuce morpho-kinematic (MK) analyses suggested that integrating a precise measurement of elapsed irrigation time ( Δt , defined as the interval from the last irrigation preceding the observation day to the start of imaging, excluding any same-day irrigation) may improve classification, but its contribution was not formally separated from nominal irrigation schedule (which represents a protocol-derived low-resolution Δt proxy). We reanalysed 140 plant-day observations from 24 plants in two controlled-environment experiments using, to isolate the predictive value of Δt , a schedule-balanced binary contrast obtained by grouping well irrigated (FC) and chronic stress (SC) against moderate and severe acute stresses (SM and SS respectively). Penalised logistic models were evaluated with plant-level balanced validation and plant-class balanced log-loss. Adding Δt reduced held-out log-loss from 0.5250 to 0.4836 (ΔLL = 0.0414; 95% CI = [0.0034, 0.0807]), whereas adding nominal schedule did not (ΔLL = −0.0039; 95% CI = [−0.0342, 0.0273]). The estimated Δt benefit remained predominantly positive under stricter validation, while schedule-preserving permutations and redundancy analysis supported an observation-specific contribution beyond schedule. These findings indicate that recent irrigation history can provide useful temporal context for MK-based classification; the underlying physiological mechanism remains unresolved.

Penalised logistic models were evaluated with plant-level balanced validation and plant-class balanced log-loss. These findings indicate that recent irrigation history can provide useful temporal context for MK-based classification; the underlying physiological mechanism remains unresolved.

papers.title: GenTile: Closing the Loop Between LLM Reasoning and Physical Telemetry for Autonomous NPU Graph Tuning
papers.abstract: Abstract Large language model (LLM) hidden widths—such as the 18 944-dimensional intermediate layer of the Qwen family—are often burst-aligned but not tile-compatible with heterogeneous NPU Cube engines, forcing the compiler to emit a small residual kernel that stalls the pipeline for up to 77% of cycles. Manual tuning does not scale across the growing space of model dimensions, sequence lengths, and operator variants. We present GenTile, a dual-role Research–Development (R&D) agent framework that closes the loop between LLM causal reasoning and on-device telemetry: a Research agent diagnoses bottlenecks from structured profiles, a Development agent materializes hardware-legal descriptors from compiler feedback, and iteration traces accumulate into a reusable knowledge base under an air-gap sandbox. On Ascend 910B, an offline hardware-faithful sandbox loop first demonstrates convergence mechanics; on real pretrained weights, the loop then measures the full multi-objective trade-off—latency, energy, memory, AICore efficiency, and approximation error (ε)—across six projection families from two Qwen generations (Qwen3.5-32B and Qwen2.5-7B). From telemetry alone, the agent deploys lossless sibling-projection fusions (QKV, gate–up) consistent with production inference-engine layouts (1.06–1.16× faster, up to 13% lower energy, ε=0, stable across sequence lengths, layer depths, and both models), and rejects every lossy low-rank rewrite—including a 1.39× lm_head speedup whose measured ε=0.89 exceeds any usable accuracy budget—while validating the Eckart–Young cliff prediction (ε → 0.002 at the tail rank) on structural layers. Baselines, ablations, cross-dimension generalization, and a sandbox loop that matches the geometric Oracle within four generations without exhaustive search further support the framework.

papers.title: Glomerular TRPC5 and Palladin immunohistochemical profiling in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis: tissue heterogeneity and exploratory clinical associations (PRIME-PATH I)
papers.abstract: Introduction Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) is a shared histopathologic pattern arising from biologically diverse podocyte injuries. Transient receptor potential canonical 5 (TRPC5) has been implicated in calcium–cytoskeletal signaling and entered clinical evaluation, whereas Palladin is an actin-associated scaffold involved in cytoskeletal organization. Their glomerular immunohistochemical patterns in human FSGS remain poorly characterized. Methods In this single-center retrospective biopsy cohort, 182 adults with biopsy-diagnosed FSGS between 2010 and 2020 were screened; 103 with adequate archived tissue, at least two evaluable glomeruli, and at least 24 months of follow-up comprised the analytic cohort. TRPC5 was scored as 0 (nuclear-only/no reproducible capillary-granular staining), 1 (discontinuous capillary-granular staining), or 2 (continuous/diffuse capillary-granular staining); scores 1–2 were grouped as TRPC5-positive. Palladin showed capillary-granular immunoreactivity in all evaluable biopsies and was classified as discontinuous or diffuse. Twenty-four-month treatment response was based on 24-hour urinary protein excretion. Poor response was the primary clinical outcome; kidney failure (maintenance dialysis or kidney transplantation) was evaluated during follow-up. Results TRPC5 immunoreactivity was present in 70/103 biopsies (68.0%) and absent in 33/103 (32.0%); Palladin staining was diffuse in 75/103 (72.8%) and discontinuous in 28/103 (27.2%). Poor response occurred in 54/103 (52.4%) and kidney failure in 33/103 (32.0%). TRPC5-positive patients more often had poor response (64.3% vs. 27.3%; P < 0.001) and kidney failure (42.9% vs. 9.1%; P < 0.001). In the primary adjusted model, TRPC5 positivity was associated with poor response (OR, 3.28; 95% CI, 1.13–9.52; P = 0.029) and kidney failure (OR, 5.51; 95% CI, 1.25–24.23; P = 0.024). Estimates were similar after adjustment for global glomerulosclerosis but attenuated and imprecise after IFTA adjustment ( n = 70). Palladin distribution was not independently associated with either outcome and did not improve model fit. Conclusion PRIME-PATH I identifies heterogeneous glomerular TRPC5 immunoreactivity as a tissue-level phenotype within morphologically defined FSGS, with Palladin providing complementary cytoskeletal staining-distribution information. These associations are hypothesis-generating, and independent prognostic value remains uncertain after accounting for chronic structural injury. The findings do not establish functional TRPC5 activation or treatment predictiveness but support prospective studies integrating etiologic classification, cell-specific localization, pathway activity, and therapeutic response.

papers.title: Village funds and poverty reduction in South Sumatra: A geographically weighted regression analysis
papers.abstract: Poverty alleviation is the main agenda of development programs in Indonesia. Most of the implemented programs are non-spatial in nature and thus not yet optimal. This study looks into spatial patterns and area-based approaches to reducing poverty in South Sumatra Province. The geographically weighted regression (GWR) method using poverty data from 2022-2024 was employed in this study. The study finds an assembled spatial poverty pattern where areas (sub-districts) with high poverty levels are surrounded by regions with high poverty levels. Therefore, the poverty alleviation strategy of each region is aligned with each influencing factor.

papers.title: PyMYB106‐PyLAC12 Modulates Callus Browning Through Phenylpropanoid‐Flavonoid Metabolism in Pinus yunnanensis
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Callus browning is the main obstacle in the process of in vitro culture of woody plants, which is more serious in conifers. Here, multi‐omics integration and transgenic approaches are employed to dissect the regulatory network of callus browning in Pinus yunnanensis . Browning callus showed marked reductions in total phenolics, flavonoids, and flavanols, with a concurrent increase in total quinone content. Non‐browning callus maintained low endogenous hormone homeostasis while sustaining elevated salicylic acid (SA) and 6‐benzylaminopurine (6‐BA) levels to enhance reactive oxygen species scavenging capacity. Weighted gene co‐expression network analysis (WGCNA) and two‐way orthogonal partial least squares (O2PLS) identified PyLAC12 as the central driver of browning. Overexpression of PyLAC12 substantially reduced phenolic acid and flavonoid contents and exacerbated browning, whereas PyLAC12 knockout produced the opposite effect. The upstream transcription factor PyMYB106 was further identified to directly bind the CAACCA motif and positively regulate PyLAC12 . Collectively, this study elucidates the molecular mechanism by which the PyMYB106‐PyLAC12 module drives callus browning through reprogramming flavonoid‐phenylpropanoid metabolic network.

papers.title: THE TRADE-OFF BETWEEN ANALGESIC POTENCY AND PROCEDURAL SAFETY: ERECTOR SPINAE PLANE BLOCK VERSUS THE GOLD-STANDARD THORACIC PARAVERTEBRAL BLOCK IN UNIPORTAL AND MULTIPORTAL VIDEO-ASSISTED THORACOSCOPIC SURGERY — A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS OF RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIALS AND PRIMARY STUDIES
papers.journal: The International Journal of Medical Science and Health Research
papers.abstract: Introduction: Uniportal and multiportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) reduce surgical trauma, yet moderate-to-severe acute pain remains common and predisposes to pulmonary complications and chronic postsurgical pain (CPSP). The thoracic paravertebral block (TPVB) is regarded as the regional "gold standard", whereas the erector spinae plane block (ESPB) is technically simpler and theoretically safer. Whether ESPB trades analgesic potency for procedural safety has not been quantified jointly. We aimed to compare the analgesic efficacy, opioid-sparing effect, recovery quality and procedural safety of ESPB versus TPVB, hypothesising that TPVB provides superior early analgesia, that both blocks converge beyond the early period, and that ESPB carries fewer block-related complications. Methods: The study strictly adhered to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines were searched from January 2011 to September 2026, supplemented by citation searching. Randomised controlled trials (RCTs), comparative cohorts and comparative case series directly comparing ESPB with TPVB in minimally invasive thoracic surgery were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale. Random-effects (DerSimonian–Laird) meta-analyses generated mean differences (MD), standardised mean differences (SMD) and risk ratios (RR); rare block-related complications were pooled with the Peto odds ratio (OR). Certainty was graded with GRADE. Results: Twenty-seven studies (24 RCTs, 3 cohorts; 2,015 participants; 26 thoracic studies, n = 1,960) were included and 20 contributed to 21 meta-analyses. TPVB produced lower rest pain at 0–2 h (MD 0.41, 95% CI 0.02–0.81; I² = 84%), an advantage below the 1-point minimal clinically important difference that disappeared from 6 h onward (24 h: MD 0.13, −0.20 to 0.46; 48 h: MD −0.08, −0.24 to 0.09). Dynamic pain did not differ at any time point. Twenty-four-hour opioid consumption showed a borderline opioid-sparing effect of TPVB (SMD 0.35, −0.00 to 0.71; p = 0.051), significant in adults only (SMD 0.41, 0.04–0.79). Rescue analgesia (RR 1.21, 0.83–1.77), PONV (RR 1.00, 0.75–1.34), hypotension (RR 0.60, 0.18–1.97), QoR-15 (MD 1.19, −4.80 to 7.17), length of stay (MD −0.13 days, −0.38 to 0.12) and CPSP (RR 0.96, 0.68–1.34) were comparable. Block-related complications (pneumothorax, pleural puncture, haematoma, unintended epidural spread) were markedly less frequent with ESPB (1/276 vs 15/270; Peto OR 0.15, 0.05–0.40; p < 0.001). Discussion: The ESPB–TPVB relationship is a time-dependent trade-off: TPVB buys a small, short-lived gain in early somatic analgesia and possibly opioid sparing at the price of a roughly seven-fold higher odds of block-related complications, whereas analgesia, recovery quality and long-term pain converge thereafter. Certainty was low to very low for most efficacy outcomes and moderate for safety, length of stay and CPSP. Conclusion: ESPB is a safer, analgesically comparable alternative to TPVB for (uniportal) VATS beyond the first postoperative hours. TPVB may be reserved for patients in whom maximal early analgesia is prioritised and procedural risk is acceptable.
papers.summary: Introduction: Uniportal and multiportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) reduce surgical trauma, yet moderate-to-severe acute pain remains common and predisposes to pulmonary complications and chronic postsurgical pain (CPSP). Results: Twenty-seven studies (24 RCTs, 3 cohorts; 2,015 participants; 26 thoracic studies, n = 1,960) were included and 20 contributed to 21 meta-analyses. Twenty-four-hour opioid consumption showed a borderline opioid-sparing effect of TPVB (SMD 0.35, −0.00 to 0.71; p = 0.051), significant in adults only (SMD 0.41, 0.04–0.79).

papers.title: Characterization of Ethyl Lauroyl Arginate‐Enhanced Poly(Vinyl Alcohol)/Chitosan Biodegradable Indicator Films Containing Betalains From White‐Fleshed Dragon Fruit Peels
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study aimed to fabricate and characterize Polyvinyl alcohol/chitosan‐based films containing 30 wt% chitosan (PCs), crude betalain‐rich extract from white‐fleshed dragon fruit (Selenicereus undatus) peels (DPE), and ethyl lauroyl arginate (LAE). DPE was obtained as a lyophilized powder from hot‐water extraction without pH adjustment, with betacyanins as the major pigment components. PCs films containing 10–50 wt% DPE were prepared, and the film with 20 wt% DPE ( β 20@PCs) exhibited the most suitable halo‐ and vapochromic responses to pH buffers and ammonia vapor. LAE was subsequently incorporated into β 20@PCs at 1, 3, 5, 7, or 9 wt% to provide antibacterial functionality. Although β 20@PCs showed significantly lower tensile performance than PCs, most LAE‐enhanced formulations caused only slight and statistically non‐significant further decreases in tensile properties. Increasing DPE content increased water vapor permeability but reduced swelling and water solubility. LAE had no significant effects on these water‐related properties, except at 7–9 wt% LAE. The β 20@PCs film showed no antibacterial activity, whereas LAE‐containing films inhibited E. coli , S. aureus , B. cereus , L. monocytogenes , and S. typhi . Among them, β 20@PCs‐3wt%LAE (E3‐ β 20@PCs) exhibited the highest ammonia‐responsive color changes. Overall, E3‐ β 20@PCs showed promising colorimetric, antibacterial, and mechanical properties for active–intelligent packaging applications.

papers.title: Nonlinear effects and spatial spillovers of emerging industry clustering on welfare performance under renewable energy transition in China''s urban agglomerations
papers.abstract: The global energy transition is currently hindered by inefficient welfare conversion and regional disparities, which have precipitated a "new resource curse" across Chinese urban agglomerations. The resulting welfare divergence between production and consumption zones underscores the urgency of optimizing industrial spatial allocation—a prerequisite for fulfilling the nation''s "dual carbon" objectives. Based on 2014–2023 POI data from eight emerging sectors, this study characterizes the spatial patterns of 19 urban agglomerations using Kernel Density Estimation. It employs an improved enhanced group-frontier dynamic SBM model with super-efficiency to gauge the welfare performance under renewable energy transition (WPRE) and develops an integrated XGBoost-SHAP-GEO model to reveal the non-linear associations and spatial spillover effects of industrial agglomeration. The study reveals: ①A "plateaued fluctuation and volatile growth" trajectory defines WPRE of Chinese urban agglomerations; ②emerging industry agglomerations exhibit polycentric evolution and a strengthening core-periphery architecture; ③the association between emerging industry agglomeration and WPRE is non-monotonic, consistent with diminishing rather than reversing returns; ④Geospatial characteristics, together with their interaction effects, constitute the primary predictors of WPRE, with associations exhibiting substantial stage-specific heterogeneity. Uncovering the nonlinear associations and spatial heterogeneity of industrial agglomeration, this work offers a scientific basis for breaking the ''new resource curse'' and enhancing industry-energy-welfare synergy. The conclusions provide significant policy implications for global resource-rich regions striving to promote inclusive welfare distribution within the renewable energy transition.

papers.title: The feasibility of training nnU-Net to segment pediatric Wilms tumor with small datasets
papers.abstract: Introduction Segmentation of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can be used in the clinical care of patients with (suspected) Wilms tumor (WT). Manual segmentation, however, is time consuming and user dependent. Deep learning can be used to automate this, but is often associated with the need for large training datasets to be trained successfully, which is inherently challenging in pediatric populations. The aim of this study was to determine the effect of the number of training patients on automated WT segmentation. Methods 56 patients with a suspected WT were included in this retrospective study. The pre-operative MRI scans were divided in a training (n = 45) and test (n = 11) set. The segmentation was based on nnU-Net, an out-of-the-box framework for image segmentation. nnU-Net was trained on a random selection of five patients, and the resulting segmentation method was tested on a fixed test set of 11 patients. Next, patients were added to the training dataset with incremental steps of five patients, up to the full dataset of 45 patients. This process was repeated 5 times to account for random sampling. The Dice score was used as measure for segmentation performance. We pragmatically defined a Dice score of > 0.80 as a reference level for segmentation performance. Results The lowest median Dice score was obtained when using a subset of five training patients (0.38). The highest median Dice score was observed for training on 45 patients (0.91). An median Dice score of 0.80 was reached using a minimal subset of 10 training patients. The Dice score showed dependency on the random selection of the training patients, with the largest spread in performance observed in the training set of five patients. A large spread in performance between the 11 test set patients was observed. Discussion Using this specific training and test cohort, a median Dice score of 0.80 was reached with just 10 training patients, however, the results showed considerable variation in the individual test patients. The performance spread between the random subsampling of the training patients highlights the importance of clinically representable datasets when dealing with the small dataset sizes inherent to pediatric oncology.

papers.title: Experimental and Computational Investigation of Thermal Stability and Mechanical Performance of HDPE/Nanoclay/Alumina Hybrid Composites
papers.abstract: The study aims to prepare high-density polyethylene (HDPE) reinforced with nanoclay (NC) and alumina fillers by the melt‑mixing technique. The modulus of samples EC1 and EC2 before and after thermal aging is 665.4, 630.6, and 702, 674 MPa, respectively. The Halpin-Tsai and the Mori-Tanaka models closely predict the modulus values compared to experimental values. The Tsai-Pagano model, the Christensen-Waals model, and the ROM model overpredict the modulus of the composites compared to the experimental modulus. The critical stress‑intensity factor of the EC1 composite before and after aging is 1.07 and 1.09 MPa m0.5, respectively. The fracture energy release values of the EC1 composite before and after aging are 1.72 and 1.71 kJ/m2, respectively. The predicted elastic modulus of the 3% alumina-reinforced composite closely matches the experimentally measured value, indicating that the COMSOL accurately estimates the ultimate stress behavior. The thermogravimetric analysis test indicates that EC2, EC3, and ECA2 samples break down at higher temperatures than pure HDPE samples. The polymer composite ECA3 shows the slowest rate of mass loss at elevated temperatures compared to other composites in the derivative thermogram for polymer composites.

papers.title: Mechanical and Thermophysical Performance of Unfired Clay Bricks Incorporating Recycled Esparto Grass Residues
papers.journal: Advances in Environmental and Engineering Research
papers.abstract: This article investigates the effects of incorporating recycled plant fibers into raw clay bricks to evaluate the resulting changes in their mechanical and thermophysical properties. The clay used, an illite type (confirmed by its potassium oxide (K2O) content), originates from the Ifrane region of Morocco and has a high silica (SiO2) content, making it a suitable building material. Different levels of recycled plant fiber incorporation, from 0% to 20% (0%, 1%, 3%, 7%, 15%, and 20% by weight), were studied. The addition of significant amounts of recycled plant fibers resulted in bricks that were more porous, lighter, and exhibited higher water absorption. A decrease in the compressive strength of the samples was observed, from 12.38 MPa for the reference samples to 3.58 MPa for the incorporation of 20% recycled plant fibers. Furthermore, the addition of a fiber-based additive improved the thermal performance of the raw clay bricks: a reduction in thermal conductivity of approximately 43% was observed compared to the reference samples, resulting in better insulating properties. The 29% increase in the specific heat capacity of the bricks indicates a greater capacity to store and release thermal energy. Beyond these thermophysical gains, the valorization of an abundant stream of plant fiber waste into a functional, raw building material reduces the extraction of raw clay, avoids the energy consumption and CO2 emissions associated with firing, and decreases the energy demand of buildings through improved insulation, thus contributing to the objectives of a circular economy and sustainable development in the construction sector.

papers.title: Multispecies Narratives as Epistemic Method: The Case of Daphnia
papers.abstract: This article explores a multispecies narrative method as an epistemic tool for rethinking scientific knowledge practices. Drawing on six peer-reviewed publications on the behaviour and longevity of aquatic invertebrates in response to predator cues, the author develops six literary narratives that reinterpret key findings through distinct narrative perspectives – from third-person objectivity to second-person direct address. These narrative forms engage with feminist epistemology, posthuman ethics, and multispecies storytelling to rethink conventional modes of scientific communication. Rather than seeking objectivity through detachment, the article embraces relationality, partiality, and affect as valid pathways to knowledge. The result is a diffractive representation of interspecies entanglements that foregrounds the epistemic role and vulnerability of nonhuman subjects and the ethical responsibilities of researchers. This work contributes to ongoing discussions in the environmental humanities, animal studies, and qualitative inquiry regarding the place of imagination and empathy in science.

papers.title: D-enantiomeric β-casein 197 disrupts biofilm-associated infection of MDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii through superior LPS binding and host cell protection
papers.abstract: Biofilms formed by multidrug-resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii are a major cause of chronic nosocomial infections and therapeutic failure. L-form antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are rapidly degraded by proteases, whereas D-enantiomeric peptides offer enhanced resistance to proteases. Here, we synthesized L- and D-β-casein 197, a milk-derived AMP, and systematically compared their antibiofilm activities against eight clinical isolates of P. aeruginosa and A. baumannii. The D-form reduced biofilm biomass by up to 83% during formation and by up to 88% in preformed biofilms. Mechanistic analyses revealed that the D-form caused more extensive membrane disruption, as demonstrated by flow cytometry and transmission electron microscopy. Isothermal titration calorimetry showed that the D-form bound LPS with higher affinity (KD 0.8 μM vs 3.1 μM), and molecular docking identified additional hydrogen bonds with lipid A. The D-form also more effectively inhibited bacterial motility. Both peptides exhibited low cytotoxicity toward cells (>90% viability at 100 μM), and the D-form reduced bacteria-induced cytotoxicity and bacterial internalization in infected macrophages more effectively than the L-form. In a Galleria mellonella infection model, D-β-casein 197 significantly improved survival against P. aeruginosa no. R1 and A. baumannii no. 13 challenge over 96 h compared to the L-form and untreated infected controls, while larval survival remained comparable to PBS controls, indicating negligible host toxicity. These findings identify D-β-casein 197 as a potent antibiofilm peptide against MDR Gram-negative biofilms, with enhanced activity, and LPS-neutralization assays confirmed that its antimicrobial potency is, at least in part, attributable to its stronger LPS binding affinity.

papers.title: Gudan Wan attenuates metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis by modulating autophagy and the Bcl-2/Caspase-3/Caspase-8 apoptotic axis
papers.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
papers.abstract: Background Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a leading global cause of end-stage liver disease, with safe and effective therapies still lacking. Gudan Wan (GDW), a traditional Chinese medicine for Gu Dan (damp-heat and food stagnation with middle-jiao dysfunction), shares analogous pathogenesis with MASH, yet its anti-MASH efficacy remains to be elucidated. Methods GDW’s therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms via in vivo toxicity and pharmacodynamic evaluation, network pharmacology, western blotting, UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS characterization, and molecular docking. A MASH model of mice was induced by high-fat diet and carbon tetrachloride (HFD+CCl 4 ). Results A 30-day toxicity test revealed no overt toxicity or organic lesions in mice at GDW doses up to 4000 mg/kg. MASH mice, GDW significantly ameliorated hepatic injury, lipid metabolic disorders, pro-inflammatory cytokine release, and fibrosis. Network pharmacology identified 237 intersecting targets, with apoptosis as the core regulatory pathway and CASP 3/8, AKT1, TP53, BCL2, and TNF as core targets. Western blotting confirmed GDW modulated key apoptotic proteins (upregulating Bcl-2, downregulating Caspase-3/8) and corrected autophagic dysfunction via LC3 and p62 modulation. A total of 179 chemical components were characterized by UHPLC-QTOF-MS, of which 19 were found to enter the liver. Molecular docking predicted favorable binding of the major active components to Caspase-3, AKT1, TP53, and TNF-α, but not to Bcl-2 or Caspase-8, suggesting indirect regulation of the latter two by GDW. Conclusion GDW exerts its anti-MASH effects by modulating autophagy and the Bcl-2/Caspase-3/Caspase-8 apoptotic axis, with its favorable safety profile supporting its therapeutic potential for further investigation.

papers.title: Decoupling Dissolution from Water Oxidation at Single-Faceted High-Entropy Perovskite Electrodes
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract High-entropy oxides (HEOs) are promising anode materials for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) due to their wide compositional space and electronic flexibility. However, their electrochemical dissolution and OER remain concurrent, preventing decoupled analysis of dissolution kinetics and stability. Here, we present a combined atomic force microscopy (AFM) and scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM) strategy to decouple lattice dissolution from water oxidation under well-defined reaction conditions. Structurally analogous, atomically flat, single-faceted (001) ABO3 perovskite electrodes, La1–xSrx(Cr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2)O3 with x = 0 and 0.3, serve as model systems to probe dissolution and OER kinetics in acid. Pipet-probed localized cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry reveal that the measured current contains contributions from both OER and lattice dissolution, the latter producing nanoscale dissolution pits beneath the SECCM droplet. By correlating pit-growth kinetics with total OER charge as a function of pulse duration (τ), overpotential (η), and pH, we quantitatively separate dissolution from OER. The proportional scaling between dissolution charge and total charge indicates that OER and dissolution proceed within a common kinetic regime, sharing a common intermediate. A rate-law-based analysis yields the standard dissolution rate constant (kd0 cm/s), transfer coefficient (α), and proton reaction order (b) for the dissolution of the 001 facet of both HEO-P. Our results unravel how aliovalent A-site substitution (30% Sr2+) alters dissolution kinetics, charge partitioning between dissolution and OER, and thickness-dependent stability, thereby enabling quantitative disentangling of the intrinsic activity and stability of HEO electrodes.

Our results unravel how aliovalent A-site substitution (30% Sr2+) alters dissolution kinetics, charge partitioning between dissolution and OER, and thickness-dependent stability, thereby enabling quantitative disentangling of the intrinsic activity and stability of HEO electrodes.

papers.title: Automated carotid artery atherosclerotic inflammation segmentation in PET using MSR-Net
papers.abstract: Abstract Abstract Objective. To develop an automated method for segmentation and uptake quantification of carotid atherosclerotic inflammation on 64Cu-CANF-comb PET while accounting for partial-volume and tissue-fraction effects. Approach. Synthetic carotid PET images with known fractional-volume ground truth were generated by combining MR-derived high-resolution activity maps with GATE Monte Carlo simulation incorporating major PET physical processes and matched to the Biograph mMR acquisition and reconstruction. A two-stage network first localized the carotid vessel wall from T1-weighted MR and then estimated voxel-wise inflammation fraction from masked PET. Both stages used a multiscale residual (MSR) convolutional backbone. Performance was compared with U-Net, Transformer U-Net, DUCK-Net, and iterative Yang partial-volume correction. Main results. In a two-alternative forced-choice study, five nuclear-medicine physicians identified real images with 54% accuracy (54/100; Wilson 95% CI 0.44–0.63; exact binomial p = 0.48). On 184 simulated test slices from five held-out patients, the proposed method achieved a weighted DSC of 0.79, compared with 0.73 for U-Net, 0.69 for Transformer U-Net, and 0.75 for DUCK-Net, with corresponding HD values of 1.85, 2.29, 2.32, and 2.23 voxels. Patient-cluster bootstrap comparisons favored the proposed method for DSC and HD against all three baselines (Holm-corrected p ≤ 0.031). Overall ENRMSE was 0.24 versus 0.59, 0.68, and 0.59 for the three DL baselines and 0.57 for iterative Yang. In seven patients, corrected SUV showed a positive association with MR-derived lipid-rich/necrotic core with hemorrhage. Significance. The proposed framework improved carotid PET segmentation and uptake quantification under simulated conditions. The patient analysis is preliminary and requires external validation with biological reference standards before clinical deployment.

In seven patients, corrected SUV showed a positive association with MR-derived lipid-rich/necrotic core with hemorrhage.

papers.title: Can Carbon Coating Improve the Durability of Carbon Xerogels as Catalyst Supports for Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell Electrodes?
papers.abstract: Abstract A carbon xerogel (CX) with a pore size of ∼70 nm was selected as support for a fuel cell electrocatalyst. While carbon xerogels offer excellent mass transport properties, their amorphous nature reduces their resistance to carbon corrosion under the oxidizing conditions of PEMFC operation. To tackle this, a partially graphitized carbon layer was deposited on the xerogel surface using chemical vapor deposition (CVD). This layer covers a large part of the micropores but keeps intact the interconnected meso/macropore network of the CX. The carbon-coated CX was also post-treated at 1500 °C under an inert atmosphere for further crystallization. Pt nanoparticles (20 wt %) were then deposited on both pristine and CVD-treated CXs by reduction of hexachloroplatinic acid in liquid phase; the resulting catalysts were evaluated with respect to their electrochemical activity and compared to a commercial carbon black-supported catalyst. The catalyst on the post-treated supports exhibited initial catalytic activities comparable to those obtained on pristine CX. After accelerated aging in RDE configuration, despite a decrease in the catalytic surface of Pt, specific activities increased while mass activities remained stable. In the Membrane-Electrodes Assembly configuration, the catalyst supported on the carbon xerogel post-treated with chemical vapor deposition and subsequent high-temperature treatment at 1500 °C exhibited encouraging durability behavior. This behavior was attributed to differences in Pt nanoparticle growth on post-treated carbon xerogel supports. Moreover, it was observed that these post-treatments do not negatively affect mass transport inside the electrode, since the meso/macropore texture remained intact.

papers.title: Emerging Diagnostic and Therapeutic Applications of Remote Patient Monitoring in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) Care• A Patient-Centred Approach to Optimizing Inhaled Therapy: Integrating Patient, Device, Drug and Disease Factors• Clinical and Serological Evaluation and Management of Rheumatic Disease-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease• Single-Inhaler Triple Therapy Is Just The Start• Optimizing In-Hospital Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) Care in Canada: Challenges, Evidence, and Future Directions
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, with prevalence projected to rise by nearly 25% between 2020 and 2050 to reach approximately 600 million people worldwide.1 COPD is characterized by persistent airflow limitation, leading to chronic dyspnea and reduced exercise capacity. Patients experience exacerbations of COPD (ECOPDs), clinically significant acute episodes characterized by increased airway inflammation and sudden worsening of breathlessness, which contribute substantially to lung function decline and are strongly associated with mortality.2 Exacerbations account for the vast majority of COPD-related healthcare use, driving hospital admissions, healthcare costs, long-term functional decline, and mortality risk.2 Despite progress in inhaled and biologic therapies, the management of recurrent exacerbations remains a significant challenge, and in fact, admissions for COPD are uniquely increasing rather than decreasing when compared with other chronic diseases after adjusting for population growth and aging in Canada.3 This highlights two important clinical realities: 1) that the current approach to COPD care is failing, and 2) that for both patients and health systems alike, there is a pressing need for innovative strategies to address and reduce the burden of COPD exacerbation admissions and readmissions.

papers.title: Experimental study and mathematical modeling of dynamic viscosity of MgO–Y₂O₃–SiO₂/water ternary hybrid nanofluid
papers.abstract: In recent years, nanofluid (NF) rheology and thermal behavior have attracted growing attention due to their promising industrial applications. This study experimentally examines how temperature (T) and solid volume fraction (SVF) affect the dynamic viscosity (µ) of a ternary hybrid nanofluid (THNF) based on MgO–Y₂O₃–SiO₂ dispersed in water. In addition, mono nanofluids (MNFs) and binary hybrids nanofluids (HNFs) containing different combinations of the three oxides were prepared and analyzed under identical conditions. All NF samples were synthesized via the conventional two-step method, with SVFs ranging from 0.06% to 0.10%, and T varying between 20 °C and 60 °C. Zeta potential analysis confirmed the stability of the THNF. The µ measurements were performed using a Brookfield viscometer. Results indicate a consistent decrease in µ with rising T, while an increase in nanoparticle (NP) concentration leads to higher µ at any given T. Among all samples, Y₂O₃-based MNF exhibited the highest µ, with a value of 2.886 at 20 °C and SVF of 0.10%, corresponding to an enhancement of 187% compared to the BF. The THNF also showed significant thickening due to synergistic interactions between its constituents. Lastly, a predictive mathematical correlation was developed to estimate µ as a function of T and SVF. The proposed model closely matched the experimental data, confirming its reliability for future implementations. Lastly, two distinct mathematical modeling approaches were employed to estimate µ as a function of T and SVF. A 7th-degree polynomial regression model was developed, achieving an exceptional R2 ≈ 0.9996, alongside a Response Surface Methodology (RSM) model rigorously validated via Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV), achieving an R2 ≈ 0.987. Both models closely matched the experimental data, confirming their reliability for practical engineering applications. Effects of T (20–60 °C) and concentration (0.06–0.10 %) were experimentally studied. Increase in concentration/or decrease in T consistently resulted in higher viscosity. Y₂O₃/water nanofluid has highest µ increase, followed by MgO–Y₂O₃ and MgO nanofluid. SiO₂/water nanofluid has lowest µ increase, confirming mild rheological influence. MgO–Y₂O₃–SiO₂/water nanofluid was found to behave as a Newtonian fluid.

papers.title: FBXO28 promotes the malignancy of non-small cell lung cancer through ubiquitination-mediated activation of BRD4
papers.abstract: Abstract The E3 ubiquitin ligase FBXO28 has been implicated in the progression of various cancers, yet its precise function and substrates remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the role of FBXO28 in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and its underlying mechanism. We observed an upregulation of FBXO28 in NSCLC, and higher FBXO28 levels correlated with poorer patient outcomes. Functional experiments revealed that silencing FBXO28 inhibited NSCLC proliferation, migration, and invasion and induced apoptosis, whereas overexpressing FBXO28 had the opposite effects. Using coimmunoprecipitation (co-IP) assays, we identified an interaction between FBXO28 and BRD4. Further investigations revealed that FBXO28 mediated the ubiquitination of BRD4 at K395 through a K63-conjugated model. The ubiquitination by FBXO28 does not lead to the degradation of BRD4, but promotes its transcriptional coactivation, as the modulation of FBXO28 affects the expression of BRD4-targeting genes and the binding of BRD4 to the promoters of its target genes. Mechanistically, FBXO28-mediated ubiquitination of BRD4 facilitates the activation of P-TEFb and subsequent phosphorylation of the serine 2 (Ser2) C-terminal domain (CTD) of the largest subunit of RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) to initiate transcription. Furthermore, in a positive feedback loop, BRD4 binds to the FBXO28 promoter and increased FBXO28 transcription. In summary, our findings highlight the pivotal role of the FBXO28/BRD4 positive feedback loop in driving the malignancy of NSCLC.

Using coimmunoprecipitation (co-IP) assays, we identified an interaction between FBXO28 and BRD4. Further investigations revealed that FBXO28 mediated the ubiquitination of BRD4 at K395 through a K63-conjugated model.

papers.title: Extrusion-Structured Plant-Based Meat Analogs: Factors Governing Texture and Quality
papers.abstract: Plant-based meat analogs (PBMAs) have attracted increasing attention as sustainable alternatives to animal meat, with extrusion becoming the most widely used structuring technology for their production.This review summarizes recent advances in extrusion-structured PBMAs, with particular emphasis on low-and high-moisture extrusion cooking, by integrating evidence from a broad range of peer-reviewed studies and reviews spanning foundational research to recent developments.The effects of key parameters including protein sources, processing variables, and functional additives are discussed in relation to the mechanism of protein transformation underlying the characteristic anisotropic fibrous structure of PBMAs.Functional properties of additives such as starches, hydrocolloids, dietary fibers, lipids, mushroom-and seaweed-derived ingredients, and other bioactives or upcycled components are discussed for their roles in modulating texture, juiciness, antioxidant activity, sensory quality, and nutritional value.Analytical approaches employed to evaluate the sensory characteristics as well as physicochemical and functional properties of PBMAs are also examined.In addition, the nutritional profile, innovations, and emerging trends are reviewed to provide insights into future perspectives for improving product quality, nutritional value, sustainability, and consumer acceptability.

papers.title: Cell-wall chemistry governs anisotropic shrinkage during wood carbonization: roles of polysaccharide degradation and exchangeable cations
papers.abstract: The anisotropic shrinkage of wood during carbonization critically affects biochar microstructure, but its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We examined shrinkage behavior in the radial (R) and longitudinal (L) directions in relation to polysaccharide thermal degradation, exchangeable cation species, and cell structure, using ten wood species (five softwoods and five hardwoods) and their cation-exchanged derivatives (H + , Na + , K + , Mg 2+ , Ca 2+ ). Thermogravimetric and continuous dimensional analyses revealed that the onset of shrinkage in the R-direction is primarily associated with hemicellulose degradation, whereas shrinkage in the L-direction is linked to cellulose degradation and occurs rapidly at temperatures 10–20 °C higher than the derivative thermogravimetric peak, when most cellulose microfibrils have already decomposed. Na + and K + lowered shrinkage onset temperatures across most species, whereas in hardwoods, R-direction shrinkage magnitude increased with H + and Mg 2+ substitution. Anatomical differences, particularly in ray parenchyma morphology, explained why hardwoods generally shrank more in the R direction. These results demonstrate that anisotropic shrinkage during wood carbonization is governed by polysaccharide-specific thermal degradation, modulated by exchangeable cation species and anatomical features. Furthermore, directional shrinkage can be predictably tuned through cation control and species selection to optimize biochar microstructure.

These results demonstrate that anisotropic shrinkage during wood carbonization is governed by polysaccharide-specific thermal degradation, modulated by exchangeable cation species and anatomical features.

papers.title: Photopolymer functionalization with trace amounts of bimetallic AgTi nanoparticles for antibacterial vat photopolymerization-produced parts
papers.abstract: Abstract Functionalization of additive manufacturing (AM) polymer feedstocks by incorporating nanoparticles (NPs) has gained considerable attention to produce functional polymer parts with tailored physicochemical properties, addressing the demand for customizable parts with unprecedented geometric freedom. In particular, vat photopolymerization (VPP) holds great potential for fabricating intricate, miniaturized, and functionalized items at superior spatial resolution. However, large fractions of nanoadditives commonly employed are prone to agglomerating and affect the processability. Herein, a facile composite formulation approach is introduced to obtain photopolymers functionalized with very low amounts of silver-titanium (AgTi) NPs and Ag-decorated titanium dioxide (TiO 2 ) NPs. Colloidal NPs of only 5.8 nm mean size are synthesized via pulsed laser ablation in liquids (PLAL), and subsequently incorporated into the polymer matrix via direct-mixing. Working curves reveal that the NPs reduce the critical energies required for VPP, confirming that the processability is maintained, which is attributed to the low NP amounts of only ≤0.05 wt% used in this study. While the mechanical properties remain unaffected by the NP incorporation, the composites exhibit antibacterial activity, as manifested by effectively inhibiting Gram-positive/-negative bacteria attachment even at only 0.05 wt% NP loading. The versatility and simplicity of the functionalization approach render it attractive for using arbitrary colloidal NP systems, extending the diversity of functionalities added to photopolymers at a minimal NP employment.
