papers.title: Fast few-shot intrusion detection via depthwise meta-learning
papers.abstract: Network intrusion detection systems (NIDS) increasingly rely on deep learning to cope with evolving cyber attacks, yet they typically require large amounts of labeled data per attack type and exhibit poor generalization to novel threats. Recent advances in meta-learning and few-shot learning have shown promise for alleviating data scarcity, while depthwise separable convolutions (DSC) offer a computationally efficient means of extracting fine-grained spatial–temporal features from network traffic. In this paper, we propose a meta-learning framework for few-shot network intrusion detection that combines a model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) objective with a one-dimensional DSC backbone. Tasks are defined episodically across attack families and datasets, enabling the meta-learner to acquire an initialization that rapidly adapts to unseen attack types using only a handful of labeled flows. We derive the corresponding bilevel optimization problem, analyze the computational benefits of DSC compared with standard convolutions, and present an end-to-end architecture tailored for flow-based NIDS. Experiments on CICIDS2017, NSL-KDD and UNSW-NB15 under challenging 5-shot and 10-shot settings demonstrate consistent improvements in accuracy and macro- $$F_1$$ over strong convolutional, metric-based and attention-enhanced baselines inspired by recent literature. The proposed approach reduces parameters by up to 65% relative to conventional convolutions while maintaining or improving detection performance. We conclude with a discussion of limitations and directions for integrating cross-domain adaptation and self-attention into meta-learned DSC architectures.

We conclude with a discussion of limitations and directions for integrating cross-domain adaptation and self-attention into meta-learned DSC architectures.

papers.title: Characterization of a coal fly ash–silica composite as a potential catalyst for hydrogenation
papers.journal: ABUAD International  Journal of Natural and Applied Sciences
papers.abstract: The steady energy demand across the continent, population growth, and increasing consumption of petroleum-based fuels driven by commercialization, urbanization, industrialization, and technological advancement have intensified the search for sustainable alternative energy sources. Hydrogenation-Derived Renewable Diesel (HDRD), also known as green diesel, is a promising renewable fuel capable of reducing environmental degradation and providing compatibility with compression ignition (CI) engines with little or no modification. This study investigated the potential of silica oxide (SiO₂)-reinforced fly ash (FA) as a heterogeneous catalyst for HDRD production from used cooking oil. Fly ash sourced from Eskom Holdings SOC Limited, South Africa, was processed, sieved, and calcined before characterization. A 60:40 FA/SiO₂ catalyst ratio was employed to enhance active metal oxides, surface area, thermal stability, and hydroprocessing performance. Physicochemical characterization using Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), Brunauer–Emmett– Teller (BET), X-ray Diffraction (XRD), and thermal analysis confirmed improvements in surface area, pore structure, and pore volume, increasing from 0.8621 to 41.2551 m²/g, 0.5920 to 45.2757 m²/g, and 0.0042 to 0.1544 cm³/g, respectively. The synergistic catalyst exhibited desirable hydrogenation properties and moderate cracking capability, demonstrating strong potential for sustainable HDRD production and waste valorization.

papers.title: CT-based prediction of EGFR mutation subtypes and TP53 co-mutation status in lung adenocarcinoma
papers.abstract: Background Epidermal growth factor receptor ( EGFR ) mutation status is a key determinant of targeted treatment in lung adenocarcinoma, whereas co-occurring TP53 alterations may further affect therapeutic response and prognosis. This study aimed to develop a noninvasive CT-based approach for predicting EGFR mutation subtypes and TP53 co-mutation status in lung adenocarcinoma, thereby providing imaging support for pretreatment risk stratification and clinical decision-making. Methods Patients with pathologically confirmed lung adenocarcinoma who underwent pretreatment chest CT and molecular testing were retrospectively enrolled from a single-center cohort. A total of 1,633 patients were included and categorized into five molecular groups: EGFR wild type, EGFR 19del, EGFR L858R, EGFR 19del with TP53 co-mutation, and EGFR L858 R with TP53 co-mutation. Based on chest CT images, key slice extraction, lesion ROI generation, automatic segmentation, and image standardization were performed. Semantic CT features, radiomics features, and deep CT representations were then derived. Under a unified data partitioning and standardized evaluation framework, four models were constructed and compared for the five-class classification task: a random forest model based on semantic CT features, a support vector machine model based on radiomics features, a Qwen-based semantic classification model, and a MedicalDINOv3-based deep learning model. To eliminate confounding bias induced by multimodal feature fusion, two ablation experiments were supplemented to split the model input features, and two MedicalDINOv3 models were built with inputs restricted to semantic features only and CT images only, respectively. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, macro-averaged area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and macro-F1 score. External validation was further conducted using public and multicenter datasets. Results Among the 1,633 patients in the internal cohort, 731 were EGFR wild type, 295 had EGFR 19del, 399 had EGFR L858R, 118 had EGFR 19del with TP53 co-mutation, and 90 had EGFR L858 R with TP53 co-mutation. To quantify the independent predictive value of different input modalities, ablation experiments on three variants of MedicalDINOv3 were performed. Ablation results revealed distinct performance among three input strategies. The MedicalDINOv3 with only semantic input obtained a test accuracy of 31.55% and an AUC of 0.6305 with limited predictive ability. The branch solely fed with CT images reached an accuracy of 55.61% and a macro-average AUC of 0.6347. The complete MedicalDINOv3 integrating CT deep features, clinical and semantic features performed best, with a test accuracy of 0.6905 and a macro-average AUC of 0.8788. This comparison proved that CT deep representations outperform traditional handcrafted imaging and semantic features, and multi-modal fusion further improves subtype stratification performance. The support vector machine model achieved an accuracy of 0.527, a macro-AUC of 0.792 and a macro-F1 score of 0.524; the random forest model achieved an accuracy of 0.455, a macro-AUC of 0.819 and a macro-F1 score of 0.412; and the Qwen-based model achieved an accuracy of 0.339, a macro-AUC of 0.700 and a macro-F1 score of 0.316. Receiver operating characteristic analyses showed that the deep learning model provided relatively stable discrimination for EGFR wild type and TP53 co-mutated categories, whereas overlap remained between the two major EGFR -sensitive subtypes, EGFR 19del and EGFR L858 R. In external validation, the public dataset used for EGFR binary classification yielded an overall accuracy of 67.0% and an AUC of 0.6666. The raw overall accuracy of the cohort was 75.5%, and raw overall accuracy is prone to overestimation when the cohort has severe class imbalance dominated by EGFR wild-type samples, which can only serve as an auxiliary reference. Multicenter five-class external validation yielded a balanced accuracy of 58.2% and a macro F1 of 0.574. The subtype-specific AUCs for EGFR wild type, EGFR 19del, EGFR L858R, EGFR 19del with TP53 co-mutation, and EGFR L858 R with TP53 co-mutation were 0.8342, 0.6504, 0.7221, 0.6586, and 0.7563, respectively. Conclusion A CT-based deep learning model can provide noninvasive stratification of EGFR mutation subtypes and TP53 co-mutation status in lung adenocarcinoma. Compared with semantic CT features and radiomics features, deep CT representations showed superior overall discriminative performance. This approach may serve as an adjunctive tool to molecular testing for pretreatment assessment in lung adenocarcinoma. However, the model showed inconsistent generalization performance across different molecular subtypes, with notably limited predictive efficacy for EGFR 19del and EGFR 19del+TP53 subtypes. Therefore, predictions for these categories should be interpreted with caution, and the model requires further validation in larger, multicenter, and standardized datasets before clinical application.
papers.summary: Ablation results revealed distinct performance among three input strategies. Compared with semantic CT features and radiomics features, deep CT representations showed superior overall discriminative performance. However, the model showed inconsistent generalization performance across different molecular subtypes, with notably limited predictive efficacy for EGFR 19del and EGFR 19del+TP53 subtypes.

papers.title: A transformer-based correction factor for critical heat flux prediction under non-uniform axial heating
papers.abstract: Critical heat flux (CHF) prediction under non-uniform axial heating remains challenging because the local thermal margin can depend on both local thermodynamic conditions and the upstream heating history. Traditional non-uniform CHF methods account for thermal-history effects through empirical correction factors, whereas the present work uses a transformer to learn this correction while retaining the conventional formulation. A neural network previously trained on a large uniform-heating CHF database is frozen and used to provide the baseline uniform-heating CHF prediction. A causal transformer model is then trained on non-uniform CHF data to predict a local correction factor from ordered axial sequences containing normalized axial position, equilibrium quality, and normalized heat-flux shape, with mass flux used as a global conditioning variable. The causal attention mask prevents downstream locations from contributing to the correction at each axial location. The model is evaluated using a benchmark non-uniform CHF database containing inlet-peaked, middle-peaked, outlet-peaked, and spike-like axial power profiles. The proposed correction is compared against the frozen uniform-heating neural network without correction, the same neural network with K 5 or Tong F corrections, and LUT-based predictions. Additional studies examine input ablation, axial-resolution transfer, training-seed robustness, and profile-family-held-out generalization. On the primary held-out test set, the transformer-based correction reduces prediction scatter relative to the classical correction-factor baselines; additional seed and profile-family-held-out tests indicate remaining sensitivity to training initialization and unseen profile families. Attention profiles at the transformer-selected minimum departure from nucleate boiling ratio (MDNBR) locations are analyzed as qualitative diagnostics of the learned sequence representation.

On the primary held-out test set, the transformer-based correction reduces prediction scatter relative to the classical correction-factor baselines; additional seed and profile-family-held-out tests indicate remaining sensitivity to training initialization and unseen profile families.

papers.title: Pyrolysis temperature-induced changes in physicochemical properties of rice husk-derived biochar: an assessment for CO2 retention potential
papers.abstract: The production of biochar from rice-husk biomass has shown significant potential to counter climate change and waste management issues. The current study assesses changes in elemental, structural and thermal characteristics of biochar produced at 380 °C, 400 °C, and 420 °C at a residence time of 2 h. The study also calculates the CO 2eq that is stored in biochar post-pyrolysis. The methodology adopted includes biochar production through pyrolysis, phase analysis, elemental analysis and CO 2eq calculations. Phase analysis revealed destruction of the cellulosic phase and development of amorphous silica following pyrolysis. CHNS analysis showed increasing carbon concentration together with decreasing H/C and O/C atomic ratios, indicating enhanced aromatic condensation and increasing carbon recalcitrance during thermal treatment. Proximate analysis demonstrated substantial devolatilization, reduction in moisture and volatile matter, and enrichment of stabilized carbonaceous fractions. Biochar yield decreased from 60.108 g at 380 °C to 40.153 g at 420 °C because of increasing thermal decomposition and volatilization losses. The calculated retained CO 2eq values ranged from 93.127 g for BC380 to 67.846 g for BC420, indicating that lower pyrolysis temperatures retained larger quantities of biomass-derived carbon despite relatively lower thermal maturity. However, the higher carbon concentration at elevated temperature did not result in greater total carbon retention because biochar yield decreased substantially with temperature. BC380 therefore retained the greatest absolute quantity of carbon despite having a lower carbon concentration than BC420. The study highlights the importance of optimizing pyrolysis conditions to maximize both carbon retention efficiency and carbon stability for sustainable biochar-mediated carbon sequestration applications.
papers.summary: The production of biochar from rice-husk biomass has shown significant potential to counter climate change and waste management issues. Phase analysis revealed destruction of the cellulosic phase and development of amorphous silica following pyrolysis. The study highlights the importance of optimizing pyrolysis conditions to maximize both carbon retention efficiency and carbon stability for sustainable biochar-mediated carbon sequestration applications.

papers.title: Experimental study of TPU and SEBS additively manufactured leaflets for novel aortic valve polymer TAVI prosthesis
papers.abstract: Background and Objective Transcatheter valve implantation is a cutting-edge technology for high and low risk patients with aortic stenosis. Bioprosthetic valves are limited due to several disadvantages as a long-term durability and structural valve degeneration. Polymeric aortic valve leaflet devices represent state-of-the-art technology to overcome limitations of bioprostheses. Nevertheless, more recent biocompatible and biostable polymers have revealed a significant potential. Additionally, 3D additive manufacturing opens new paths for patient-specific design of biomedical implants. Flexible polymers may not only mimic native aortic valve, but also may improve long-term durability. Polyurethanes and styrene polymers are promising materials for modern polymer valves. Nevertheless, mechanical properties of additive manufactured TPU or SEBS leaflets are not properly studied. Methods Experimental study of TPU and SEBS samples and aortic valve leaflets for novel aortic valve polymer TAVI prosthesis is presented. Tensile tests and compression tests of three types of FDM-printed samples with various filament alignments (axial alignment, transversal alignment, diagonal alignment) were performed. The results of tests confirmed that longitudinal axial alignment achieve a maximum stress compared to transversal and diagonal directions. Compressive tests of TPU and SEBS 3D-manufactured aortic valve leaflets with digital image correlation technology were performed. Young’s modulus and Poisson’s ratio were evaluated. Moreover, parameters of constitutive models were found. Results The TPU tensile specimen exhibits the highest stress/strain values at a speed of 100 mm/min, regardless of the filament alignment pattern. Slightly lower results are observed at a speed of 50 mm/min, which is likely associated with a wide range of plastic deformation. In the case of SEBS, a different pattern is observed: at 500 mm/min, it demonstrates high resistance to fracture, unlike TPU. A comparison of TPU and SEBS specimens at the same speeds and with the same alignment, based on maximum stress values, shows a minimal difference of 4% with the axial alignment at a speed of 50 mm/min; however, when comparing strains, the difference increases to 90%. The results of the compression experiment on aortic valve specimens made of TPU and SEBS at a speed of 30 mm/min showed that TPU force values for is considerably lower (4% of the maximum case), while for SEBS the spread increases to 20% of the maximum case. Conclusion SEBS aortic valve leaflets were shown to be stiffer than TPU. It can be a step for choice of stiffer/softer leaflets for patient-specific device. The proposed approach can help manufacturers in elaboration and manufacturing of new TAVI polymer devices design made of TPU and SEBS polymers for clinical applications.

The results of the compression experiment on aortic valve specimens made of TPU and SEBS at a speed of 30 mm/min showed that TPU force values for is considerably lower (4% of the maximum case), while for SEBS the spread increases to 20% of the maximum case. The proposed approach can help manufacturers in elaboration and manufacturing of new TAVI polymer devices design made of TPU and SEBS polymers for clinical applications.

papers.title: Pluronic F-127-functionalized magnetic ternary hybrid nanoparticles for co-delivery of paclitaxel and psoralen: a synergistic strategy to overcome multidrug resistance in triple-negative breast cancer
papers.abstract: A series of magnetic ternary hybrid nanoparticles were synthesized through the chemical integration of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs), poly (lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA), and lecithin, further functionalized with Pluronic F-127 (PEO-PPO-PEO). The ternary architecture afforded nanoparticles with well-defined spherical morphology, tunable particle sizes (69–166 nm), and high colloidal stability with zeta potentials exceeding −30 mV. Spectroscopic analyses, including FTIR, DSC, XRD and PLM, confirmed the successful incorporation of therapeutic agents within the ternary matrix, revealing their amorphous dispersion and strong intermolecular interactions with the carrier components. Magnetic characterization demonstrated retained superparamagnetic behavior, highlighting the magnetic responsiveness of the ternary system. In vitro studies against paclitaxel-resistant SUM159/TXR triple-negative breast cancer cells showed that the ternary nanoparticles enhanced cellular uptake, induced synergistic G0/G1 and G2/M cell cycle arrest, and promoted early-stage apoptosis. Co-encapsulation of psoralen and paclitaxel within the ternary hybrid framework amplified cytotoxic effects compared to individual formulations. In vivo evaluation using a xenograft tumor model confirmed superior tumor growth inhibition and minimal systemic toxicity. These results underscore the chemical design and structural optimization of Pluronic F-127-functionalized magnetic ternary hybrid nanoparticles as a promising strategy to overcome multidrug resistance and enhance therapeutic efficacy in aggressive cancers. This study constructed an Pluronic F-127-functionalized magnetic ternary hybrid delivery system co-loaded with superparamagnetic nanoparticles, PTX and PSO, achieving synergistic effects of magnetic targeting, hemotherapy and drug-resistance reversal, which provides a novel strategy for precise therapy of drug-resistant TNBC.

papers.title: Machine Vision-Based Defect Detection for Automotive Brake Pads: A Review of System Components, Image Processing Methods, and Applications
papers.abstract: Automotive brake pads are safety-critical components whose manufacturing quality directly affects braking reliability. Manual inspection is inefficient and susceptible to subjective judgment, whereas machine vision provides a non-contact and automated solution for defect detection. This article reviews machine vision-based inspection of automotive brake pads from three perspectives: system components, image processing methods, and industrial applications. The reviewed technologies include image acquisition hardware, conventional image processing, machine learning, deep learning, and their applications to contour, surface, character, and dimensional inspection. Existing methods are compared in terms of detection capability, interpretability, data dependence, computational cost, environmental robustness, and deployment suitability.The literature shows that conventional image processing remains effective under stable imaging conditions, while deep learning offers stronger feature representation and adaptability but requires representative datasets and greater computing resources. Current challenges include limited public datasets, inconsistent evaluation protocols, sensitivity to industrial variations, and the trade-off between accuracy and real-time performance. Future research should emphasize standardized datasets, lightweight models, few-shot learning, multimodal sensing, and integration with intelligent manufacturing systems. This review provides a reference for the development and industrial deployment of machine vision-based brake-pad inspection.

papers.title: Chitosan Nanoparticles Loaded with Alkaline-Released Rice Bran Hydroxycinnamic Acids: Physicochemical Characterisation, Antioxidant Activity and In Vitro Bioaccessibility
papers.abstract: Food-grade nanocarriers are widely investigated for improving the stability and bioaccessibility of labile phenolics. Ferulic and p-coumaric acid, the principal hydroxycinnamic acids of rice bran, were recovered from this rice milling by-product and encapsulated in chitosan nanoparticles by ionic gelation with sodium tripolyphosphate. Because they occur mainly esterified to cell-wall polysaccharides, aqueous ethanolic extraction, acid hydrolysis and alkaline hydrolysis were compared as release routes; alkaline hydrolysis gave the highest total phenolic content (4.58 mg gallic acid equivalents per g), cupric reducing capacity and by far the highest levels of both acids. This extract was encapsulated at three phenolic loadings; the 1.5 mg GAE/mL loading was the highest loading that remained nanoscale with polydispersity below 0.4. The resulting particles had a mean diameter of 184.7 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.35 and a zeta potential of +32.8 mV, retained on loading, and appeared under electron microscopy as discrete spheroidal particles of 100–200 nm that were absent from the blanks. Encapsulation efficiency was highest for this formulation, 34.6% by Folin–Ciocalteu, and 42.6% and 36.4% for p-coumaric and ferulic acid by UHPLC-DAD. A synthetic mixture matched to the extract was encapsulated more efficiently (52.3% and 45.3%, respectively), supporting an inhibitory effect of the extract matrix. FTIR, XRD and TGA were consistent with entrapment, reduced crystallinity and altered thermal decomposition relative to chitosan. Per unit of phenolic content, the reducing capacity of the nanoparticles matched that of the free extract, so that encapsulation preserved intrinsic antioxidant activity. Under simulated digestion, intestinal phase recovery of both acids was approximately 4-fold that ofthe free extract (p < 0.001), with antioxidant recovery likewise being higher. Chitosan nanoparticles are therefore promising for valorising rice bran phenolics in functional foods and nutraceuticals.

papers.title: Synthesis, crystal structure, and characterization of a new crystalline berberine–2-sulfobenzoate salt, integrating vibrational spectroscopy and quantum chemical investigation
papers.abstract: A hydrothermal crystallization screen was conducted to expand the solid-form landscape of berberine. Hydrolysis of saccharin under the applied conditions produced 2-sulfobenzoic acid, leading to the formation of a new crystalline berberine–2-sulfobenzoate salt (BER–SBA). Single-crystal X-ray diffraction established a 1:1 salt structure stabilized by C–H•••O interactions between berberine and sulfobenzoate ions and O–H•••O interactions between neighboring sulfobenzoate units. Agreement between the experimental and simulated powder X-ray diffraction patterns confirmed the phase identity of the bulk material. BER–SBA exhibited a higher differential scanning calorimeter onset temperature than the investigated berberine chloride sample (257.6 °C ± 0.5 °C) and underwent single-step decomposition after melting, indicating greater apparent thermal robustness up to the melting transition. FT–Raman spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations using a 1:2 molecular cluster provided complementary insight into the local intermolecular interactions. The Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM), reduced-density-gradient, natural bond orbital, and molecular electrostatic potential analyses supported the hydrogen-bonding and charge-transfer network associated with intermolecular stabilization within the modeled assembly. Frontier-orbital analysis further indicated that salt formation altered the calculated electronic properties of the system. Furthermore, molecular docking demonstrated favorable binding affinities against 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A (HMG-CoA) reductase, mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), and Nrf2 targets, respectively. Overall, the crystallographic, thermal, spectroscopic, and computational results establish BER–SBA as a distinct crystalline berberine salt and provide a molecular-level understanding of its solid-state stabilization. These findings support BER–SBA as a promising solid form for further pharmaceutical evaluation, particularly with respect to hygroscopicity and formulation performance.

papers.title: Оптимізація режиму живлення та густоти посіву як фактор підвищення якості зерна кукурудзи
papers.abstract: Мета. Визначити особливості формування хімічного складу зерна гібридів кукурудзи різних груп стиглості за оптимізованої густоти посіву та сумісного застосування мінеральних добрив і біопрепарату Блу N в агрокліматичних умовах Центрального Лісостепу України. Методи. Дослідження проводили впродовж 2024–2026 рр. на базі СТОВ «Любарецьке» Київської області на посівах гібридів кукурудзи P9255 та P8436. Площа облікової ділянки становила 33 м², дослід закладено з чотирикратною повторністю за послідовного багатоярусного розміщення варіантів. Схема досліду передбачала застосування мінеральних добрив у нормах N60P45K45, N90P60K60, N120P90K90 та N150P120K120 у поєднанні з позакореневим внесенням біопрепарату на основі азотфіксувальної бактерії Methylobacterium symbioticum у фазу 5–6 листків і варіювання густоти стояння рослин (60, 70 та 80 тис. рослин/га). Результати. Встановлено залежність вмісту крохмалю та сирого протеїну в зерні від генотипових особливостей гібридів, густоти стояння рослин і системи удобрення. У гібрида P8436 вміст крохмалю становив 70,90–73,30 %, а його вихід складав 7,05–10,19 т/га, а у гібрида P9255 відповідні показники становили 70,15–72,50 % та 7,56–10,18 т/га. Виявлено, що збільшення густоти посіву від 60 до 70 тис. росл./га сприяло підвищенню вмісту крохмалю у більшості варіантів, тоді як подальше загущення до 80 тис. росл./га супроводжувалося його певним зниженням. Водночас максимальний вихід крохмалю з одиниці площі у гібрида P8436 (10,19 т/га) формувався за густоти 80 тис. росл./га, а у гібрида P9255 (10,18 т/га) – за густоти 70 тис. росл./га на фоні N150P120K120 у поєднанні з азотфіксатором. Встановлено, що вміст сирого протеїну в зерні P8436 становив 8,35–10,05 %, а P9255 складав 8,65–10,35 %. При цьому його найвищі показники (10,05 та 10,35% відповідно) забезпечувало поєднання густоти 60 тис. росл./га з внесенням максимальної норми добрив і азотфіксатора. Підтверджено, що підвищення рівня мінерального живлення у поєднанні з азотфіксатором сприяло накопиченню сирого протеїну в зерні обох гібридів. Висновки. Доведено, що підвищення рівня мінерального живлення у поєднанні з азотфіксатором сприяло збільшенню вмісту сирого протеїну в зерні обох гібридів. Визначено, що оптимізація густоти стояння рослин та системи мінерально-біологічного живлення забезпечувала диференційоване формування якісних показників зерна залежно від генотипу гібрида. Виявлено, що P9255 характеризувався дещо вищим вмістом сирого протеїну, тоді як P8436 – вищою концентрацією крохмалю та максимальним його виходом.

papers.title: Injectable Hydrogels for Tissue Engineering: From Injectable Biomimetic Matrices to Organoid and In Situ Regeneration
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Hydrogel injectables mark a revolutionizing step forward for the field of regenerative medicine, as these biomaterials offer a minimally invasive alternative for the repair and reconstruction of tissues and organs.By mimicking the 3D microenvironment of the body, these biomaterials have successfully eliminated the need for surgical intervention, thus reducing the overall cost of healthcare and the rate of patient morbidity.The recent literature on the subject, as reported for the period of 2024-2026, has been focused on the development of hydrogels with enhanced biological and physiochemical properties that mimic the natural extracellular matrix (ECM) of the body.The current review article will discuss the current state of the art for the field of injectable hydrogels, with a special emphasis on the recent advances made with the development of novel and sophisticated hydrogel biomaterials.The different cross-linking mechanisms for the development of these biomaterials will be discussed, including the recent advances made with the development of novel cross-linking mechanisms for the gelation of these biomaterials under physiological conditions.The recent advances made with the encapsulation and co-delivery of cells will also be discussed, including the impact of these biomaterials on the proliferation and differentiation of stem cells.The recent literature on the subject will be analysed for the different applications of these biomaterials for the repair and reconstruction of various tissues and organs, including the recent advances made with the development of injectable in situ organoids and mini-tissues.The recent limitations and future scope for the field of injectable hydrogels will also be discussed.

papers.title: Bacterial–fungal shifts and functional reprogramming in CDI: insights from matched metagenomic and metatranscriptomic profiling
papers.abstract: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a leading cause of antibiotic-associated diarrhea, yet most microbiome studies have focused on bacterial composition, overlooking fungal contributions and transcriptionally active functions. Here, we applied matched metagenomic (MG) and metatranscriptomic (MT) sequencing to diarrheal stool from 100 adults (50 CDI+, 50 CDI−) to characterize taxonomic structure, functional potential and expression, predicted metabolites, and bacterial–fungal interactions. CDI− samples exhibited relatively greater taxonomic evenness, whereas CDI+ samples showed relatively higher MT KEGG Ortholog richness, indicating broader transcriptional activity. Beta diversity analyses demonstrated significant separation by CDI status, strongest in MT functional profiles. CDI+ microbiomes were enriched for opportunistic and transcriptionally active taxa, including C. difficile , Lactococcus cremoris , Nitratidesulfovibrio vulgaris , and fungi such as Candida albicans and Nakaseomyces glabratus , while CDI− communities were relatively enriched for obligate anaerobic commensals (e.g., Faecalibacterium , Roseburia , Subdoligranulum ). Functionally, CDI+ communities were relatively enriched in transport, stress-response, motility, quorum sensing, and amino acid metabolism pathways, whereas CDI− retained core metabolic functions. Network analyses identified significant enrichment of fungal-commensal co-exclusion relationships in the CDI+ metatranscriptomic network relative to CDI-, and predicted metabolites implicated bile acid disruption and lipid remodeling. Together, these findings define CDI as a trans-kingdom, functionally reprogrammed ecosystem and highlight the importance of integrating fungal ecology and transcriptional activity in CDI pathogenesis.

papers.title: Dietary butyrate alleviates high-fat diet-induced colonic mucosal impairment accompanied by increased gut-derived indole-3-acetic acid and enhanced PPARγ signaling
papers.abstract: Introduction High-fat diet (HFD) induces intestinal barrier impairment, associated with gut microbiota dysbiosis, endotoxin translocation and metabolic dysfunction. Dietary butyrate has been reported to improve intestinal homeostasis, but the underlying mechanism remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate the effects of dietary butyrate on HFD-induced colonic mucosal dysfunction and to explore underlying mechanisms with respect to the role of gut microbiota and its metabolites. Methods Male APOE*3-Leiden.CETP mice, a well-established translational model for diet-induced metabolic dysfunction, were fed an HFD with or without 5% sodium butyrate. Metabolic phenotypes, plasma lipopolysaccharide (LPS), colonic histology, inflammatory responses, and tight junction-associated changes were assessed. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) was performed in antibiotic-treated recipient mice to assess the contribution and transferability of butyrate-shaped gut microbiota. Cecal metagenomic sequencing and LC/MS-based colonic indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) measurement were performed. Caco-2 cells were used to assess the direct effects of sodium butyrate and IAA on enterocytes and to determine, through pioglitazone treatment and PPARγ knockdown, whether PPARγ mediates IAA-induced enterocyte responses. Results Dietary butyrate induced favorable changes in multiple colonic barrier-associated parameters, including improved colonic architecture, lower circulating LPS levels, decreased Tnf-a and Il-1b expression, and increased CLDN2, Reg-family, and PPARγ expression in the colon. In addition, butyrate reduced body weight gain, fat mass accumulation and improved glucose metabolism. FMT from butyrate-treated donors partially reproduced these beneficial effects in HFD-fed recipients. Metagenomic analysis showed enrichment of Bacteroidota and Bacteroides , particularly B. uniformis and B. thetaiotaomicron , accompanied by increased colonic IAA levels. In Caco-2 cells, IAA increased the expression of PPARγ, Reg4 , and CLDN2. While PPARγ agonist pioglitazone mimicked the upregulation of REG4 and CLDN2 expression by IAA, siRNA-induced PPARγ knockdown attenuated IAA-induced REG4 and CLDN2 upregulation. Conclusion Dietary butyrate improves colonic mucosal homeostasis under HFD feeding, accompanied by gut microbial remodeling and increased colonic IAA levels. Together with the PPARγ-dependent epithelial response to IAA observed in Caco-2 cells, these findings suggest a potential mechanistic framework linking butyrate-associated microbial changes, IAA metabolism, and epithelial PPARγ signaling.

papers.title: Thermal sculpting of nanoconfined single-atom cavities enables urea electrosynthesis with near-unity selectivity
papers.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic urea synthesis from CO 2 and NO 3 – offers a sustainable alternative to energy-intensive industrial methods, yet precise C–N coupling remains hindered by kinetic mismatches between the reduction reactions. Here, we report a strategy leveraging programmable Zn-node gasification to thermally sculpt 1.5–1.8 nm cavities within zeolitic imidazolate frameworks, hosting atomically dispersed Cu–N 4 sites. Thermal transformation creates size-matched nanoconfined environments for selective catalysis. An optimal confinement metric descriptor (9.64) is introduced as a predictive parameter, correlating cavity geometry with local electric-field and Cu d-band modulation. This design stabilizes *CO and *NO intermediates, effectively suppressing parasitic reactions and lowering C–N coupling barriers. Consequently, the catalyst delivers a urea yield of 71.32 g g cat –1 h –1 with 98.9% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in gas diffusion cells. Pilot-scale testing demonstrates stable operation over 300 h with an FE of 90%, establishing nanoconfinement as a design principle for competitive-performance urea electrosynthesis.

papers.title: Environmentally friendly lignin-bonded wood-based composites for thermal energy storage in buildings
papers.abstract: This study developed a fully bio-based composite consisting of sodium lignosulfonate, a water-soluble lignin derivative (Lig), wood fibre (WdF), and a phase change material (PCM) for building applications. WdFs formed the structural matrix, methyl palmitate (MeP) provided latent heat storage, and lignin served as a renewable binder and stabilizing agent. The composite was designed to combine effective thermal energy storage and enhanced resistance to biological degradation while maintaining its mechanical and physical integrity. The developed Lig@WdF/MeP board had a low density of approximately 355 kg m −3 and an internal bond strength of 0.037 MPa. DSC analysis revealed a melting temperature of 25.8 °C and a melting enthalpy of 95.9 J g −1 , confirming its suitability for passive thermal regulation. The incorporation of MeP increased the thermal conductivity from 0.091 ± 0.005 W m −1 K −1 for Lig@WdF to 0.118 ± 0.006 W m −1 K −1 for Lig@WdF/MeP. The composite retained 98.9% of its initial melting enthalpy after 500 thermal cycles and exhibited no visible MeP leakage or measurable mass loss. During the heating stage of the thermoregulation test, Lig@WdF/MeP reduced the maximum temperature by approximately 3 °C compared with the reference board. The composite exhibited strong biological resistance across all evaluated organisms. Termite survival decreased markedly from 74.7% in the control specimens to 5.2% in Lig@WdF/MeP. Similarly, all Hylotrupes bajulus larvae introduced into Lig@WdF/MeP specimens were found dead at the end of the test, while radiographic examination revealed an almost complete absence of larval galleries. After eight weeks of mould exposure, Lig@WdF/MeP received a rating of 1, compared with 5 for the control specimens, confirming substantially reduced mould development. These findings demonstrate that Lig@WdF/MeP integrates heat storage, low density, structural integrity, and biological resistance within a single lignin-bonded wood composite, offering a sustainable solution for next-generation, lightweight, non-structural building-envelope components.

papers.title: Transfer Learning Based Mechanical Reliability Prediction of Smart Sustainable Marine Composite Materials Under Cyclic Loading
papers.journal: The International Journal of Maritime Engineering
papers.abstract: For offshore applications, smart sustainable marine composites offer excellent strength and corrosion resistance;nevertheless, cyclic stress causes increasing deterioration. This research proposes a transfer learning-based model for predicting the mechanical reliability of smart sustainable marine composite materials under cyclic loading. Composite laminates reinforced with sustainable fibers and a bio-based polymer matrix were fabricated and experimentally characterized through tensile, flexural, and fatigue tests. Damage evolution and failure mechanisms were analyzed using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), while dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) and digital image correlation (DIC) were employed to assess stiffness degradation and strain distribution. The optimized composite achieved 78.6 MPa tensile strength and 118.5 MPa flexural strength at 40% fiber volume fraction (FVF), with 55.3% residual strength retention after 75,000 cycles. The transfer learning model attained R2 (0.98) and Root mean square error (RMSE) (2.84 MPa), enabling accurate reliability prediction with limited data. Overall, the proposed model supports durable and reliable offshore marine composite structural design.

papers.title: Lithium-salt anion regulation of ion transport and interfacial stability in PVDF-HFP/PAN/LLZTO composite polymer electrolytes
papers.abstract: Introduction The growing demand for safer and longer-lasting lithium-ion batteries has highlighted the limitations of conventional liquid electrolytes, particularly their susceptibility to oxidative decomposition and interfacial degradation. Composite polymer electrolytes (CPEs) offer a promising alternative for improving lithium-ion transport and interfacial stability. Methods In this study, poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene)/polyacrylonitrile (PVDF-HFP/PAN) was employed as the polymer matrix, with Ta-substituted lithium lanthanum zirconate (LLZTO) incorporated as an inorganic ceramic filler. Lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI) and lithium difluoro(oxalato)borate (LiODFB) were separately introduced to investigate the effects of lithium-salt anions on the structural, mechanical, and electrochemical properties of the resulting CPEs. Results At a salt loading of 30 wt%, the LiTFSI-based electrolyte (PSI 30%) achieved an ionic conductivity of 6.08 × 10 −4 S cm −1 , a tensile strength of approximately 8.5 MPa, and a Li + transference number of 0.58, outperforming the LiODFB-based electrolyte (PFB 30%) in mechanical strength and lithium-ion transport. The LiFePO 4 /PSI 30%/Li cell delivered discharge capacities of 162.61 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C and 107.14 mAh g −1 at 1 C. After 100 cycles at 0.1 C, the discharge capacity remained above 159 mAh g −1 , corresponding to approximately 98% capacity retention. Discussion These findings suggest that lithium-salt anion selection plays an important role in regulating ionic conductivity, mechanical integrity, and electrochemical performance within PVDF-HFP/PAN/LLZTO composite electrolytes. The LiTFSI-based system exhibits more favorable overall performance, providing useful insights into the design of composite polymer electrolytes for lithium-metal batteries.

papers.title: Treatment Outcomes in Chronic Osteomyelitis: Clinical, Microbiological, and Imaging Predictors - A Systematic Review
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: Chronic osteomyelitis is a persistent bone infection in which microbial biofilm, necrotic bone, impaired vascularity, soft-tissue compromise, and structural defects complicate durable eradication.Contemporary management combines radical debridement, deep microbiological sampling, systemic and local antimicrobial therapy, dead-space management, skeletal stabilization, and soft-tissue reconstruction.Despite these advances, treatment outcomes remain heterogeneous.Objective: To systematically evaluate treatment outcomes in adult chronic osteomyelitis and determine how clinical characteristics, microbiological findings, and conventional or advanced imaging parameters influence infection eradication, recurrence, wound complications, reoperation, functional recovery, and limb preservation.Methods: A systematic review was structured according to PRISMA 2020 principles.MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL were considered together with citation and reference-list searching.Primary adult studies reporting chronic osteomyelitis treatment outcomes in relation to clinical, microbial, anatomical, reconstructive, or imaging characteristics were eligible.Searching identified 2,470 records.After removal of 521 duplicates, 1,949 titles and abstracts were screened, 207 full-text reports were assessed, and 17 studies were retained for qualitative synthesis.Quantitative meta-analysis was not performed because of heterogeneity in anatomical sites, disease classification, surgical strategies, antimicrobial carriers, follow-up periods, and definitions of cure.Results: Treatment outcomes differed according to disease phenotype and therapeutic strategy.Single-stage specialist protocols reported infection-eradication rates of approximately 85-94%, whereas recurrence exceeded 20% in several complex or microbiologically difficult cohorts.Among 100 Cierny-Mader III-IV cases treated with standardized singlestage excision and local gentamicin delivery, 94% remained infection-free after a mean follow-up of more than six years.In contrast, a 93-patient cohort treated with antibiotic-loaded resorbable beads had 22.6% recurrence.Local antibiotic carrier properties influenced both clinical and radiological outcomes: in a 359-patient comparison, recurrence was 11.2% with calcium-sulphate pellets versus 4.4% with a calcium-sulphate/hydroxyapatite carrier, while radiological bone-void filling was 40.0% and 73.9%, respectively.Clinical predictors of poorer outcome included smoking, peripheral vascular compromise, open-injury-related disease, repeated previous treatment, compromised host status, and complex soft-tissue reconstruction.Pseudomonas aeruginosa, non-fermenting Gram-negative bacilli, polymicrobial infection, and resistant organisms were repeatedly associated with greater treatment difficulty.Imaging increasingly influenced prognosis by improving definition of resection boundaries.In a 70-patient 2025 cohort, recurrence was 35% after radiograph-guided osteotomy compared with 10% after MRI guidance and 5% after SPECT guidance.A 2026 MRI-radiomics model combining clinical and imaging variables achieved an external-validation AUC of 0.910 for recurrence prediction, while PET/MRI-enhanced mapping was associated with recurrence of 10.0% versus 35.7% with a conventional imaging pathway.Conclusion: Successful treatment of chronic osteomyelitis depends on the interaction between surgical source control, host biology, pathogen characteristics, bone and soft-tissue reconstruction, and accurate definition of disease extent.Clinical and microbiological risk factors remain important, but emerging imaging evidence suggests that anatomical mapping and quantitative imaging may substantially improve individualized treatment planning.Prognostic assessment should therefore integrate clinical, microbiological, reconstructive, and imaging variables rather than relying on any single marker of disease severity.

papers.title: Development and evaluation of a simplified Illinois soil nitrogen test
papers.abstract: Since 1960, alkali-hydrolyzable nitrogen (N) has been utilized to determine potentially mineralizable N in soil as a more rapid alternative to biological incubations. This fraction can be estimated by a diffusion technique commonly known as the Illinois Soil N Test (ISNT-1), which involves a 5-h diffusion with sodium hydroxide (NaOH) in a 473-mL widemouth Mason jar sealed with a lid modified to support a Petri dish containing boric acid (H 3 BO 3 ) solution for absorption of ammonia (NH 3 ) liberated during heating on a commercial griddle at 48–50°C. A simplified version of the method (ISNT-2) was developed and evaluated that avoids the need for lid modification and the use of a griddle, in which 2 g of soil is treated with 10 mL of 2 M NaOH in a 237-mL Mason jar and incubated at 25 ± 1°C for 24 h followed by titrimetric determination of the diffused NH 3 -N. Comparative studies using 18 Illinois soils from N response trials showed (i) a strong correlation between the two versions of the ISNT ( R = 0.99); (ii) consistent ratios of ISNT-2:ISNT-1 that ranged from 0.39 to 0.44; and (iii) equal effectiveness in differentiating sites where fertilizer N response was likely (> 25%), possible (0–25%), and unlikely (0%). In comparison to the original technique, the ISNT-2 has the advantages of improving reproducibility and increasing sample throughput for routine soil testing as required for site‐specific N management.

papers.title: Extending biostasis to pregnancy: defining an unexamined biomedical problem
papers.abstract: Our review of the scientific literature identified no studies directly addressing the cryopreservation of a pregnant individual or the preservation of an embryo or fetus in utero , despite the routine use of cryopreservation for embryos, oocytes, and sperm in reproductive medicine and the enrollment of individuals of reproductive age in biostasis organizations. This paper defines this unexamined problem by synthesizing evidence from cryobiology, reproductive and developmental biology, clinical medicine, bioethics, and law. It develops a conceptual framework that treats the pregnant individual and conceptus as one physical body containing two biologically distinct systems, and distinguishes established evidence, testable hypotheses, and speculative scenarios. Two falsifiable hypotheses follow: that cryoprotectant delivery across the maternal–fetal interface is rate-limited under whole-body perfusion, and that the resulting maternal–fetal concentration gradient varies with gestational age. The paper analyzes four preservation scenarios, the clinical precedent of somatic support after maternal brain death, and the consent, surrogate decision-making, and jurisdictional questions these scenarios raise. Membership data from three biostasis organizations indicate that roughly one in eight members of organizations reporting age data is a woman of reproductive age. The paper does not propose clinical protocols or claim feasibility. It sets out a prioritized research agenda and recommendations for organizational policy in a previously unexplored area of biomedical research.

The paper does not propose clinical protocols or claim feasibility.

papers.title: Evaluation of the apparent temperature-control contribution of solid-solid phase change materials to low-temperature crack resistance of asphalt
papers.abstract: The temperature-control performance of low-temperature polyurethane solid-solid phase change materials (LPSP) can significantly improve the low-temperature performance of asphalt pavements. However, studies evaluating the low-temperature performance of LPSP-modified asphalt considering the temperature-control effect remain limited. Moreover, the quantitative contribution of the temperature-control effect to low-temperature performance improvement has not yet been clarified, and the relationship between temperature-control performance and low-temperature performance improvement remains to be further elucidated. In this study, the low-temperature performance of LPSP-modified asphalt considering the temperature-control effect was evaluated using dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA). A new method combining constant-temperature bending beam rheometer (BBR) and dynamic-cooling DMA tests was proposed to evaluate the apparent temperature-control contribution of LPSP to the improvement in low-temperature performance. The apparent temperature-control contribution rate was defined as (Δ T DMA − Δ T BBR )/Δ T DMA × 100%, where Δ T BBR and Δ T DMA denote the improvements in critical cracking temperature obtained from BBR and DMA tests, respectively. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) was further employed to simulate the temperature-control performance of LPSP-modified asphalt and investigate its relationship with the resulting low-temperature performance improvement. The results indicate that the optimal low-temperature performance was achieved at a polytetramethylene ether glycol (PTMEG) mass fraction of 75%, a particle size of 30 mesh, and an LPSP content of 9 wt%. As the LPSP content increased from 1.5 wt% to 9 wt%, the apparent temperature-control contribution rate increased from 60.5% to 76.4%. Within the investigated PMA75 composition range, the temperature-control performance of LPSP-modified asphalt exhibited a strong linear correlation with the apparent improvement in critical cracking temperature (R² = 0.9907).

The results indicate that the optimal low-temperature performance was achieved at a polytetramethylene ether glycol (PTMEG) mass fraction of 75%, a particle size of 30 mesh, and an LPSP content of 9 wt%.

papers.title: Development of efficient betaine-based natural deep eutectic solvents for metal leaching from waste printed circuit boards
papers.abstract: Abstract The rapid growth of electronic waste has intensified the need for sustainable approaches for metal recovery from waste printed circuit boards (WPCBs). In this study, betaine-based natural deep eutectic solvents (NADES) were developed as lixiviants for metal extraction from WPCBs. Betaine (BET) was used as the hydrogen bond acceptor, while ethane-1,2-diol (ETD), propane-1,2-diol (PPD), and butane-1,2-diol (BTD) served as hydrogen bond donors (HBDs) to investigate the influence of HBD structure on the physicochemical properties and leaching performance of the resulting NADES. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) indicated intermolecular interactions between BET and the diol-based HBDs, while thermogravimetric analysis/derivative thermogravimetry (TGA/DTG) showed pronounced mass-loss-rate maxima above 240 °C for all three NADES. Rheological measurements revealed Newtonian flow behaviour, with viscosity increasing with increasing diol chain length; BET:ETD exhibited the lowest viscosity (50.1 mPa·s) at 20 °C. Under the experimental conditions of 75 °C, 6 h, 1.0 M H 2 O 2 , 500 rpm, and a solid-to-liquid ratio of 1:20, BET:ETD achieved leaching efficiencies of 99.3% for Cu, 99.5% for Pb, 97.8% for Fe, 95.4% for Al, 90.5% for Sn, and 73.9% for Ti. Kinetic analysis based on the shrinking core model and activation energy evaluation indicated a mixed-control mechanism involving interfacial reaction and diffusion processes. SEM, XRD, and FTIR analyses further indicated substantial dissolution of metallic phases while the polymeric and glass-fibre matrix was largely preserved. Overall, the results demonstrate that betaine-based NADES, most especially BET:ETD, offer tunable physicochemical properties and effective metal-leaching performance for WPCB recycling.

papers.title: Charge Transfer with a Spin. II: A Framework for Diabatization Which Localizes Charge and Spin
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abstract: Abstract We investigate a diabatization procedure that localizes charges (in real space) and localizes spins (in spin space) for open-shell systems that exhibit charge transfer in the presence of spin–orbit coupling. The procedure is applied to a two-state crossing between pairs of Kramers-restricted doublet states (which can also be considered effectively a four-state crossing). To generate the relevant diabatic states, we employ a two-step optimization over complex-unitary rotations that sequentially maximizes dipole and spin moments through iterative Jacobi sweeps; the resulting update rules are effectively equivalent to those of approximate joint diagonalization applied to charge and spin. The method converges rapidly and yields smooth diabatic potential energy surfaces that preserve dipole and spin properties (e.g., a smoothly varying spin quantization axis) along the reaction coordinate while maintaining time-reversal symmetry.

papers.title: Irradiation-induced amplification of electric fields at oxide interfaces as revealed by correlative DPC-STEM and DFT
papers.abstract: Heterointerfaces are ubiquitous in modern devices, found in technologies ranging from microelectronics to structural components for energy applications. Many of these emerging technologies are found in applications such as satellites, batteries, and next generation nuclear reactors, that are subject to harsh environments. In some scenarios, multiple extreme conditions, such as irradiation and corrosion, act on the material simultaneously. Extending the lifetime of these technologies is dependent on a detailed understanding of how their component materials platforms and interfaces respond in extreme environments, where irradiation and corrosion may couple in unique ways, distinct from corrosion under ambient conditions. Oxides, which form readily over metal underlayers, can act as protective coatings; enhancing the robustness of oxide overlayers to protect underlying metal alloys is a potential avenue towards corrosion mitigation. Here we study the impact of irradiation-induced non-equilibrium defects on charge segregation and electric fields at and near multi-phase oxide heterointerfaces. We perform a detailed study of irradiated Fe2O3-Cr2O3 thin film heterostructures using first-principles DFT electronic structure modeling paired with 4D-STEM DPC and EELS techniques to measure nanoscale changes in electric fields. Our results show clear evidence that irradiation drives substantial modulation of interfacial electric fields that can be tailored by controlling the atomistic chemical structure of the oxide interface. We show that irradiation can selectively induce built-in electric fields, thereby altering their direction; this suggests a pathway to engineering protective oxide heterostructure overlayers that can electrically control the spatial distribution of defects, with significant implications for the design of corrosion-resistant materials for extreme environments.

papers.title: Causality in liquid water as a hallmark of emergent glassy dynamics
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract: In molecular liquids such as water, time-delayed influences between microscopic or mesoscopic variables are typically probed using time-correlation functions, which are symmetric under detailed balance and therefore blind to dynamical asymmetries. Here, we characterize water’s dynamics using a causal inference metric that captures asymmetric couplings between collective variables. Analyzing equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations at ambient conditions and in the high-density liquid (HDL) regime of supercooled water, we uncover pronounced asymmetries in the couplings between orientational and translational degrees of freedom across multiple time and length scales. At room temperature, rotational modes exert a modest directional influence on translational dynamics. In contrast, in the supercooled HDL regime, translational motions emerge as the primary drivers of the dynamics, suggesting facilitation-like relaxation mechanisms characteristic of glassy systems. These results reveal a qualitative reorganization of dynamical couplings across thermodynamic conditions, implying that molecular liquids at thermal equilibrium can exhibit an emergent directionality in their fluctuation couplings. As a consequence, our analysis reveals that external perturbations acting on specific degrees of freedom can induce a stronger arrow of time in the causal relations between translational and orientational modes.

papers.title: Scalable and Printable Three-Phase Ion Gel Electrocatalyst Device
papers.abstract: Abstract Scalable electrocatalyst systems that are mechanically robust, thermally stable, and compatible with large-area manufacturing are critical for advancing next-generation electrochemical technologies. Here, we present an ion gel-based electrocatalyst device platform capable of stable operation at elevated temperatures beyond the practical limits of many conventional polymer electrolyte systems. The device consists of a polybenzimidazole (PBI)- and 1-hexyl-3-methylimidazolium trifluoromethanesulfonate ([HMIM][OTf])-based ion gel integrated with Au electrodes and graphene- or carbon nanotube-supported Pt catalyst layers, demonstrating compatibility with scalable and solution-processable fabrication methods. Thermogravimetric analysis and infrared spectroscopy confirmed thermal stability beyond 200 °C without significant structural degradation. To demonstrate electrocatalytic operation at elevated temperature, formic acid electrocatalytic decomposition was investigated using formic acid electrooxidation and hydrogen evolution as the half-cell reactions. Under continuous 4 mol % formic acid gas flow at temperatures near 100 °C, the devices sustained stable steady-state electrocatalysis over multiday operation without observable ion gel degradation or device failure. Kinetic analysis revealed that open-circuit behavior differs substantially from conventional gas-phase thermocatalytic formic acid decomposition on Pt, whereas closed-circuit operation followed the expected kinetic trends for Au-limited formic acid electrooxidation suggesting that the observed rates were not governed solely by mass transport. These results demonstrate that ion gel-based electrocatalyst devices provide a thermally durable and manufacturing-compatible platform for elevated-temperature electrochemical applications.

papers.title: Composite bio-briquettes from bagasse and cotton stalks: Chemical, physico-mechanical and emissions analysis
papers.abstract: Biomass selection and characterization are critical in producing briquettes of high quality. The study investigated properties that influence performance of composite carbonized briquettes. Samples were made from cotton stalks, bagasse, bentonite clay, and molasses in proportions of 58.2 wt%, 31.7 wt%, 9.0 wt%, and 1.2 wt%, respectively. Laboratory tests were undertaken using elemental and thermogravimetric analyzers to determine ultimate and proximate analysis of residues and briquettes. A Fourier Transform Infrared spectrophotometer was used to obtain the structural composition of residues and scanning electron microscope to assess the morphology of briquettes. Water boiling test was undertaken following the ISO 19867-1:2018 standard to determine thermal efficiency and emissions of CO and PM2.5. Compounds in the ash were determined using an X-Ray Fluorescence spectrometer. Results showed volatile matter of 83.0, 80.8, and 24.5 wt% for cotton stalks, bagasse, and briquettes, respectively. Fixed carbon of residues was relatively low with cotton stalks at 14.0 wt% and bagasse at 15.5 wt%. The predominant structure was cellulose with 42.7% for cotton stalks and 68.8% for bagasse. Morphological analysis showed a porous heterogeneous structure having non uniform open pores with dimensions between 2 and 20. A high thermal efficiency of 86.4% and low burning rate of 2.66 g/min was registered. The emission rate was 0.14 g/min for CO and 13.29 mg/min for PM2.5. The major compounds found in ash were SiO2 at 51.6 wt% and Al2O3 at 20.5 wt%. The briquettes satisfied the ISO and WHO standards required for cooking and water heating applications using cookstoves.

Results showed volatile matter of 83.0, 80.8, and 24.5 wt% for cotton stalks, bagasse, and briquettes, respectively. The briquettes satisfied the ISO and WHO standards required for cooking and water heating applications using cookstoves.

papers.journal: Turbo Jurnal Program Studi Teknik Mesin
papers.abstract: Oil palm empty fruit bunch (OPEFB) fibers are promising as composite reinforcement because they are lightweight, widely available, environmentally friendly, and relatively low production costs. This study aimed to investigate the alkali treatment and volume fraction effects on the physical and mechanical properties of OPEFB fiber-reinforced composites. Reinforcement consisted of OPEFB fibers screened to 50 mesh, with polyester resin as the matrix and methyl ethyl ketone peroxide as the catalyst at a 100:1 resin-to-catalyst ratio. Fibers were alkali-treated using 4% NaOH for either 1 hour or 2 hours. Composites were fabricated with fiber volume fractions of 20% and 30%. An experimental program evaluated physical properties (density and water absorption) and mechanical properties (flexural strength and impact resistance). Results show that both fiber volume fraction and alkali treatment significantly affect the composites’ properties. The best performance was observed for the composite containing 20% fiber volume fraction treated with 4% NaOH for 2 hours, which achieved a flexural strength of 45.3 MPa and a water absorption of 0.65%.

papers.title: Valorization of mango by-products into prebiotic ingredients: a critical review on functional properties and gut microbiota modulation mechanisms
authors: L. T. Mohamad Arif Rahmat Teo
papers.abstract: Abstract The growing demand for sustainable functional ingredients has intensified interest in valorizing agro-industrial by-products as prebiotic sources. Mango ( Mangifera indica ) processing generates substantial residues, including peel, seed kernel, and pomace, which are rich in dietary fiber and polyphenols. This review critically evaluates the potential of mango by-products as prebiotic ingredients by integrating compositional characteristics, processing strategies, and mechanisms of gut microbiota modulation. Mango-derived substrates exhibit structural complexity due to the coexistence of polysaccharides and polyphenols, enabling multifunctional mechanisms beyond conventional carbohydrate-based prebiotics. Key components such as pectin, pectic oligosaccharides (POS), and resistant starch (RS) resist gastrointestinal digestion and undergo microbial fermentation, leading to short chain fatty acid (SCFA) production and bioactive metabolite formation. Polyphenol–microbiota interactions further contribute through biotransformation and cross-feeding mechanisms. Processing strategies significantly influence prebiotic functionality by modifying molecular structure and fermentability, although trade-offs between structural integrity and microbial accessibility remain. Despite promising functional properties, including gut barrier support and metabolic modulation, current evidence is largely derived from in vitro and animal studies, with limited human clinical validation. Overall, mango by-products represent promising but emerging prebiotic systems. Future research should focus on standardized processing, mechanistic validation, and well-designed clinical studies to support their application as functional food ingredients.

This review critically evaluates the potential of mango by-products as prebiotic ingredients by integrating compositional characteristics, processing strategies, and mechanisms of gut microbiota modulation. Future research should focus on standardized processing, mechanistic validation, and well-designed clinical studies to support their application as functional food ingredients.

papers.title: Early warning of PVC overheating in a simulated 10 kV cable trench using thermally induced particulate matter
papers.abstract: Thermally induced particulate matter (TIPM) may provide an indicator of abnormal cable-material heating before combustion. This study combines thermogravimetric analysis, a qualitative comparison with a particle counter, and sensor measurements in a 6 m simulated cable trench. The PVC sample lost approximately 1.6% of its mass below 200 °C. This observation is consistent with low-temperature volatile release but does not identify the emitted species or establish a particle-formation pathway. Five laser particle sensors (LPS), spaced 1 m apart, monitored end-source and central-source configurations at 100 °C–110 °C, 150 °C–160 °C, and 200 °C–210 °C. No sensor response was reported at 100 °C–110 °C in the trench tests. At the two higher temperature ranges, response onset depended on source position and distance. In the reported end-source test at 200 °C–210 °C, N1 responded at 18.31 min and the HCl sensor at 27 min, a difference of 8.69 min. This is a single-run comparison, not a validated lead time to ignition. The spatial response patterns support further evaluation of distributed particle sensing, while replication, quantitative detection thresholds, and field-interference testing are needed before deployment rules can be established.

papers.title: Intelligent prediction of mechanical properties of backfill materials using a PSO-optimized XGBoost model
papers.abstract: Abstract Backfill mining technology has been established as a primary method for achieving green and low-carbon coal mining. However, the mechanical properties of backfill materials are influenced by multiple parameters, accompanied by issues such as prolonged production cycles and high costs. To achieve rapid matching between the mechanical characteristics of backfill materials and actual working conditions, an intelligent prediction model was developed in this study using the XGBoost algorithm to predict the mechanical performance of backfill materials. First, a multifactor dataset was constructed based on laboratory experiments, and the optimal solution was identified through hyperparameter optimization via Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Accordingly, a PSO-XGBoost prediction model was designed to investigate the properties of backfill materials under various mixing ratios. Second, based on experimental data of backfill material proportions, the input features were selected as gangue content, gangue particle size, fly ash, cement, and fiber, while the uniaxial compressive strength, elastic energy index, and impact energy index were set as outputs. Finally, the coefficient of determination (R²), root mean square error (RMSE), and mean absolute error (MAE) were employed as evaluation metrics to assess the predictive performance of the model. Factors influencing the mechanical properties of backfill materials were also analyzed. The results demonstrated that the PSO-XGBoost model achieved coefficients of determination of 0.96846, 0.97814, and 0.96403 for predicting uniaxial compressive strength, elastic energy index, and impact energy index, respectively, exhibiting superior predictive performance compared to other models and enabling accurate prediction of the mechanical properties of gangue-cemented backfill materials. The findings contribute to facilitating the advancement of intelligent and green mining practices.

papers.title: Efficient removal of fusidic acid from aqueous solution using synthesized zinc magnesium aluminum layered double hydroxide adsorbent
papers.abstract: Pharmaceutical residues in the water have become a growing environmental concern because of their potential ecological and human health effects and their persistence. The Zn-Mg-Al layered double hydroxides (LDH) were prepared by the co-precipitation method, and their efficiency was tested as an adsorbent for the elimination of fusidic acid (FA) from aqueous solution. Characterization of the synthesized material was done by FTIR, SEM, XRD, EDS, BET, and TGA. The parameters affecting adsorption performance, such as pH, dosage of the adsorbent, contact time, initial concentration of FA and temperature, were investigated by batch adsorption experiments. The most efficient removal was obtained in 210 min at the optimum conditions of FA adsorbent dosage (1.25 g/L), agitation speed (250 rpm), concentration (20 mg/L), pH 5, and temperature (20 ± 1 °C), and showed the best agreement with the PSO model. Kinetic analysis suggested the PSO model best fitted the experimental data, while isotherm studies showed good agreement with the Freundlich model, indicating a heterogeneous adsorption behavior. Thermodynamic analysis shows that adsorption process was thermodynamically favorable. Besides, the reusability and structural stability of the adsorbent improved after calcination treatment, whereas the adsorption rate was slightly decreased. The results indicated that the Zn-Mg-Al LDH is a promising and economical adsorbent for the removal of pharmaceutical contaminants from aqueous stream.

papers.title: Multi-sensor Calibration Technology for Intelligent Connected Vehicles
papers.abstract: Multi-sensor fusion is fundamental to environment perception in intelligent connected vehicles, but its reliability depends on maintaining a consistent spatiotemporal reference among cameras, LiDAR, millimetre-wave radar, and IMU/GNSS. This review examines multi-sensor calibration from a vehicle life-cycle perspective, focusing on how calibration parameters drift, how miscalibration is detected, when recalibration should be triggered, how parameters are recovered online, how the vehicle should operate while calibration is uncertain, and how recovery should be verified. Intrinsic, extrinsic, and temporal parameters are distinguished from pairwise and joint calibration architectures, while temporal errors are further separated into fixed offsets and time-varying synchronisation effects. Calibration methods are organised by their constraint sources, including artificial targets, natural-scene structure, and motion consistency, with learning-based approaches treated as an implementation paradigm rather than a separate information source. The review further compares requirements across end-of-line production, research platforms, and in-service maintenance, showing that in-service accuracy should be defined by downstream functional tolerance. A major remaining challenge is online verification: existing residuals and consistency checks provide only indirect evidence, while accepted criteria linking calibration uncertainty to downstream safety margins are still lacking. Future research should integrate detection, recovery, degraded operation, and verification within a unified maintenance loop.

papers.title: Upgrading of scrap tire derived pyrolytic oils through catalytic oxidative desulphurization over iron tailored Tetrapak® based catalyst
papers.abstract: The upgrading of sulfur-rich pyrolytic oils derived from waste tires remains a major challenge for their utilization as alternative transportation fuels due to the presence of refractory thiophenic compounds. In this work, we reported the carbothermal production of a iron tailored catalyst produced by pyrolyzing waste aluminum containing contaminated food packaging (waste Tetrapak ® ). The catalytic activity of iron tailored catalyst was evaluated in the oxidative desulfurization of tire-derived pyrolytic oil containing 7139 ppm sulfur using a biphasic H₂O₂ system. The effects of reaction temperature, reaction time and catalyst loading were systematically investigated reaching a sulfur removal up to 57% at 100 °C after 6 h using a catalyst loading of up 5 wt%. The catalyst maintained stable activity after three consecutive cycles, while XPS and FESEM analyses after reaction evidenced partial oxidation and enlargement of iron nanoparticles.

papers.title: Influence of Glutaraldehyde on the Properties of Agar-Based Films
papers.abstract: Abstract Biopolymers have been used as alternatives to fossil-derived polymers. In this context, agar, a polysaccharide extracted from seaweed, has stood out due to its properties in the formulation of polymeric films. In this work, agar was used in combination with glycerol and glutaraldehyde to formulate polymeric films by the casting method with water as solvent. The films produced were characterized regarding their water interactions using swelling, solubility, and contact angle tests. Mechanical and physical properties were determined using a tensile test and thickness measurements. Optical microscopy was used to analyze the surface, and scanning electron microscopy was used to analyze the surface and cross-section of the films. Spectroscopic properties were obtained by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and ultraviolet–visible spectroscopy. Thermal degradation was determined by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). It was possible to produce polymeric films with a thickness of around 120 μm and mechanical properties like those found on low-density polyethylene, showing tensile strengths of 15–16 MPa. The solubility of the material was 42% and the swelling ranged between 349–555%, depending on the concentration of glutaraldehyde added to the film formulation of films. Adding glutaraldehyde altered the surface characteristics of the films while maintaining the other properties. However, no evidence of cross-linking reactions was found.

papers.title: Comprehensive Survey of Distributed Optimization: Challenges, Strategies, and Applications
papers.journal: Journal of Machine Learning and Information Security
papers.abstract: Distributed optimization plays an important role in multi-node collaborative computing and has developed rapidly in recent years, both in theory and applications. However, most classical distributed optimization algorithms are generally developed under idealized communication settings, which, to some extent, limit their applicability to practical systems with complex constraints. This survey aims to bridge the gap between theory and practice in distributed optimization by examining its theoretical foundations, recent progress, and major open challenges. Initially, we outline some theoretical breakthroughs regarding graph topologies, objective functions, and acceleration strategies. The discussion then turns to approaches for addressing practical constraints like stochastic noise, limited bandwidth, and asynchronous delays. Finally, we present several directions that are worth exploring in the future.

papers.title: Balancing the Performance Trade-off of Polymer Blends with Heterogeneously Dispersed Nanodomains via Reactive Processing
papers.abstract: Polymer blends are ubiquitous though there are persistent material-property trade-offs, due to the limitation of structural design. Here we report a reactive processing strategy that creates heterogeneously dispersed nano-domains (hDNs) of rubbery ethylene-acrylic ester-glycidyl methacrylate terpolymer (EGMA) in polyoxymethylene (POM) matrix. Pre-reactive blending of EGMA with poly (L-lactide) (PLLA) and subsequent melt processing with POM result in formation of the unique morphology, where PLLA serving as the leveraging forces for opposing uniform distribution via chemical bonds and macro-phase separation by physical associations. The resulting materials exhibited optimized mechanical performance impossible to be acquired with conventional counterparts. This work identifies herein innovates how reactive processing can regulate phase morphology while balancing the trade-off among toughness, ductility, strength and stiffness in multicomponent polymer blends, representing a paradigm shift in narrowing gap between structure and tailor-made property towards pilot plant scale. Polymer blends are ubiquitous though there are persistent material-property trade-offs, due to structural design. Here the authors design multicomponent polymers optimizing the material properties.
