papers.title: Spatiotemporal evolution and driving factors of green transformation in resource-based cities of Western China
papers.abstract: Western China’s resource-based cities (WRBCs) have characteristics of “resource dependence” and “development lag,” and all resource-based cities will face difficulty accomplishing green transformation (GT). This paper uses 39 samples of WRBCs from 2003 to 2021, identifying the sources of differentiation in GT in WRBCs through the Dagum Gini coefficient, Kernel density function, and spatial Durbin model. Furthermore, we analyze the driving factors and effects of GT. The results show that the overall GT of WRBCs assumes a fluctuating upward tendency. Interregional disparities are the primary source of differentiation in the GT of WRBCs, and absolute differences within the region are generally narrowing. The digital economy (DIG), agglomeration of productive service industries (SEV), urban industrial innovation (UINV), infrastructure level (IL), and GDP can promote GT. DIG and IL produce positive spillover effects promoting the adjacent region’s GT; however, economically developed regions, the siphoning effect occurs, which is adverse to the GT of the adjacent region. The results are still valid after a series of robustness tests. GT has a positive spatial spillover effect, with an effective spillover boundary of 400 km and a peak of 300 km. This study can support the quantitative for promoting GT and balancing regional inequality in resource-based cities.

papers.title: Dissecting the reciprocal association between cytoskeletal mechanics and senescence-associated phenotypes in human dermal fibroblasts
papers.abstract: Introduction Cellular mechanical properties play crucial roles in governing cellular functions, with their dynamic changes influenced by various factors including physiological and pathological states. Skin photoaging is closely linked to fibroblast senescence and extracellular matrix (ECM) dysfunction, yet the interplay between cellular senescence and cytoskeletal mechanics remains poorly understood. This study aimed to characterize cytoskeletal mechanical changes and explore whether maintaining F-actin cytoskeletal stability could attenuate senescent phenotypes in photoaged human dermal fibroblasts (HDFs). Methods A model of HDFs with senescence-associated phenotypes was established by ultraviolet B (UVB) irradiation. Micromechanical properties of UVB-irradiated HDFs were evaluated using integrated cellular, molecular, and biophysical approaches, encompassing the analysis of cellular apparent modulus, cell-mediated ECM contraction, and actin cytoskeletal contractile units. Latrunculin A (LAT-A) and Jasplakinolide (JASP) were employed for targeted remodeling of the F-actin cytoskeleton to evaluate their effects on cellular senescence-associated markers. Results UVB-irradiated HDFs with senescence-associated phenotypes exhibited reduced apparent Young’s modulus, impaired F-actin polymerization and organization, diminished myosin II regulatory light chain phosphorylation, and compromised collagen matrix contraction. Disruption of F-actin polymerization with LAT-A in young HDFs was accompanied by the appearance of cellular senescence markers, including upregulation of p21 and MMP1, downregulation of Lamin B1 and COL I. Conversely, stabilizing F-actin with JASP in UVB-exposed HDFs attenuated these changes, preserved spindle-shaped cellular morphology, and reduced the expression of senescence markers. Discussion Our findings confirm that UVB-induced senescence-associated phenotypes in HDFs are accompanied by impaired F-actin cytoskeletal mechanics, and pharmacological modulation of F-actin partially alters multiple senescence-associated markers. These findings provide theoretical evidence and potential intervention strategies to disrupt the establishment of the UVB-induced senescent phenotype in HDFs.

papers.title: Revisiting the MS paradox: automated 2.5D FLAIR segmentation and DTI microstructural profiling reveals dissociation between lesion burden and reference-like intralesional tract profiles
papers.abstract: Introduction Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reveals macroscopic lesion burden in multiple sclerosis (MS) but correlates poorly with clinical phenotype, a phenomenon known as the clinico-radiological paradox. While diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics assess microstructural damage, standard whole-lesion averaging may obscure microstructurally spared white matter within heterogeneous plaques. Methods We propose a fully automated, multimodal pipeline to identify and quantify reference-like intralesional segments (RLIS) within MS lesions (i.e., the cluster exhibiting maximum feature-space similarity to subject-specific, lesion-spared reference tissue). A modified 2.5D U-Net, developed and evaluated on a cohort of 75 MS patients (115 series), performed automated FLAIR lesion segmentation. In an independent cohort of 100 MS subjects, intralesional DTI metrics (FA and MD) were extracted along streamlines reconstructed via Constrained Spherical Deconvolution tractography. Unsupervised clustering algorithms, validated against a subject-specific, lesion-spared reference CST streamlines (internal capsule), identified operationally defined reference-like segments. Results The 2.5D U-Net achieved robust segmentation performance (DSC: 0.732, VC: 0.954), exhibited higher nominal metrics in a contextual benchmark comparison (DSC: 0.682, VC: 0.864). Across the clinical cohort, lesion count (11–131) and volume (0.54–57.3 mL) varied widely. Among the evaluated clustering methods, K-Means and Gaussian Mixture Models proved to be the most conservative, identifying median reference-like segment proportions of 26% and 22%, respectively. Crucially, the proportion of reference-like intralesional segments showed no significant monotonic association with macroscopic lesion volume or count. Conclusion This automated framework successfully integrates robust deep learning-based lesion segmentation with tract-specific analysis to quantify the proportion of reference-like intralesional segments. The observed dissociation between overall lesion burden and RLIS suggests that this index serves as a promising candidate metric for exploring microstructural features that may contribute to the clinico-radiological paradox.

papers.title: Adaptation and psychometric properties of the life conditions scale in university staff: a study in Spain and Colombia
papers.abstract: Background Health promotion within the university setting requires valid and reliable instruments to identify factors related to lifestyle, emotional well-being and mental health among staff. Although the Life Conditions Scale (LifeConScale) had previously been validated in adolescents, there were no instruments specifically integrating these dimensions for university personnel. Therefore, adaptation and validation for use with higher education professionals is necessary. Objective To adapt the LifeConScale and examine its psychometric properties in university staff, including Teaching and Research Staff and Technical, Management, Administrative and Services Staff. Materials and methods A cross-sectional study was conducted with 440 professionals from two universities in Spain and Colombia. The instrument was adapted via a Delphi process with health and health-promotion experts. Common-factor exploratory factor analysis with parallel analysis and oblique rotation assessed internal structure; Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin and Bartlett’s test evaluated sampling adequacy. Reliability was estimated with McDonald’s omega. Measurement invariance for core dimensions (personal wellbeing, anxiety, physical activity) between countries was examined through nested multigroup confirmatory factor analysis (configural, metric and scalar). Results Sampling adequacy was adequate (KMO = 0.850; p < 0.001). Parallel analysis and common-factor exploratory factor analysis with oblique rotation identified seven interpretable factors: personal wellbeing, anxiety, physical activity, snacking, leisure screen use, social media use, and fruit and vegetable intake. The Personal Wellbeing Index and GAD-7 showed no cross-loadings and a moderate latent correlation, supporting discriminant validity; the AUDIT-C was retained as an independent validated scale scored with its original algorithm. Reliability (McDonald’s omega) was excellent for anxiety (ω = 0.929), wellbeing (ω = 0.922) and social media (ω = 0.920), and good for physical activity (ω = 0.859), leisure screens (ω = 0.795), fruit and vegetables (ω = 0.760) and snacking (ω = 0.753). Heterogeneous dietary and sleep indicators were treated as formative and not aggregated into summative scores.

papers.title: Modification of Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate)/Poly(lactic acid) Blends by In-Situ Reactive Melt Processing for Sustainable Packaging Application
papers.abstract: Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate) (PHBV) is a biopolyester produced by bacterial biosynthesis that has the potential to replace commodity plastics. However, poor melt strength and a narrow processing window limit its packaging application. In this work, commercial and pilot-scale PHBV is biosynthesized from fermented dairy manure using mixed microbial culture, extracted with dimethyl carbonate, and purified. Blends of the purified PHBV with poly(lactic acid) (PLA) were reactive melt-processed with triallyl isocyanurate (TAIC; 0.2–0.3 wt%), Joncryl (0.1–0.5 wt%), and talc (0.1 wt%), followed by injection molding. Rheological, thermal, and mechanical properties were studied and compared with modified commercial PHBV/PLA blends. The formulation containing 0.3% TAIC/0.3% Joncryl/0.1% talc showed the highest complex viscosity, indicating improved processability. Thermal analysis showed a broadened processing window for the laboratory PHBV/PLA blend but a reduction for the commercial blend. Molar mass analysis indicated considerable thermomechanical degradation, particularly in the laboratory blend. FTIR and gel fraction analysis were consistent with limited network formation in the commercial blend, whereas the laboratory blend showed no measurable gel fraction, with property improvements mainly attributed to enhanced chain entanglement. Differential scanning calorimetry showed reduced crystallinity in both blends. Mechanical testing showed reduced stiffness in both blends. Reactive melt processing enhanced the PHBV/PLA processability for sustainable packaging applications.
papers.summary: Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate) (PHBV) is a biopolyester produced by bacterial biosynthesis that has the potential to replace commodity plastics. Mechanical testing showed reduced stiffness in both blends. Reactive melt processing enhanced the PHBV/PLA processability for sustainable packaging applications.

papers.title: Forecasting Corporate Credit Risk with Machine and Deep Learning: A Forward-Looking Early-Warning Framework for U.S. Listed Firms
papers.journal: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
papers.abstract: Accurate assessment of corporate credit risk matters for investors, lenders and regulators, but traditional accounting-ratio models often miss the changing and non-linear pattern of financial distress. This study examines whether machine learning and deep learning models can produce more accurate and stable credit risk scores for large U.S. listed firms. The analysis uses quarterly financial statements of 1,133 S&P 1500 constituent companies from 2010 to 2025 (72,960 firm-quarter observations), and risk labels are constructed from an adapted Altman Z'-Score. Sixteen financial variables are converted into economically interpretable ratios to mitigate multicollinearity and make the models more stable. Four models are compared: XGBoost, LSTM, BiLSTM and CNN-LSTM, with hyperparameters tuned through grid search. The pattern is clear. XGBoost records the strongest in-sample performance (R² = 0.8904, RMSE = 0.1533), but its performance drops noticeably out of sample. LSTM, in contrast, produces the best test-set results (R² = 0.8073, RMSE = 0.2105). The trained models are then used to forecast credit risk for the next three quarters (2026Q1-Q3). These results emphasize the importance of capturing temporal dynamics in credit risk assessment and provide a practical early-warning framework for investors and risk managers.

papers.title: Investigating cardiorespiratory fitness, cerebral blood flow, and brain metabolism in epilepsy
papers.abstract: Introduction Idiopathic generalized epilepsies (IGEs) are characterized by seizures that propagate through widespread thalamocortical networks including the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC). Poor cardiorespiratory fitness may exacerbate neurovascular and metabolic vulnerability including heightened susceptibility to sudden unexpected death in epilepsy. We aimed to examine cardiorespiratory fitness, regional cerebral blood flow (CBF), and metabolite concentrations in patients with IGEs (PwIGEs) and to determine the effect of seizure control status on these physiological and neurochemical measures. Methods Forty-six participants (31 PwIGEs, 15 healthy controls) underwent a graded exercise test to assess maximal oxygen uptake (VO2peak) as a measure of cardiorespiratory fitness and completed 3T MRI including multi-delayed pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (pCASL) to assess CBF and single-voxel spectroscopy (SVS) to assess ratios of N-acetylaspartate and glutamate/glutamine complex to total creatine (NAA/tCr and Glx/tCr, respectively) in the ACC and thalamus. Group differences and seizure control effects in PwIGEs were examined using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA). Results VO2peak, thalamic CBF, ACC NAA/tCr, and ACC Glx/tCr did not significantly differ between groups. PwIGEs exhibited higher ACC CBF (p = 0.039) and lower thalamic NAA/tCr (p = 0.012) than healthy controls. PwIGEs with active seizures showed significantly lower thalamic Glx/tCr compared to those who were seizure-free (p = 0.003). Discussion These findings suggest poor cardiorespiratory fitness is not epilepsy-specific and likely attributable to lifestyle and that region-specific alterations in perfusion and metabolic milieu in PwIGEs characterized by higher ACC CBF and lower thalamic NAA/tCr and Glx/tCr in those with active seizures. The multimodal neuroimaging approach provides convergent evidence of thalamocortical network dysregulation underlying IGE pathophysiology.

papers.title: Supramolecular Cellulose Crystalline Organisation and Its Relationship with Density, Thermal Stability, and Micromechanical Behaviour in Native Wood
papers.abstract: Understanding the extent to which the supramolecular crystalline organisation of native wood is associated with its macroscopic, thermal and micromechanical properties remains an active area of inquiry in biomass characterisation. In this study, the crystalline, thermal, and micromechanical characteristics of Oriental spruce (Picea orientalis (L.) Peterm.), Scots elm (Ulmus glabra Huds.), Canadian poplar (Populus × canadensis Moench), Austrian pine (Pinus nigra J.F. Arnold), Turkish red pine (Pinus brutia Ten.), and black locust (Robinia pseudoacacia L.) were comparatively investigated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), thermogravimetric–derivative thermogravimetric (TGA-DTG) analysis, Vickers microhardness, and density measurements. Microhardness generally aligned with density trends among the sampled wood specimens; black locust exhibited the highest density (0.727 g/cm3) and, alongside Austrian pine, recorded the highest mean parallel-to-grain hardness (18.0 kgf/mm2). In the perpendicular-to-grain direction, Turkish red pine reached the maximum value (9.9 kgf/mm2). Conversely, Canadian poplar yielded the lowest values across all three evaluated parameters (0.371 g/cm3 density, 6.7 kgf/mm2 parallel, and 3.1 kgf/mm2 perpendicular). XRD profiles confirmed the characteristic cellulose I structure in all examined specimens, with the (200) reflection occurring at 22.06–22.31° and crystallinity index (CrI) values ranging from 55.91% (Scots elm) to 60.07% (Turkish red pine). Apparent crystallite sizes (L200) ranged from 2.68 nm (Scots elm) to 2.94 nm (black locust), indicating modest variation in the measured crystalline parameters. TGA-DTG analysis revealed variation in the observed thermal degradation profiles, with maximum degradation temperatures of 333.0–366.7 °C and total mass losses of 52.3–65.3%. Exploratory comparisons indicated that these nanoscale crystallographic parameters do not present a simple linear relationship with macroscopic thermal mass loss or hardness. Overall, these findings indicate that cellulose crystalline organisation, thermal degradation, density, and micromechanical behaviour are interconnected yet non-equivalent properties. Integrating these multiparametric evaluations provides further insight into the relationships between nanoscale cellulose organisation and the higher-level properties of wood.

papers.title: Molybdenum‐carbothioamide complexes as potential single‐source precursors for MoS 2 thin film
papers.journal: Bulletin of the Korean Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2 ) thin films are widely used in batteries, transistors, supercapacitors, and 2D materials owing to their tunable bandgaps and flexible structural characteristics. To deposit pure MoS 2 thin film, molybdenum precursors have been developed using various organic ligands. In this study, we designed and synthesized novel molybdenum(VI) complexes that can be used as volatile precursors for MoS 2 thin films. N ‐alkoxy carbothioamide ligands were introduced into Mo(N t Bu) 2 Cl 2 (DME) to dissociate the chloride and DME ligands, and two novel Mo complexes, Mo(N t Bu) 2 (mdpaS) 2 ( 1 ) and Mo(N t Bu) 2 (edpaS) 2 ( 2 ), were successfully synthesized in hexane. All the synthesized complexes were analyzed by 1 H and 13 C nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, and single‐crystal X‐ray diffraction to determine their structures. The crystal structures showed that all the complexes had a distorted octahedral structure with hexacoordination. Thermogravimetric analysis was performed to investigate the thermal characteristics of the synthesized complexes. After thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), the residues were analyzed by X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) to evaluate the formation of MoS 2 at high temperatures without an external sulfur source. The TGA and XPS results indicated that all complexes formed MoS 2 upon thermolysis at high temperatures. The synthesized complexes have volatility and metal‐sulfide covalent bonds; therefore, we expect that they could be used as single‐source precursors for depositing MoS 2 thin films.

The TGA and XPS results indicated that all complexes formed MoS 2 upon thermolysis at high temperatures.

papers.title: Chitosan–Poly(vinyl alcohol)–Tea Tree Essential Oil Composite Films: Fabrication, Physicochemical Properties, and Inhibitory Effects on Representative Bacterial Strains and Application for Blueberry Preservation
papers.abstract: Conventional polyethylene (PE) wrap has poor degradability and causes environmental pollution. Meanwhile, pure chitosan (CS) films exhibit weak mechanical strength, and CS–polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) blend films show limited inhibitory performance. To address these limitations, a biodegradable bio-based preservation film was fabricated by incorporating tea tree essential oil (TTEO) into a CS–PVA matrix via a solvent-casting method. The formulation was optimized using single-factor and orthogonal experiments. The films were characterized using SEM, FTIR, XRD, and TGA; their optical, swelling, mechanical, and inhibitory properties were evaluated. Blueberries were coated with the composite film and stored at ambient temperature for 10 days. The optimal formulation consisted of 3.0 wt% CS, 0.5 wt% TTEO, and 1.5 wt% PVA, with good inter-component compatibility driven by hydrogen-bond interactions. The optimized composite film achieved a light transmittance of 88.30% at 600 nm and exhibited inhibition-zone diameters of 1.18 cm and 1.14 cm against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, respectively. Compared with the pure CS film, the composite film obtained higher elongation at break (141.36%) and stress at break (0.42 MPa). The composite-film-coated blueberries showed suppressed MDA accumulation and reduced water loss under ambient storage conditions. This composite film exhibited superior comprehensive performance compared with the pure CS film and provides a promising degradable active-packaging candidate for fruit and vegetable preservation.
papers.summary: Conventional polyethylene (PE) wrap has poor degradability and causes environmental pollution. Meanwhile, pure chitosan (CS) films exhibit weak mechanical strength, and CS–polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) blend films show limited inhibitory performance. The films were characterized using SEM, FTIR, XRD, and TGA; their optical, swelling, mechanical, and inhibitory properties were evaluated.

papers.title: Cerebrovascular flow field reconstruction method based on residual network of physical information
papers.abstract: Introduction Accurate characterization of the hemodynamic environment within intracranial aneurysms is important for rupture‐risk assessment and interventional treatment planning. Although computational fluid dynamics (CFD) provides high‐fidelity flow‐field data, its computational cost limits parametric analyses across multiple vascular geometries and inlet flow conditions. Existing physics‐informed neural‐network surrogates are predominantly trained for individual geometries and single flow conditions. Systematic comparisons of performance degradation under geometric and flow‐rate distribution shifts across different architectures remain lacking, and the distinct roles of physics‐based constraints under in-distribution versus out‐of‐distribution conditions have not been thoroughly examined. Methods This study proposes PIReN, a physics‐informed residual network that decomposes the velocity‐pressure field into a learnable baseline field and a gated residual correction. The training objective incorporates continuity and steady, incompressible Navier‐Stokes momentum residuals. Training and in‐domain evaluation employ seven geometries; zero‐shot testing uses 16 fully held‐out geometries, and flow‐rate generalization is evaluated via five leave‐one‐flow‐rate‐out folds. These two protocols withhold complete geometries or flow conditions and avoid spatial-correlation leakage. Results In the pointwise‐random in‐domain test, PIReN achieves an aggregate relative L 2 error of 11.34% ± 0.65%, outperforming a standard PINN (16.57% ± 1.04%) and purely supervised MLP (14.74% ± 0.72%). These optimistic values describe spatial‐interpolation accuracy. Using a contiguous axial held‐out block while fixing model weights, PIReN still delivers superior accuracy: under the pooled configuration, its aggregate relative L 2 error is 30.35%± 2.55% versus 39.27%±2.85% for PINN. PIReN dominates across all four metrics, both partitions and five configurations, with a larger absolute performance margin under the stricter block partition. On geometry set B, the corresponding errors for PIReN and the PINN are 42.71% and 121.92%, respectively. Discussion Ablation studies show that removing the residual decoder produces the largest increase in prediction error, whereas the physics‐informed loss terms primarily reduce governing‐equation residuals. These results indicate that PIReN reduces performance degradation under changes in vascular geometry and inlet flow rate and provides a promising framework for steady‐state cerebrovascular flow‐field surrogate modeling.

Discussion Ablation studies show that removing the residual decoder produces the largest increase in prediction error, whereas the physics‐informed loss terms primarily reduce governing‐equation residuals. These results indicate that PIReN reduces performance degradation under changes in vascular geometry and inlet flow rate and provides a promising framework for steady‐state cerebrovascular flow‐field surrogate modeling.

papers.title: Optimization of Freeze-Dried Microcapsules Containing Polyphenol-Rich Fruit Extracts: Bioactive Compound Retention, Physicochemical Properties, and Thermal Stability
papers.abstract: Polyphenol-rich plant extracts contain valuable bioactive compounds, but their limited stability and susceptibility to environmental conditions can restrict their application in food systems, making microencapsulation a promising approach for their protection and controlled incorporation. This study investigated the effects of extract source, wall material, and core-to-matrix ratio on the technological properties, encapsulation performance, and retention of bioactive compounds in freeze-dried microcapsules. Four polyphenol-rich sources (red grape skins, black carrot, chokeberry, and blackcurrant), three wall materials (maltodextrin, soy protein isolate, and trehalose), and three core-to-matrix ratios (2:1, 1:1, and 1:2) were evaluated using a D-optimal experimental design. Dry matter, water activity, encapsulation efficiency, yield, loading capacity, and retention of polyphenols, flavonoids, and anthocyanins were determined. FTIR spectroscopy combined with PCA was used for molecular characterization. DSC and SEM were applied to further investigate the powder's properties. The effects of the factors varied among responses. Maltodextrin generally provided the most favorable technological properties in terms of dry matter content, water activity and encapsulation yield, as well as the highest retention of bioactive compounds, while encapsulation efficiency was primarily determined by the core-to-matrix ratio. Loading capacity was affected by all factors and their interactions. Model optimization identified red grape skin extract with maltodextrin at a 1:1 ratio as the most desirable formulation. These findings highlight the importance of multi-response optimization in designing effective polyphenol encapsulation systems.

papers.title: Root biomass distribution in response to increasing active layer thickness across plant communities in a permafrost peatland
papers.abstract: In Arctic tundra, the majority of plant biomass is belowground. As temperatures increase and permafrost thaws, new soil volume containing nitrogen becomes available for plant roots, potentially leading to new plant–soil interactions. Whether or not different plant communities adapt their rooting depth distribution in response to increasing active layer thickness, whether roots at depth are similar to shallow ones, and if deep‐rooting species potentially redistribute thawed‐out nitrogen into more shallow layers remains poorly understood. We studied root biomass, rooting‐depth distribution, root dry matter content (RDMC), and 15 N natural abundances in a low Arctic peatland. We did this in two plant communities, dominated either by the graminoid Eriophorum vaginatum or by various dwarf shrubs, each with either a shallow (51.3 ± 0.9 cm) or a deep (69.4 ± 1.9 cm) active layer. Root biomass declined sharply with depth but did not differ between plant communities or active layer thicknesses, although roots reached the thawfront. RDMC was unaffected by active layer thickness, but was lower in E. vaginatum and declined with depth for roots of both functional types. This suggests relatively more acquisitive roots with faster growth and shorter lifespan in deeper soils. Presence of the deep‐rooting E. vaginatum increased foliar δ 15 N ratios of other species, indicating a potential redistribution of nitrogen in the soil column. Our results suggest that, despite the presence of deep‐rooting plants and roots down to the thawfront in shallow and deep active layers, rooting depth distribution remains relatively constant. This indicates that an increase in deep roots in response to thawing permafrost is relatively species‐specific and might not result in measurable differences in root biomass or its distribution, irrespective of plant community. The decreasing RDMC with depth illustrates that resource strategies vary not only among species but also with soil depth, with implications for carbon and nutrient cycling.

papers.title: Morphological, thermal, and rheological behavior of poly( l -lactide) and poly( meso- lactide) blends
papers.abstract: Polylactide (PLA) is one of the most widely studied biodegradable polymers. However, poly(meso-lactide) (PMLA), an amorphous PLA, remains poorly characterized. This study investigates the thermal, rheological behavior, and morphology of poly(l-lactide) (PLLA) and PMLA blends across a wide composition range. Characterizations were performed using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), small amplitude oscillatory shear (SAOS) rheology, and atomic force microscopy (AFM). Nanoscale heterogeneity is suspected for the 10% and 90% w/w% HMW PLLA/HMW PMLA compositions, while 30 w% HMW PLLA, 50 w% HMW PLLA, and 70 w% HMW PLLA compositions exhibited immiscibility. DSC revealed two glass transition temperatures for 30 w% HMW PLLA, 50 w% HMW PLLA, and 70 w% HMW PLLA blends, corresponding to those of the neat phases, 48.2 ± 0.1 °C for HMW PMLA and 61.8 ± 0.4 °C for HMW PLLA, and a single Tg for the 10% and 90% w/w% HMW PLLA/HMW PMLA composition blends. AFM revealed an emulsion-type morphology at 30 and 70 wt. % HMW PLLA compositions and a co-continuous structure at 50 wt. % HMW PLLA. SAOS results presented a shoulder in the low frequency storage modulus for all blends. The Palierne model was used to fit the dynamic data of the blends and estimated the dispersed phase relaxation time, reinforcing the immiscibility conclusions. Relaxation spectra were obtained for all blends, showing two distinct relaxation modes associated with PLA nature and the interfacial tension of the blend. These results suggest that PMLA and PLLA are largely immiscible.

papers.title: Silkworm Pupae-Derived Chitosan/Poly(vinyl alcohol) Films with Silver Nitrate: Structure, Properties, and Antibacterial Activity Against Gram-Negative and Gram-Positive Bacteria
papers.abstract: Chitosan-based films are attracting attention as renewable antibacterial materials for food packaging, but chitosan from crustacean sources remains costly, and insect-derived alternatives are hardly explored. This study examined how the polymer ratio and silver nitrate (AgNO3) incorporation govern the properties of films prepared from chitosan (CS) extracted from mulberry silkworm (Bombyx mori) pupae, an abundant by-product of the sericulture industry in Uzbekistan. Films were cast from CS and poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) solutions at volume ratios of 75:25, 60:40, and 50:50, with and without AgNO3, and characterized by infrared spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy with elemental analysis, and thermal analysis, together with mechanical, swelling, acid-stability, and water vapor transmission measurements. Antibacterial activity was assessed by agar diffusion against ten reference and clinical bacterial strains. The characteristic bands of both polymers were retained at essentially unchanged positions in all compositions, and the degree of structural order followed the PVA content. The CS/PVA 50:50 film reached the highest tensile strength (60.7 ± 7.8 MPa) and the lowest thickness-normalized water vapor permeability among the binary films, and AgNO3 increased the residual mass on heating, reduced swelling, and extended the antibacterial spectrum to nine of the ten strains, including two Staphylococcus aureus isolates and Acinetobacter baumannii, whereas no film inhibited Enterococcus faecalis. Film properties can therefore be tuned through composition, supporting the development of silkworm-derived chitosan films as antibacterial polymeric materials for packaging and related non-contact applications.

papers.title: Folic Acid-Functionalized Chitosan-Coated Oleosomes Engineered for Enhanced Anti-Arthritic Delivery of Syzygium cumini Seed Extract
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of folic acid-functionalized chitosan-coated oleosomes (F-CS-OL) loaded with Syzygium cumini (SYG) seed extract against rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in a complete Freund’s adjuvant (CFA)-induced arthritis rat model. Methods: Rats received treatments via the oral route for 11 days following arthritis induction. The colloidal formulation exhibited an average particle size of 80.78 ± 1.02 nm, a zeta potential of −15.5 ± 1.12 mV, and an encapsulation efficiency (EE) of 94.98 ± 0.56%, alongside characterization by TEM, FTIR, and DSC. CFA-induced arthritis produced a pronounced inflammatory and angiogenic response, marked by significantly elevated serum levels of TNF-α, IL-6, CRP, VEGF, ICAM-1, MMP-3, and CXCL13 compared with the normal control group. Results: While treatment with free SYG extract resulted in moderate reductions in these biomarkers, the nanoencapsulated extract (SYG-loaded F-CS-OL) produced significantly greater reductions in inflammatory, chemotactic, matrix-remodeling, and angiogenesis-associated biomarkers compared with the untreated CFA-induced arthritis group. Histopathological examination of joint tissues further supported the biochemical findings. Conclusions: Overall, SYG-loaded F-CS-OL exhibited potent anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory activities and significantly reduced biomarkers associated with angiogenic signaling in CFA-induced arthritis in CFA-induced arthritis. These findings suggest that folic acid-functionalized nanocarriers may represent a promising strategy for enhancing the therapeutic potential of SYG; however, further pharmacokinetic and safety studies are warranted to support clinical translation.

papers.title: Peri-transplant eculizumab for preventing antibody-mediated rejection in kidney transplant recipients at high immunologic risk: a systematic review with design-stratified evidence synthesis
papers.abstract: Introduction Highly sensitized candidates, preformed donor-specific antibodies, and ABO incompatibility restrict access to kidney transplantation and increase antibody-mediated rejection (AMR) risk. We systematically evaluated peri-transplant eculizumab-containing prophylaxis in high-immunologic-risk kidney transplantation. Methods We searched PubMed, Europe PMC, Ovid Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Ovid CENTRAL, ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO ICTRP, and supplementary sources; database searches ended 10 June 2026, and registry searches ended 20 August 2026. Results A total of 31 reports were included; 30 were linked to 14 studies or registry projects, and one pathology report was retained qualitatively. In the only randomized trial, centrally confirmed AMR occurred in 5/51 recipients in both the eculizumab and standard-desensitization groups [risk ratio (RR) 1.00, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.31–3.25]. A historical comparison reported AMR in 2/26 versus 21/51 recipients (RR 0.19, 95% CI 0.05–0.74), but treatment era, post-transplant plasma exchange, and clinical management changed concurrently. An 80-recipient single-arm study reported three AMR events by week 9. Long-term follow-up showed no consistent graft-survival or kidney-function advantage, while persistent donor-specific antibodies and chronic microvascular injury remained evident. Discussion Eculizumab can provide terminal complement blockade within selected combination prophylaxis, but randomized evidence does not establish an incremental reduction in AMR. Definitive trials require standardized background therapy, rescue criteria, long-term graft outcomes, and infection surveillance. This systematic review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261484542). Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/ , identifier CRD420261484542.

papers.title: CFT-Triplet: integrating contextual, frequency and textural features for fine-grained pulmonary fissure detection
papers.abstract: Accurate detection and integrity assessment of pulmonary fissures are essential for the effective treatment of emphysema and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, clinical CT scans often present fissures with weak contrasts and severe deformations. Standard deep learning approaches face two fundamental limitations in this task: First, they exhibit an inherent “spectral bias,” preferentially learning low-frequency shapes while suppressing high-frequency boundary details (i.e., the fissures). Second, existing Transformer-based global modeling incurs quadratic computational costs, limiting the efficient capture of long-range anatomical continuity. To address these challenges, we propose CFT-Triplet, a framework that integrates Contextual, Frequency, and Textural features for robust fissure detection. The core of our framework is the CFT-Triplet Block, an architectural unit designed to extract and fuse these three complementary features within a unified module. Within each Triplet Block, we design a hybrid topology: (1) To model long-range anatomical dependencies, we incorporate Bidirectional Mamba2, which captures global Contextual information with linear complexity; (2) To specifically compensate for spectral loss, these contextual features are serially refined by a dedicated Frequency module, sharpening high-frequency boundary components; (3) Simultaneously, a parallel CNN-based Textural branch is utilized to extract local spatial patterns. This triplet design ensures that every network layer possesses both the global receptive field and the sensitivity to local edges. The multi-view features are then fused via a Gate-Net module to maximize complementarity. Extensive experiments on the Shandong Provincial Chest Hospital (SPCH) dataset—where 400 high-quality CT scans were selected from 500 collected cases after rigorous data cleaning (partitioned into 320 training, 40 validation, and 40 testing sets at the patient level to prevent data leakage)—demonstrate that CFT-Triplet outperforms state-of-the-art methods on our private SPCH dataset.

papers.title: Human Tumor Microbiomes are Site-Specific Across Five Body Locations
papers.abstract: Tumor-associated microbial communities may influence cancer development, yet their patterns across anatomical sites remain incompletely characterized. The analysis used 424 samples from The Cancer Microbiome Atlas (TCMA), including tumors from the colon, esophagus, head/neck, rectum, and stomach, along with healthy tissues. Comparisons covered microbial abundance, alpha and beta diversity, core taxa, and differential abundance. Random forest models were used to assess classification. Tumor and healthy samples had similar overall community profiles, with no significant difference in Shannon diversity and little beta-diversity variation explained by tumor status. Anatomical site accounted for more variation than any other variable examined. Colon and rectum showed similar communities, while esophagus, head/neck, and stomach formed another group. Diversity measures, core and differential taxa, and predictive models supported this division. These results suggest that anatomical location has a stronger association with microbial composition than tumor status and should be considered when developing microbial biomarkers.

papers.title: Vanadium Oxide–Modified Cathodes for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries: A Review
papers.abstract: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) are gaining traction as a safe, low‑cost alternative to lithium‑based systems, not least because of their high ionic conductivity. Among the candidate cathode materials, vanadium oxides stand out for their layered/open frameworks, multiple valence states, and high theoretical capacities—V₂O₅ in particular offers a combination of facile synthesis and a two‑electron redox chemistry that gives a respectable 589 mAh·g⁻¹. In practice, though, its poor electronic conductivity, sluggish Zn²⁺ diffusion, structural degradation upon repeated cycling, and active‑material dissolution remain serious bottlenecks. This review summarizes the four main classes of AZIB cathodes and the three prevailing energy‑storage mechanisms, then focuses on recent modification strategies for V₂O₅—namely, preparation routes, Li⁺‑storage/deintercalation behavior, morphology engineering, and conductive composite design—and discusses how each strategy improves electrochemical performance. Despite these advances, long‑term structural stability and rate capability at high current densities still fall short of practical requirements. The aim here is to offer a reference for developing better vanadium‑based cathodes in the future.

papers.title: Oxidation of Alcohols over Recyclable Zeolite-Supported MnO2 Nanoparticles: A Sustainable Catalytic Approach
papers.abstract: MnO2 nanoparticles were eco-friendly synthesized using Lawsonia inermis extract as a capping and stabilizing agent and then immobilized on the surface of 13X molecular sieve zeolite (MnO2@Z). The green-supported catalyst was tested for the selective oxidation of benzyl alcohol (BzOH) to benzaldehyde (BzDH) in the presence of H2O2 oxidant. The catalyst was characterized using FTIR, XRD, FE-SEM, EDX, TGA, and BET analysis. Many tests were performed to study the effects of reaction time, reaction temperature, amount of catalyst, and H2O2:BzOH ratio on the catalytic performance. The highest activity was achieved after 6 h of reaction at 80 °C, using 250 mg catalyst, and 1.25H2O2: 1BzOH molar ratio. Utilizing the biochemical properties of Lawsonia inermis extract, a highly stable heterogeneous catalyst was developed for the selective oxidation of benzyl alcohol to benzaldehyde. This work demonstrates a heterogeneous catalytic oxidation approach with potential sustainability advantages, including catalyst recyclability and the use of H2O2 as an oxidant. Although the current study demonstrates promising catalytic performance, further optimization of catalyst loading, energy consumption, and recovery procedures, together with comprehensive green chemistry assessments, will be required for future scale-up applications.

papers.title: Robust bio-based epoxy vitrimers with dual dynamic boronic ester and β-hydroxy ester bonds: self-healing, weldability and recyclability
papers.abstract: Development of bio-based epoxy vitrimers faces a persistent trade-off between high mechanical/thermal performance and efficient dynamic reversibility for self-healing and recycling. Herein, we report a series of furan-based epoxy vitrimers (DGFB-x) that integrate dual dynamic covalent bonds, boronic ester and β -hydroxy ester, within a single network. These materials are synthesized by curing a bio-based diglycidyl furan-2,5-dicarboxylate (DGF) monomer with an aminophenylboronic acid-derived crosslinker ( di -BONH 2 ). The chemical structures are confirmed by FTIR and NMR, and the crosslinked nature is verified by swelling tests. By adjusting the crosslinker ratio, the tensile strength can be tuned from 48.5 to 75.4 MPa and the Young’s modulus from 137.3 to 512.5 MPa, while the elongation at break decreases correspondingly. Thermal analysis shows excellent stability with initial decomposition temperatures ( T 5% ) above 270 °C and heat-resistant indices ( T s ) up to 163.3 °C. Owing to the dual dynamic exchange mechanisms, the optimized DGFB-1.0 exhibits outstanding self-healing efficiency (98.2% at 90 °C for 60 min), high welding efficiency (>94%), remarkable reprocessability (81.3% tensile strength retention after three cycles), and effective chemical recycling via alcoholysis (recovery >90%). Furthermore, DGFB-1.0-based carbon-fiber-reinforced composites are successfully recycled with preserved carbon fiber quality and mechanical properties. This work proposes a tentative molecular design approach aimed at alleviating the performance-recyclability conflict in sustainable thermosets.

This work proposes a tentative molecular design approach aimed at alleviating the performance-recyclability conflict in sustainable thermosets.

papers.title: Sex differences dominate urinary extracellular DNA concentrations and variability in humans and rodents
papers.abstract: Urinary extracellular DNA has emerged as a promising non-invasive biomarker for kidney and urinary tract diseases. However, its physiological concentration, variability, and potential sex-dependent differences in healthy individuals are poorly defined. This lack of baseline knowledge limits the clinical and translational use of urinary extracellular DNA. Morning urine samples were collected from 66 healthy adults (33 women and 33 men), as well as from female and male mice and rats. Extracellular DNA was isolated from urine supernatant and quantified fluorometrically. Nuclear and mitochondrial DNA were measured using quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Urinary creatinine, osmolality, and deoxyribonuclease activity were assessed to evaluate potential confounding factors. Fragment size distribution was analysed using capillary electrophoresis. Sex differences were analysed using unpaired statistical tests, variability was assessed by comparing variances and coefficients of variation, and correlations were evaluated using Pearson analysis. Women exhibited approximately 5-fold higher concentrations of urinary extracellular DNA than men and showed markedly greater inter-individual variability. These differences persisted after normalization to creatinine and osmolality and were significant for nuclear DNA but not mitochondrial DNA. Female mice and rats also demonstrated higher extracellular DNA concentrations than males, with approximately 2-fold higher levels in mice and 11-fold higher levels in rats. No association was found between extracellular DNA concentration and urine concentration parameters, menstrual cycle phase, or urinary deoxyribonuclease activity. Most urinary extracellular DNA consisted of nucleosome-sized fragments. Biological sex is a major determinant of urinary extracellular DNA concentration and variability in humans and rodents. The high physiological variability, particularly in females, limits the use of absolute urinary extracellular DNA levels as a standalone biomarker. These findings underscore the necessity of incorporating sex-specific considerations into the design, analysis, and interpretation of urinary extracellular DNA studies.

Sex differences were analysed using unpaired statistical tests, variability was assessed by comparing variances and coefficients of variation, and correlations were evaluated using Pearson analysis.

papers.title: Tailoring the Electrical and Thermal Response of PVA Nanofibers Through Metal Oxide Incorporation via Electrospinning
papers.journal: Ibn AL- Haitham Journal For Pure and Applied Science
papers.abstract: This study investigates the structural, thermal, and electrical properties of polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) nanofibers doped with a ZnO–CoO binary oxide, synthesized via a controlled electrospinning process at an applied voltage of 16 kV and a flow rate of 0.8 mL/h. FESEM analysis revealed a systematic morphological transition from smooth, uniform fibers to a bead-on-string structure as the dopant concentration increased from 1 wt% to 5 wt%. Moreover, quantitative analysis revealed fine fiber morphologies, with the minimum diameters reaching 17 nm, 23 nm, and 26 nm of different concentration ratios, respectively. X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis confirmed the amorphous nature of both the pristine and doped nanofibers. The absence of metallic crystalline peaks suggests that the dopants were uniformly distributed throughout the polymer matrix, which is consistent with established literature. Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectra demonstrated an increasing shift in the vibrations of the hydroxyl (–OH) functional groups, signifying strengthened intermolecular interactions. Thermal analysis via TGA/DSC indicated that while low-level doping (1 wt%) enhances thermal stability, higher dopant concentrations result in a reduction of the characteristic degradation temperatures. Electrical characterization revealed that the conductivity follows an Arrhenius-type behavior, in which the activation energy ( ) was significantly reduced with increasing dopant concentration. The lowest value of 0.031 eV was attained for the composite containing 4 wt% of the ZnO–CoO hybrid. These results suggest that the charge transport mechanism is thermally activated and that the incorporation of metal oxide dopants effectively lowers the energy barrier for carrier hopping. Consequently, the synthesized hybrid nanofibers demonstrate a high degree of tailoring capability for tunable electronic applications

papers.title: Overview of X-ray Thomson scattering measurements of extreme states of matter
papers.abstract: Since its first successful applications in the early 2000s, X-ray Thomson scattering (XRTS) has emerged as one of the most successful tools for the diagnostics of extreme states of matter in the laboratory. By sampling the dynamic structure factor of the electrons, XRTS is capable of giving detailed insights into the atomic-scale physics of the matter probed. Moreover, thermodynamic parameters, such as the mass density, temperature, and ionization state, are routinely inferred from XRTS measurements, providing a comprehensive characterization of the sample probed. In addition, the dynamic structure factor is of considerable interest in its own right, since it contains information on other effects such as the plasmon shift, miscibility between species, electronic states, and potential transitions between these states. In this work, we provide an extensive overview of previous XRTS experiments at both traditional laser and X-ray free-electron laser facilities, including information about the probed material (elements and conditions), scattering geometry, and analysis methods, as well as the corresponding references. In addition, we briefly discuss the advantages and shortcomings of widely used analysis methods for XRTS spectra and reflect on upcoming future developments in XRTS experiments and theory.

papers.title: Improving photosynthate allocation dynamic simulations of crops under water stress conditions
papers.abstract: Abstract. Accurately simulating crop photosynthate allocation under water stress is critical for predicting both food security and ecosystem carbon sequestration (SOC inputs). Current crop models often rely on static or growth-stage-fixed partitioning coefficients, which limits their ability to capture the physiological plasticity of crops responding to fluctuating environmental conditions. This study develops a water-driven, stage-dependent carbon allocation scheme within the Agro-C model to better represent crop responses to soil moisture variability. The scheme dynamically adjusts photosynthate partitioning coefficients for roots (PR) and leaves (PL), integrates the yellow-to-green leaf ratio (YGR), and incorporates a water stress–induced leaf senescence module. By linking carbon allocation to both soil moisture and crop development, the approach improves the representation of physiologically regulated allocation processes and enhances the realism of crop simulations. Model evaluation using extensive datasets for maize and wheat demonstrates substantial improvements in simulation accuracy, with R2 values reaching 0.77–0.95 for aboveground biomass (AGB) and 0.62–0.83 for belowground biomass (BGB). These results underscore the importance of dynamically representing carbon allocation under water stress and offer an improved framework for simulating carbon–water interactions in agroecosystems.

papers.title: Laminated structure design accommodates thermal expansion mismatch for mechanically and thermally dual-stable thermoelectric contacts
papers.abstract: The quality of the barrier layer (BL) directly determines the long-term stability of thermoelectric (TE) modules. Conventional BLs struggle to simultaneously achieve thermal expansion matching with TE materials and robust diffusion-blocking capability. Here we show a bimetallic multilayer BL strategy that ensures thermal expansion matching while constructing a controllable interfacial stress field to inhibit element diffusion. Taking skutterudite (SKD) as an example, we construct a BL with alternating Nb and Cu layers, in which Nb serves as the primary diffusion barrier, while Cu tailors the effective thermal expansion behavior and regulates the stress field at the SKD/Nb interface via Nb/Cu back stress, thereby achieving mechanical stability and a strong diffusion-blocking effect. After aging at 823 K for 60 days, the SKD/Nb-Cu interface remains intact and maintains a low contact resistivity ( < 1 μΩ·cm²). Furthermore, the strategy proves effective in Bi2Te3- and GeTe-based TE systems, demonstrating its universality. This work proposes a design strategy based on laminated metals, in which thermal expansion of the barrier layer is tailored to regulate interfacial stress–diffusion coupling, enabling mechanically and thermally dual-stable thermoelectric contacts.

papers.title: Performance optimization and combined mechanisms of fiber-FRP hybrid reinforcement systems in seawater sea sand concrete: a comprehensive review
papers.journal: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science
papers.abstract: Abstract This review examines performance optimization and the combined mechanisms of fiber–FRP hybrid reinforcement systems in seawater sea sand concrete (SWSSC) for marine infrastructure, synthesizing a consolidated corpus of 178 peer-reviewed studies published up to 2026 across material fundamentals, system configurations, mechanical performance, bond behavior, marine durability, and optimization methodologies. Properly designed hybrid configurations achieve 15–30% higher compressive strength and 20–45% enhanced flexural performance relative to plain SWSSC; consistent with a conservative, baseline-referenced reading of the evidence, these gains are treated as combined additive effects of triaxial confinement and micro–macro crack bridging rather than as proof of non-linear synergy. Optimal fiber volume fractions typically remain below 0.5%, with micro/macro combinations giving the strongest combined response, while CFRP exhibits the smallest mechanical degradation under seawater exposure relative to GFRP and BFRP—an advantage that remains conditional and bounded by accelerated-laboratory testing. Significant standardization gaps persist in bond models, long-term performance prediction, and physics-informed AI optimization. The review establishes a mechanism-driven framework and traceable design guidance for sustainable marine concrete.

papers.title: Multiplexed sensor arrays for high-spatiotemporal decoding of complex physiological networks
papers.abstract: Multiplexed sensor arrays expand biomedical interfaces by allowing independently recoverable sensing sources to share limited transmission, addressing, readout, acquisition, and computational resources. This Review compares time-, frequency-, spatial-, optical-, code-, and hybrid-multiplexing through a requirement–resource framework. We examine how signal integrity, front-end electronics, calibration, materials, mechanics, power, and data handling constrain source-specific recovery and outline architecture-selection principles for reliable physiological sensing and bidirectional biointerfaces.

papers.title: Direct Seawater Electrolysis for Decentralised Hydrogen Production: Opportunities for the Blue Economy
papers.abstract: The blue economy is one of the most carbon-intensive sectors globally, with shipping alone emitting over 1000 Mt CO2 annually. Decarbonising it needs a clean, energy‑dense fuel, and green hydrogen has emerged as a leading option. However, existing electrolysis systems remain centralised, relying on freshwater and poorly suited to offshore conditions. Direct seawater electrolysis (DSE) resolves this by coupling offshore renewables with seawater to produce hydrogen directly at the point of demand. This eliminates the need for dedicated desalination, potentially reducing hydrogen production costs by up to 30%. Yet deployment is constrained by competing chlorine evolution, anodic corrosion, and cathodic hydroxide precipitation. In addition, scalable seawater electrolyser architectures remain underdeveloped. Advancing DSE requires integrating catalyst innovation with durable, environmentally robust system design. Here, we connect mechanistic strategies for mitigating cathodic precipitation with an ionically bonded heterostructure design principle for anodic OER-CER selectivity, and extend both to the underexplored challenges of intermittency and membrane durability. At scale, DSE could transform energy supply in the blue economy, enabling decentralised hydrogen production directly from seawater.
papers.summary: The blue economy is one of the most carbon-intensive sectors globally, with shipping alone emitting over 1000 Mt CO2 annually. In addition, scalable seawater electrolyser architectures remain underdeveloped. At scale, DSE could transform energy supply in the blue economy, enabling decentralised hydrogen production directly from seawater.

papers.title: Formulation and Evaluation of Azathioprine – loaded Chitosan Microspheres for Sustained Drug Delivery
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a persistent, degenerative joint disorder marked by joint pain, stiffness and impaired mobility.Conventional drug therapy often requires frequent dosing due to short half-life and limited bioavailability of drugs that leads to adverse drug effects and poor patient compliance.Azathioprine (AZA), an immunosuppressive drug, has been shown to have anti-inflammatory and disease-modifying effects in the treatment of OA.However, its low bioavailability and short half-life pose challenges for effective treatment.The polymeric microspheres provide a promising controlled drug delivery through prolonging drug release and improving therapeutic efficacy.Chitosan is widely used because of its slow degradation rate, improved biocompatibility and suitability for sustained release formulations.The project intended to create and characterize AZA-loaded chitosan microspheres for targeted and sustained medication administration.The Microspheres were prepared by emulsification heat-denaturation method and evaluated for pre formulation studies, compatibility studies and characterization by zeta potential and in vitro studies.UV Spectrometric analysis authenticated max at 276 nm and calibration curves demonstrated good linearity.Compatibility studies demonstrated no notable interaction between the drug and polymer.In vitro studies depicted sustained drug release over an extended period along with diffusion-controlled kinetics.The findings propose that Azathioprine loaded Chitosan microspheres give an optimistic controlled drug delivery system capable of prolonged therapeutic effect and reduced dose frequency.F6 among all the formulations was found to be the optimized one.This method may enhance the drug efficacy and provide better patient compliance for the treatment of Osteoarthritis.Moreover, in vitro studies are supported to demonstrate clinical and pharmacokinetic performance.General principles are shown in Figure 1.

papers.title: Radiology-Guided Targeted Drug Delivery: Enhancing Precision Therapeutics through Advanced Imaging Techniques
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Radiology-guided targeted drug delivery is an emerging precision-therapeutic strategy that integrates advanced imaging, minimally invasive intervention, and targeted delivery platforms to improve drug localization and treatment monitoring.Conventional systemic therapy is often limited by nonspecific biodistribution, poor tissue penetration, premature clearance, and dose-limiting toxicity, particularly in oncology, neurological disorders, cardiovascular disease, and inflammatory conditions.Image-guided approaches address these limitations by enabling lesion localization, route planning, real-time procedural guidance, biodistribution assessment, and early response evaluation.Ultrasound, CT, MRI, fluoroscopy, PET, SPECT, and hybrid imaging systems each contribute distinct advantages for localized, regional, molecular, or theranostic delivery.Drug delivery platforms such as nanoparticles, liposomes, microbubbles, hydrogels, radioligands, and catheter-based systems further enhance site-specific therapeutic deposition and in vivo tracking.Applications include focused ultrasound-mediated blood-brain barrier modulation, CT-guided intratumoral therapy, PET/SPECT-guided radioligand treatment, nanomedicine-based carrier tracking, and locoregional therapy for solid tumors.Despite challenges related to biological heterogeneity, imaging standardization, safety, scalability, and regulatory translation, radiology-guided targeted drug delivery offers a clinically relevant pathway for individualized treatment.Continued integration of molecular imaging, theranostics, smart carriers, and quantitative monitoring may improve therapeutic precision, reduce systemic toxicity, and strengthen patient-specific treatment optimization.

papers.title: AceTherm: Accelerated Thermal Analysis of Chiplet Integration Using Non-Conformal FEM
papers.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
papers.abstract: As advanced process nodes continue to scale, heterogeneous integration technologies such as 2.5D/3D packaging, chiplets, and high-bandwidth memory have been widely adopted. However, these advances introduce substantially higher power densities, more complex interconnection structures, and increasingly diverse material systems. The resulting localized hotspots raise reliability concerns such as electromigration, thermomechanical stress, and structural warpage, making layout-driven thermal simulation with balanced accuracy and efficiency essential for rapid design iterations. This paper proposes AceTherm, an automated thermal simulation framework driven by Graphic Data System (GDS) layout and Process Design Kit (PDK) process parameters, which integrates non-conformal finite element method with customized sparse-matrix solvers. By exploiting the layered structure of the chip architecture, the simulation domain is sampled and discretized with a non-conformal mesh and high-resolution material mapping, significantly reducing degrees of freedom (DOFs) while preserving accuracy. The mesh division and sampling resolution provide a two-level control for trading off accuracy and speed, and the convergence and error behavior are analyzed to characterize the discrete scheme of AceTherm. Exploiting the structural properties of the resulting coefficient matrix, AceTherm employs supernodal sparse Cholesky factorization to accelerate the solution process. Notably, the symbolic factorization can be reused across multiple thermal load scenarios when the mesh pattern remains unchanged. Numerical experiments show that the proposed method achieves a 104.6 × speedup over the conventional COMSOL solution and reaches up to 539.2 × in repeated or preset-parameter simulations, while maintaining the average temperature error below 1 K. The combination of high computational speed, layer-aware modeling, and sub-Kelvin accuracy positions AceTherm as a practical tool for thermal analysis and optimization in heterogeneous IC back-end design.

papers.title: Recurrence and Treatment Failure in Chronic Osteomyelitis: Clinical, Microbiological, and Anatomical Predictors - A Systematic Review
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: Chronic osteomyelitis remains prone to persistence and recurrence despite advances in surgical debridement, antimicrobial treatment, local antibiotic delivery, bone reconstruction, and soft-tissue coverage.Failure is rarely explained by a single factor.Host vulnerability, repeated previous treatment, microbial phenotype, bone loss, vascular compromise, and the feasibility of achieving complete source control interact to determine long-term outcome.Objective: To systematically evaluate clinical, microbiological, and anatomical predictors of persistent infection, recurrence, reoperation, reconstructive failure, and amputation in adults treated for chronic osteomyelitis.Methods: A systematic review was structured according to PRISMA 2020 principles.MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL were considered together with reference-list and citation searching.Eligible primary studies evaluated adults with chronic appendicular osteomyelitis, post-traumatic osteomyelitis, implant-associated infection, infected nonunion, or chronic limb osteomyelitis and reported treatment failure or recurrence in relation to identifiable predictors.Search identified 3,214 records.After removal of 706 duplicates, 2,508 records underwent title and abstract screening.Full texts of 259 reports were assessed, and 22 studies were retained for qualitative synthesis.Meta-analysis was not undertaken because of substantial heterogeneity in disease definition, reconstruction technique, microbiology, follow-up, and definitions of failure.Results: Recurrence ranged from approximately 6% in standardized specialist-center single-stage cohorts to 45.5% in a 2026 multicenter cohort involving staged management of large bone defects.In a 424-patient induced-membrane cohort, recurrence occurred in 12.26%; at least three previous operations, post-traumatic etiology, and internal fixation during the first stage independently increased recurrence risk.In a 314-patient limb osteomyelitis cohort, recurrence was 16.9%, with segmental bone defects, smoking, and Gram-negative bacilli independently associated with recurrence.Post-traumatic tibial osteomyelitis treated with bone transport showed an 11.4% recurrence/reinfection rate; Pseudomonas aeruginosa, exposed bone, and more than three previous operations were independent predictors.Vascular compromise increased recurrence odds approximately fivefold in a 120-patient reconstructive cohort.Microbiologically, P. aeruginosa, Gram-negative bacilli, polymicrobial growth, ESBLproducing Enterobacteriaceae, and multidrug resistance were associated with unfavorable outcomes.MRSA primarily increased persistent infection rather than subsequent recurrence, with an adjusted odds ratio of 2.26 for persistence among 482 patients with S. aureus osteomyelitis.Large defects increased treatment complexity substantially; however, standardized reconstruction could mitigate anatomical risk.Conclusion: Recurrence in chronic osteomyelitis is best predicted by the accumulation of risk across three domains: compromised host and treatment history, difficult microbiology, and anatomical/reconstructive complexity.Smoking, vascular compromise, repeated previous operations, exposed bone, post-traumatic disease, segmental defects, internal fixation in active infection, Gramnegative organisms, P. aeruginosa, and polymicrobial or resistant infection identify higher-risk patients.Anatomical severity is not synonymous with inevitable failure when complete source control and appropriate reconstruction are achievable.Multidimensional preoperative risk assessment should therefore guide debridement, microbiological sampling, reconstruction, antimicrobial planning, and duration of follow-up.

papers.title: Quality by Design-Based Development and In Vitro Characterization of a Herbosomal Delivery System for Enhanced Solubility, Stability, and Controlled Release of a Herbal Bioactive
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Silymarin is a widely used hepatoprotective phytoconstituent; however, its clinical effectiveness is limited by poor aqueous solubility and low oral bioavailability.The present study aimed to develop and optimize silymarin-loaded herbosomes using the solvent evaporation method to improve its physicochemical characteristics and in vitro drug release.A Quality by Design (QbD) approach employing a 3² full factorial design was adopted to investigate the influence of the drug-to-phospholipid ratio and ethanol volume on critical quality attributes, including particle size, entrapment efficiency, and cumulative drug release.The prepared herbosomes were characterized for particle size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, drug loading, entrapment efficiency, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, differential scanning calorimetry, scanning electron microscopy, in vitro drug release, release kinetics, and accelerated stability.The optimized formulation exhibited nanosized particles with a narrow size distribution, high entrapment efficiency, favourable zeta potential, enhanced drug loading, and sustained drug release compared with pure silymarin.FTIR and DSC studies indicated successful complex formation between silymarin and phosphatidylcholine without chemical incompatibility, while SEM confirmed the formation of uniform spherical particles.Overall, the developed herbosomal formulation demonstrated improved pharmaceutical performance and represents a promising phospholipid-based delivery system for enhancing the solubility and in vitro release characteristics of silymarin.

papers.title: Strategic and carbon footprint assessment of Brazil's iron mining wastes for construction
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Engineering Sustainability
papers.abstract: This study investigates the reuse potential of three iron mining wastes from Brazil’s Iron Quadrangle: iron ore tailings (IOT), iron ore sandy tailings (IOST), and iron waste rock (IWR). The materials were characterised through physical, chemical, mineralogical, and thermogravimetric analyses, combined with a CPQvA-based qualitative assessment and a carbon footprint analysis for concrete mixtures incorporating mining wastes. IOT presented chemical and physical characteristics compatible with supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs), although X-ray diffraction analysis indicates high crystallinity, suggesting a predominantly filler effect in cement-based composites. IOST, composed primarily of quartz, presents characteristics favourable for use as fine aggregate. IWR exhibited suitable properties for applications such as roller-compacted concrete dams and pavement layers. The qualitative assessment identified IOST as the most promising material, followed by IWR. Carbon footprint analysis indicated that replacing conventional aggregates with IOST and IWR, combined, or substituting 5% of Portland cement with IOT, can reduce carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions from raw material production and transportation for concrete by up to 5%, while these combined strategies can reduce the carbon footprint by approximately 10%, with the magnitude varying by concrete class and cement type. The results highlight the need to integrate legal, environmental, technical, and logistical aspects into waste reuse strategies.

The results highlight the need to integrate legal, environmental, technical, and logistical aspects into waste reuse strategies.

papers.title: Thermo-Mechanical Ablation (TMA®) with Tixel® C for Evaporative Dry Eye Associated with Meibomian Gland Dysfunction: A Multicenter, Open-Label, Single-Arm, Exploratory Clinical Study
papers.abstract: Background: Tixel® C (Novoxel Ltd., Netanya, Israel) is a thermomechanical system that conducts heat to soft tissue via a titanium tip heated to 400 °C and has been used for skin rejuvenation, including the eyelids. Its efficacy for dry eye disease (DED) and meibomian gland dysfunction (MGD) has been reported, but it has not been evaluated in Japanese patients. Methods: This multicenter, open-label, single-arm, exploratory clinical study examined the efficacy and safety of Tixel C for evaporative dry eye associated with MGD. Patients underwent three treatment sessions at 2-week intervals, with 10 pulses applied to the upper and lower eyelids of both eyes in two overlapping rows (skin contact, 6 ms; tip protrusion, 400 μm). The primary endpoint was the change in tear film break-up time (TBUT) and the secondary endpoint was the change in the Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI). Results: Twenty patients (4 men, 16 women; mean age, 53.6 ± 16.7 years) were enrolled, and 3 patients discontinued the study. The mean TBUT change was 2.470 s and OSDI improved by a mean of −29.459 (p < 0.0001). No major adverse events occurred. Conclusions: Tixel C was associated with improved tear film stability and subjective symptoms, and no major adverse events were observed during the short follow-up period.

papers.title: Biopolymer Composites Filled with Brewer’s Spent Grain for Yeast Immobilization
papers.abstract: Biopolymer-based composites incorporating natural fillers were developed as carriers for various microbiological applications. Three commercially available biodegradable and bio-based polymers: poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) (PHB), poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate) (PHBV), and polylactide (PLA)were used as matrices. Brewer’s spent grain (BSG), a by-product of the brewing industry, was employed as a natural filler. A series of biocomposites containing 20, 30, and 40 wt% BSG were fabricated. The structure and thermal properties of the composites were characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). Surface properties were evaluated by measuring contact angles with two probe liquids, enabling calculation of surface energy and its polar and dispersive components. In turn, microscopic studies were conducted to evaluate the adhesion and colonization of Metschnikowia andauensis cells on the prepared carriers. The biocontrol activity of the cell–carrier system was assessed using the agar plate method. The results identified the most promising formulations: PHBV with 40 wt% BSG and PLA with 20–40 wt% BSG, especially with 30 wt% BSG. However, the highest biocontrol efficacy among cells adhered to the biocomposite materials was observed with the last one. This study explored the relationship between the physicochemical properties of BSG-filled biopolymers and their suitability for microbial colonization, highlighting their potential as functional carriers for yeast cells.

papers.title: Multi-omics analysis reveals coordinated transcriptional and epigenetic remodeling of tenocytes under IL-1β-driven inflammatory stimulation
papers.abstract: Background Tendinopathy is frequently associated with chronic inflammation driven by pro-inflammatory cytokines. Among these, interleukin-1β (IL-1β) serves as a central mediator of tendon degradation, yet its genome-scale transcriptional and epigenetic consequences in tenocytes remain incompletely characterized. Methods We profiled the transcriptomes and chromatin accessibility landscapes of control and IL-1β-treated primary rat tenocytes using RNA-seq and ATAC-seq, respectively. Differential expression and accessibility analyses, region-associated differentially expressed gene (RAD) analysis, gene functional enrichment analysis, and transcription factor motif enrichment analysis were performed to delineate the regulatory mechanisms underlying IL-1β-induced cellular response. Results IL-1β elicited a profound transcriptional alteration, with 1, 468 differentially expressed genes (811 upregulated and 657 downregulated). Upregulated genes were enriched for immune and inflammatory response pathways, whereas downregulated genes encompassed tendon-specific matrix programs and broader mesenchymal developmental pathways. Concordantly, ATAC-seq revealed 15, 257 differentially accessible regions, with a striking asymmetry toward increased accessibility under IL-1β treatment. Integrative analysis revealed a potential association between chromatin remodeling and transcriptional alterations. Motif enrichment within IL-1β-high accessible regions (IL-1β-HARs) identified C/EBP and NF-κB family members as candidate regulators of inflammatory gene activation, while control-HARs (Ctrl-HARs) harbored motifs for homeostatic transcription factors. Conclusions These findings demonstrate that IL-1β affects tenocyte homeostasis by simultaneously activates inflammatory gene programs and suppresses tendon-associated expression through coordinated transcriptional and epigenetic remodeling. The transcription factor regulatory elements identified here provide a mechanistic hint for future investigation, and we hypothesize that targeting these elements may offer a potential therapeutic strategy for inflammatory tendon disorders, while this possibility remains to be tested experimentally.

papers.title: Case Report: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome triggered by Rhinovirus/Enterovirus infection with cutaneous thrombotic microangiopathy requiring surgical management
papers.abstract: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) represents a complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) characterized by microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and end-organ damage, most frequently affecting the kidneys. Although infection is a well-recognized precipitant, extensive skin involvement is uncommon. Here, we describe a 14-year-old boy who developed aHUS following Rhinovirus/Enterovirus infection. He was found to have anemia, thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury, hematuria, and proteinuria, and peripheral smear examination demonstrated schistocytes. Complement evaluation showed reduced C3 and factor I concentrations, increased soluble C5b-9, and preserved ADAMTS13 activity. Investigations for Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli, systemic autoimmune disease, and alternative infectious etiologies were negative. Even with eculizumab, corticosteroids, therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE), and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), his condition progressed to petechiae, ecchymoses, hemorrhagic bullae, and necrotic lesions of the axilla, neck, and back. Since the necrotic areas failed to heal and were accompanied by continued platelet consumption and a heightened risk of infection, surgical debridement and wound closure were undertaken after the platelet count reached 81 × 10^9/L. Histopathologic analysis of the excised tissue confirmed cutaneous thrombotic microangiopathy with microvascular thrombosis. Following the procedure, platelet count, hemoglobin, and complement C3 returned to normal, and the wound healed without complication. At subsequent follow-up, the scars were supple and level, with no sensory deficit or functional limitation. This report expands the range of infectious triggers associated with aHUS and demonstrates that persistent necrotic cutaneous thrombotic microangiopathy may necessitate prompt surgical management in addition to complement inhibition and supportive treatment.

This report expands the range of infectious triggers associated with aHUS and demonstrates that persistent necrotic cutaneous thrombotic microangiopathy may necessitate prompt surgical management in addition to complement inhibition and supportive treatment.
