papers.title: Effect of Plasticizer Concentration on the Characteristics of Polyvinyl Alcohol-Based Films
papers.abstract: This research focuses on the fabrication and characterization of polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) films incorporating varying concentrations (0, 5, 10, 15 wt.%) of triacetin (TRI) as a bioplasticizer. The effects of TRI on the physical, surface and structural, dynamic mechanical and barrier properties of polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) films were systematically investigated. The physical characteristics such as thickness and density of the films were influenced by TRI content. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analysis revealed notable changes in surface morphology with increasing TRI concentration, while water contact angle measurements indicated altered wettability. Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy confirmed molecular interactions between TRI and PVA matrix. X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis showed a reduction in crystallinity upon the addition of TRI. Moreover, dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) revealed variations in storage modulus, loss modulus, and glass transition temperature (Tg), indicating improved flexibility and processability of the plasticized films. Gas barrier properties exhibited a concentration-dependent behavior; the addition of 5 wt.% TRI enhanced the barrier performance against oxygen and carbon dioxide, whereas higher plasticizer contents (notably 15 wt.%) resulted in increased gas permeability. Therefore, 5 wt.% TRI was determined as the optimum content for packaging applications.

papers.title: Electro-Thermal Analysis and Optimization of Wireless Power Transfer Coupler for Rotary Steerable Systems
papers.abstract: In rotary steerable systems, stable coupling and effective thermal management of the wireless power transfer (WPT) magnetic coupler during rotation are critical to reliable system operation. An unstable coupling coefficient can degrade power transfer efficiency, while uncontrolled losses may lead to thermal failure and compromise system stability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a dual-solenoid-Q-type rotary magnetic coupler suitable for rotary steerable tools and systematically analyzes and optimizes its heat generation and heat dissipation characteristics. The proposed magnetic coupler maintains a stable coupling coefficient throughout the rotation process without requiring complex winding schemes or coil configurations. To reduce heat source losses, the effects of coil turns, receiver opening angle, and coil height on heat generation are investigated in detail. Furthermore, a coupled heat dissipation model is established to comprehensively evaluate the combined effects of six key structural parameters, including coil height spacing, transmitter and receiver turns, transmitter and receiver turn spacing, and receiver opening angle, on the average temperature and total loss of the magnetic coupler. Based on the optimized parameters, a 500 W WPT simulation model with an LCC-S compensation topology is established. The results show that the proposed optimization method effectively reduces system losses, with the total system loss remaining below 40 W. The maximum temperature rise is significantly reduced to 17 °C, corresponding to a reduction of more than 43%. These results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively suppresses the risk of overheating under extreme downhole operating conditions and improves the operational reliability of the WPT system.

papers.title: Thermophysical behavior and transient thermal performance of a Fe3O4/paraffin nano-enhanced phase change material for solar desalination applications
papers.journal: Solar Energy Materials and Solar Cells
papers.abstract: The low thermal efficiency and limited nocturnal operation of conventional solar stills remain major challenges for sustainable solar desalination. This study experimentally investigates a paraffin-based phase change material enhanced with 1 wt.% Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles as a thermal energy storage medium for improving the transient thermal behavior and overall performance of a single-slope solar still. The Fe 3 O 4 /paraffin nanocomposite was prepared using a surfactant-assisted dispersion method and characterized by SEM, DSC, FTIR, and thermal conductivity measurements. Outdoor experiments were conducted in Benguerir, Morocco, during four clear sky days in August 2024, representing typical summer operating conditions, using three configurations: a conventional solar still (CSS), a PCM-assisted solar still (PCMSS), and a nano-PCM solar still (NPCMSS). The thermal analysis further included the evaluation of internal convective, evaporative, and radiative heat-transfer coefficients, together with external thermal losses. Fe 3 O 4 incorporation increased paraffin thermal conductivity by approximately 47%, facilitating heat transfer within the storage medium and maintaining favorable basin-water temperatures and water to glass temperature differences during the cooling period. Although the NPCM exhibited an approximately 22% reduction in latent heat storage capacity, the NPCMSS achieved a 65.2% increase in freshwater productivity relative to the CSS, with a corresponding productivity uncertainty of 2.4%. The NPCMSS also attained daily energy and exergy efficiencies of 29.33% and 2.04%, with corresponding uncertainties of 2.3% and 2.6%, respectively. Economic and environmental assessments further indicated reduced freshwater production cost and improved CO 2 mitigation performance. Overall, Fe 3 O 4 /paraffin NPCM shows strong potential for improving passive solar desalination under the investigated conditions.

Economic and environmental assessments further indicated reduced freshwater production cost and improved CO 2 mitigation performance. papers.title: Thermo-Responsive PNIPAM-Based Nanocomposite Hydrogels for Solubility Enhancement and Controlled Delivery of Poorly Water Soluble Anticancer Drugs
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: The poor solubility of numerous anticancer medications in water leads to constrained bioavailability and diminished therapeutic effectiveness.The current research sought to create thermo-responsive poly(Nisopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM)-based nanocomposite hydrogels to improve solubility and facilitate the controlled release of a weakly water-soluble anticancer agent.PNIPAM nanocomposite hydrogels were produced using free-radical polymerisation, employing N,N′-methylenebisacrylamide as a crosslinking agent and augmented with silica nanoparticles.The refined formulation demonstrated a swelling ratio of 845 ± 28% beneath the lower critical solution temperature (LCST) and 312 ± 17% above the LCST, with an LCST of 33.4 ± 0.6°C.The drug loading efficiency and encapsulation efficiency were recorded at 91.6 ± 2.1% and 88.3 ± 1.8%, respectively, with the drug's apparent aqueous solubility exhibiting a 6.9-fold enhancement relative to the unaltered drug.SEM research demonstrated a significantly porous interconnected structure, whereas FTIR and DSC investigations validated effective drug encapsulation devoid of chemical incompatibility.In vitro drug release exhibited prolonged release, achieving a cumulative drug release of 92.4 ± 2.5% at 48 hours under physiological circumstances, in contrast to 34.8 ± 1.9% for the pure drug suspension.The release kinetics conformed to the Korsmeyer-Peppas model (R² = 0.992) with a diffusion exponent (n = 0.61), signifying anomalous transport.The nanocomposite hydrogel demonstrated markedly increased cytotoxicity towards MCF-7 breast cancer cells, diminishing cell viability to 24.8 ± 3.2% in contrast to 51.6 ± 2.8% for the free drug at the same concentration (p < 0.001).These results indicate that thermo-responsive PNIPAM-based nanocomposite hydrogels significantly enhance drug solubility and facilitate regulated, temperature-sensitive drug release, positioning them as viable carriers for targeted anticancer therapy.

papers.title: SOLUBILITY ENHANCEMENT OF CURCUMIN BY SOLID DISPERSION: FORMULATION, CHARACTERISATION AND IN VITRO DISSOLUTION EVALUATION
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Curcumin has considerable pharmaceutical interest but its poor aqueous solubility and slow dissolution restrict formulation performance.The present study compared curcumin solid dispersions prepared with an equalproportion carrier system of polyethylene glycol 6000 (PEG 6000) and polyvinylpyrrolidone K30 (PVP K30).Physical mixtures (PM1-PM3) and solid dispersions were prepared at drug:total carrier ratios of 1:1, 1:2 and 1:3 by kneading (F1-F3), solvent evaporation (F4-F6) and melting (F7-F9).The products were evaluated for practical yield, drug content, apparent saturation solubility in phosphate buffer pH 6.8 and in vitro dissolution using USP apparatus II.The selected batch was characterised by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and a 30day short-term stability study.Apparent saturation solubility increased from 7.70 ± 0.15 µg/mL for pure curcumin to 84.40 ± 0.58 µg/mL for F6, corresponding to a 996.10% increase.F6 showed a practical yield of 94.42 ± 0.69%, drug content of 96.66 ± 0.62% and 96.25% dissolution at 120 minutes compared with 33.68% for pure curcumin.FTIR retained the principal drug and carrier bands without a new prominent covalent functional group.The disappearance of the distinct curcumin melting endotherm in DSC, marked attenuation of curcumin reflections in PXRD and altered surface morphology in SEM indicated substantial reduction of the crystalline contribution, although residual PXRD peaks supported partial rather than complete amorphisation.F6 retained drug content and dissolution performance with only minor numerical changes over 30 days.The solvent evaporation method at a 1:3 drug:total carrier ratio produced the most favourable combined performance and represents a practical approach for enhancing the apparent solubility and dissolution of curcumin.

papers.title: Securescape: Deep Vision-Based Framework For Behavioral Crime Detection And Face Intelligence
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence and deep learning technologies has profoundly impacted the evolution of contemporary surveillance and security systems.Intelligent monitoring systems are now more in demand to address the increasing security concerns in public spaces, financial institutions, and urban environments.This paper aims to present an intelligent suspicious activity detection and crime face recognition system using AI technology for enhanced automatic surveillance systems.The system incorporates intelligent pose estimation, anomaly detection, and object detection mechanisms for detecting abnormal human activities such as aggressive movements, loitering, and the presence of dangerous objects in the monitored area.For accurate object detection, the system incorporates a YOLO based intelligent object detection model for detecting suspicious objects such as weapons and dangerous items in real-time scenarios.In addition to activity analysis, the system incorporates a Grassmannian-based intelligent facial recognition system using CNN architectures for accurate criminal face recognition based on facial feature analysis with a criminal database.The framework continually processes video streams from surveillance systems, detects unusual activities, and sends out alerts when unusual behavior or identified offenders are detected.The automated notification systems help in efficient response from security authorities.The inclusion of intelligent surveillance systems and face recognition helps in efficient monitoring by reducing manual surveillance activities and increasing accuracy in potential threats

papers.title: Biodegradable Foam Synthesized from Lignin-Rich Brewer’s Spent Grain Waste with Potential Use as a Sustainable Alternative for Packaging Applications
papers.abstract: Abstract Biodegradable foams derived from agroindustrial residues provide a sustainable alternative to existing petroleum-based packaging, while supporting circular bioeconomy objectives. In this study, biofoams were synthesized using raw brewer’s spent grain (BSG1) and lignin-enriched residues (BSG2 and BSG3) obtained postfermentation for ethanol production. Chemical composition analysis of all BSG biomasses revealed that BSG1 contained 18.72% total lignin, whereas BSG2 and BSG3 exhibited substantially higher lignin contents of 78.28 and 83.69%, respectively, representing nearly a 4-fold increase. SEM (scanning electron microscopy) analysis showed an increase in biofoam porosity from BSG1 (0.4%) to BSG2 (7.8%) and BSG3 (13.4%), which correlated with enhanced compressive strength (0.49–0.50 MPa) and improved thickness recovery under uniaxial cyclic compression. It also exhibited reduced water absorption, from 20% in BSG1 to 7 and 11% in BSG2 and BSG3, respectively. The enhanced lignin content may have contributed to the strength and moisture resistance of the biofoams, whereas the relatively low water absorption of the processed BSG likely supported its degradation in the environment. The foams exhibited high solubility in river and seawater (48–70%) and near-complete soil degradation within 7–10 weeks, highlighting their rapid environmental decomposition. Thermal analysis (TG/DTG) confirmed the multistage degradation typical of lignocellulosic materials, with higher residual char in BSG2 and BSG3 reflecting their lignin-rich composition. Collectively, these results demonstrated that lignin-rich BSG residues can be transformed into mechanically robust, moderately porous, thermally stable, and rapidly biodegradable biofoams, combining enhanced strength, controlled hydrophilicity, and environmental compatibility. This work establishes a zero-waste cascade valorization strategy in which lignin-rich fermentation residues are upcycled into biodegradable biofoams, providing a sustainable pathway for replacing petroleum-based packaging materials.

papers.title: Hydrogel-Encapsulated Sodium Acetate Trihydrate/Paraffin Wax Hybrid Phase Change Materials with Suppressed Supercooling and Enhanced Thermal Reliability
papers.abstract: Abstract Organic–inorganic hybrid phase change materials (PCMs) offer a promising approach to combine the high latent-heat storage capacity of hydrated salts with the phase stability of organic PCMs; however, interfacial incompatibility, phase separation, leakage, dehydration, and severe supercooling continue to limit their practical application. Herein, a shape-stable sodium acetate trihydrate/paraffin wax (SAT:PW) hybrid PCM was developed via an A200 silica-stabilized Pickering emulsion and subsequently encapsulated within an acrylamide-based hydrogel network. The Pickering emulsion enabled stable integration of the hydrophilic SAT phase and hydrophobic PW phase, while the hydrogel framework physically confined the hybrid PCM, suppressing leakage, reducing cumulative thermal mass loss, and improving thermal reliability during repeated phase transitions. Among the investigated formulations, SAT:PW90 provided the most favorable overall balance of latent-heat storage, crystallization performance, supercooling suppression, and leakage resistance in hydrogel encapsulation, exhibiting a melting peak temperature of 64.70 °C, a crystallization peak temperature of 47.74 °C, a melting enthalpy of 228.8 ± 1.0 kJ kg–1, a thermal conductivity of 0.556 ± 0.03 W m–1 K–1, and a low supercooling degree of 2.1 ± 0.85 °C. Under the investigated TGA conditions, hydrogel confinement reduced the cumulative mass loss to ∼1.25% at 75 °C and ∼2.2% at 155 °C, compared with ∼7.2 and ∼22%, respectively, for SAT:PW90, while retaining a melting enthalpy of 146.7 ± 1.5 kJ kg–1, a melting peak temperature of 63.96 °C, and a low supercooling degree of 4.0 °C. Following 100 heating–cooling cycles, the composite retained 95.8% of its initial melting enthalpy, with a supercooling degree of only 4.7 °C, demonstrating promising thermal reliability. These findings establish Pickering-emulsion stabilization combined with hydrogel confinement as an effective strategy for developing shape-stable hybrid PCMs for low-temperature solar thermal energy storage and building thermal-management applications.

papers.title: Real-world clinical effectiveness and exploratory longitudinal immunological changes of Efgartigimod in myasthenia gravis: a retrospective study and a single-cell analysis in one patient
papers.abstract: Introduction Efgartigimod, an antagonist of the neonatal Fc receptor, has demonstrated efficacy in generalized myasthenia gravis, but evidence from routine clinical practice remains limited, and its immunological effects beyond immunoglobulin G reduction are incompletely understood. Methods We retrospectively evaluated the 12-week effectiveness and safety of Efgartigimod in 21 patients with acetylcholine receptor antibody-positive generalized myasthenia gravis. Outcomes included changes in Myasthenia Gravis Activities of Daily Living scores, response rates defined by reductions of ≥2 and ≥5 points, achievement of minimal symptom expression, changes in prednisone dosage, and adverse events. To explore potential longer-term immune changes, paired peripheral blood mononuclear cell samples obtained from one patient at baseline and after 6 months of repeated treatment were analyzed using single-cell RNA sequencing and T- and B-cell receptor repertoire sequencing. Results The median MG-ADL score decreased from 7.0 (IQR, 6.0–8.0) at baseline to 1.0 (IQR, 1.0–1.5) at week 12. After the first and second treatment cycles, 85.7 and 94.7% of patients achieved CMI, respectively, while 57.1 and 84.2% achieved ≥5-point reductions. At week 12, 73.7% of patients achieved MSE. Treatment was generally well tolerated, with two mild adverse events and no serious adverse events. Exploratory longitudinal profiling in one patient identified reduced myeloid inflammatory activity and antigen-presentation signatures, attenuated predicted inflammatory intercellular communication, and a more dispersed pattern of T- and B-cell clonal expansion after prolonged treatment. Conclusion The clinical cohort findings support the effectiveness and favorable safety profile of Efgartigimod in routine practice. The exploratory single-cell and immune repertoire analyses from one patient provide preliminary insights into potential immunological changes beyond IgG reduction and require validation in larger cohorts.

papers.title: Combined application of salicylic acid and silicon enhances photosynthetic capacity and yield in different dry-cultivated rice varieties: associations with osmotic adjustment substances and antioxidant enzyme activity
papers.abstract: Single applications of silicon (Si) and salicylic acid (SA) can alleviate plant stress. However, the effects of their combined application on dry-cultivated rice and the differences between varieties remain unclear. A preliminary laboratory experiment established the optimal silicon fertilizer application rate at 45 kg ha -1 . Subsequently, a preliminary experiment conducted in 2022 determined the optimal SA concentration at 1.0 mM. Based on these findings, four treatments were set up in 2023: control (CK), single application of Si (T1), single application of SA (T2), and Si + SA (T3). The results indicated that the combined application of Si and SA significantly enhanced both the grain yield and photosynthetic capacity of dry-cultivated rice. Under the T3 treatment, grain yield increased by 80.7% and 77.3% in cultivars SJ18 and HK88, respectively, compared with the CK. This yield improvement was primarily attributable to increases in two key yield components: the number of effective panicles (up by 17.6% and 29.3%, respectively) and the number of grains per panicle (up by 26.9% and 22.6%, respectively). The responses of the agronomic traits to the treatment were consistent with the yield trends. Physiologically, the combined application of Si + SA enhanced the photosynthetic capacity of the photosystem II (PSIl) system by improving chlorophyll fluorescence parameters, increasing antioxidant enzyme activities, and enhancing soluble sugar, soluble protein content, endogenous SA, and Si contents. The responses of different varieties to the combined application of Si + SA differed significantly. 10 days after spraying, the soluble sugar and protein content of HK88 increased by 36.1% and 22.7%, respectively, compared with CK, which were numerically greater than the corresponding increases observed in SJ18 (10.7% and 17.4%, respectively). This finding suggests that drought-resistant varieties may require greater accumulation of osmotic adjustment substances to alleviate drought stress. Therefore, the combined application of SA and Si is closely associated with increased levels of osmotic adjustment substances and endogenous SA and Si, as well as enhanced antioxidant enzyme activities. These coordinated physiological responses contribute to enhanced photosynthetic capacity of the PSII system, ultimately improving drought tolerance, dry matter accumulation, and grain yield in dry-cultivated rice. These relationships are further supported by significant positive correlations observed in our structural equation modeling analysis. This approach provides a new and effective way of alleviating drought stress and increasing the yield of dry-cultivated rice.

Therefore, the combined application of SA and Si is closely associated with increased levels of osmotic adjustment substances and endogenous SA and Si, as well as enhanced antioxidant enzyme activities.

papers.title: How and Why Do We Measure Cellular Heat?–Significance and History—
papers.abstract: Temperature is a fundamental physical quantity that governs chemical reaction rates, molecular diffusion, and protein stability, and is therefore intimately linked to biological function. In cells, heat is generated through a variety of nonequilibrium processes, including metabolism and mechanical activity. Cellular thermometry is increasingly recognized not only as a method for measuring temperature but also as a framework for investigating intracellular energy conversion, heat dissipation, and the spatial localization of cellular function. This review examines the significance of thermal measurement in cell-related research and traces the historical development of the field, from bulk calorimetry of cell populations to single-cell and subcellular measurements enabled by optical and microfabricated sensors. We summarize the major methodological platforms, including fluorescent polymeric thermometers, inorganic nanoparticles, fluorescent proteins, small-molecule probes, and contact-based microsensors, highlighting their respective strengths and limitations with regard to spatial and temporal resolution, targeting capability, and quantitative reliability. We also discuss the central controversy in the field, namely the “10 5 gap issue,” which refers to the discrepancy between experimentally reported intracellular temperature changes and theoretical predictions based on classical heat conduction. Finally, we consider future perspectives. Rather than remaining focused solely on temperature measurement, cellular thermometry is evolving toward a broader framework of cellular thermal analysis that encompasses heat production, heat transport, and cellular thermophysical properties.
papers.summary: Temperature is a fundamental physical quantity that governs chemical reaction rates, molecular diffusion, and protein stability, and is therefore intimately linked to biological function. This review examines the significance of thermal measurement in cell-related research and traces the historical development of the field, from bulk calorimetry of cell populations to single-cell and subcellular measurements enabled by optical and microfabricated sensors. We summarize the major methodological platforms, including fluorescent polymeric thermometers, inorganic nanoparticles, fluorescent proteins, small-molecule probes, and contact-based microsensors, highlighting their respective strengths and limitations with regard to spatial and temporal resolution, targeting capability, and quantitative reliability.

papers.title: FORMULATION AND DEVELOPMENT OF CURCUMINLOADED NANOBUBBLES: PHYSICOCHEMICAL CHARACTERISATION AND IN VITRO RELEASE EVALUATION
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Curcumin possesses wide pharmacological potential, but its very low aqueous solubility and poor dispersion limit formulation development.The present study aimed to formulate curcumin-loaded nanobubbles using a phospholipidpolymer shell and to evaluate their physicochemical characteristics, solid-state behaviour and in vitro release at pH 7.4.Curcumin-loaded nanobubbles were prepared using Epikuron 200, chitosan, palmitic acid, Pluronic F68 and sulfur hexafluoride.Preliminary processing and formulation variables were screened, and the selected composition was prepared by gradual addition of an ethanolic lipid phase to an aqueous chitosan-Pluronic F68 phase, followed by solvent evaporation, probe sonication and sulfur hexafluoride purging.The selected formulation contained curcumin 10 mg, Epikuron 200 121 mg, chitosan 0.22% w/v, palmitic acid 20 mg and Pluronic F68 0.28% w/v in 10 mL.It showed a particle size of 361.8 ± 4.6 nm, PDI of 0.286 ± 0.009, zeta potential of +28.0 ± 0.7 mV, entrapment efficiency of 77.7 ± 0.9% and drug loading of 4.67 ± 0.03%.FTIR spectra showed retention of characteristic curcumin bands without formation of unexplained new peaks.Comparative DSC and PXRD patterns indicated reduced crystalline order of curcumin after formulation.At pH 7.4, cumulative curcumin release at 24 h increased from 60.85 ± 0.54% without ultrasound to 83.56 ± 0.34% after ultrasound exposure.The release profiles were best described by the Korsmeyer-Peppas model.The developed nanobubbles provided satisfactory physicochemical properties and ultrasound-enhanced curcumin release at pH 7.4.

papers.title: Chinese herbal medicine combined with conventional therapy for gastric precancerous lesions: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Background Chronic atrophic gastritis and gastric precancerous lesions are associated with increased gastric cancer risk. Chinese herbal medicine is widely used as an adjunct to conventional therapy, but the certainty and clinical interpretation of its effects remain unclear. Objective To evaluate the efficacy and safety of Chinese herbal medicine added to the same conventional therapy for chronic atrophic gastritis and gastric precancerous lesions. Methods Eight international and Chinese databases and three trial registries were searched from inception to 31 March 2026 and updated to 16 August 2026. Randomised controlled trials comparing Chinese herbal medicine plus the same conventional therapy with conventional therapy alone and reporting extractable pathological outcomes were included. Random-effects models used restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp inference. Additional sensitivity analyses examined clinically comparable histopathology, baseline balance based on auditable pretreatment data, and exclusion of high-risk-of-bias results. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and certainty using GRADE. Results Sixty-nine randomised trials comprising 6,983 participants in eligible comparisons were included. Exploratory Broad end-of-treatment analyses favoured combined treatment for gastric mucosal atrophy (30 studies; SMD −1.63, 95% CI −2.03 to −1.24), intestinal metaplasia (29 studies; SMD −1.48, 95% CI −1.90 to −1.06), and dysplasia or intraepithelial neoplasia (21 studies; SMD −1.25, 95% CI −1.51 to −0.99). Heterogeneity was substantial (I 2 82.4%–92.7%); prediction intervals crossed the null for atrophy and intestinal metaplasia but not for dysplasia/intraepithelial neoplasia. Sensitivity analyses restricted to clinically comparable histopathological assessments included only three to four studies and were imprecise, with confidence intervals crossing the null. Helicobacter pylori clearance/negative conversion among baseline-positive participants was higher with combined treatment (15 studies; RR 1.25, 95% CI 1.15–1.37), whereas the strict test-of-cure sensitivity was imprecise (3 studies; RR 1.19, 95% CI 0.91–1.56). There was no clear evidence of a difference in reported adverse events (14-study evidence set; RR-contributing studies = 12; RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.58–1.50), which should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent safety. Certainty was low for all five principal outcomes. Conclusion Chinese herbal medicine added to conventional therapy may be associated with lower short-term pathological scores on average, but the magnitude and clinical meaning of these effects remain uncertain because of trial limitations, marked heterogeneity, and imprecision in clinically comparable analyses. The findings do not establish durable histological regression or gastric cancer prevention, and the pooled estimates should not be interpreted as a class-wide effect applicable to all Chinese herbal medicines. Systematic Review Registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261442138 , identifier CRD420261442138.

papers.title: Bioactive Bacterial Cellulose Films Functionalized with Pecan Nutshell [Carya illinoinensis (Wangenh) K. Koch] Extract and Glycerol: Physicochemical, Thermal, and Antibacterial Properties
papers.abstract: Valorizing agro-industrial by-products as feedstocks for coatings and biomaterials offers a sustainable route to value-added materials. This study investigated the effects of pecan nutshell extract (PNSE) and glycerol on the physicochemical, bioactive, and antibacterial properties of functionalized bacterial cellulose (BC) films. PNSE showed a high phenolic and flavonoid content and substantial antioxidant capacity (DPPH, ABTS, and FRAP). BC-based films containing PNSE and glycerol were subsequently characterized by FTIR, SEM, TGA/DTG, and DSC, and their antibacterial activity was evaluated by disk diffusion against Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 25923, Escherichia coli ATCC 35218, and Salmonella typhimurium ATCC 14028. The extract contained 742.91 ± 4.04 mg GAE/g of total phenolic compounds, 82.42 ± 0.67 mg CE/g of flavonoids, and 475.13 ± 2.84 µmol TE/g in the DPPH assay. ATR-FTIR revealed spectral changes consistent with interactions among cellulose hydroxyl groups, glycerol, and phenolic constituents of PNSE. SEM revealed changes in surface morphology, and TGA/DTG recorded degradation temperatures of up to 386 °C. The BC-PNSE-GC-4 formulation exhibited the strongest antibacterial activity against S. aureus, demonstrating an inhibition zone of 18 mm. The developed films show promising potential for use in active food packaging applications.

papers.title: FORMULATION, CHARACTERIZATION AND EVALUATION OF TOPIRAMATE LOADED FAST DISSOLVING TABLETS.
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: The present study was designed to formulate, optimize and evaluate the topiramate loaded fast dissolving tablets (FDTs) for better patient compliance which will ensure rapid drug release.Superdisintegrants, Crospovidone (CPV) and Sodium Starch Glycolate (SSG), were selected for the direct compression method to get fast dissolving tablets.A full-factorial experimental design with two variables (CPV and SSG) was used to explore the influence of the CPV and SSG concentration on disintegration time and percentage drug release.Precompression and post-compression physiochemical properties like flow properties, hardness, friability, weight variation, disintegration time and in vitro drug release of the prepared formulations were determined.Drugexcipient compatibility was studied by Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) and Powder X-ray Diffraction (PXRD) studies.All the physicochemical properties of the formulations were acceptable and within the Pharmacopeial requirements.The optimized formulation with 25 mg of Crospovidone and 12 mg of Sodium Starch Glycolate exhibited disintegration time of 26 s and cumulative drug release 96.12% in 15 min.Statistical analysis revealed a significant effect for both the superdisintegrants on the tablet properties namely disintegration time and cumulative drug release and greater effect was observed for Crospovidone.Good correlation between the predicted and experimental responses were used to validate the optimization model.The study found that the optimized Topiramate fast dissolving tablets showed excellent disintegration characteristics, as well as better dissolution characteristics, and that there is a potential for improving the adherence of patients to these tablets for the treatment of epilepsy.
